meta.evidence_policy: A=指南/教科书/系统综述共识；B=单项研究/机制研究/综述；C=模型/假说/临床经验/证据有限。每条笔记标注证据等级与来源；每日更新只保存原文标题/摘要/链接，不自动生成结论。
meta.disclaimer: 本知识库用于运动科学学习与训练参考，不构成医疗诊断或治疗建议。疼痛、麻木、无力、红旗症状请先咨询医生/物理治疗师。
meta.synthesis_policy: 自动任务负责抓取、去重、归档与索引；跨学科综述由智能体基于来源整理，并标注证据等级。不会用无来源的生成内容替代原始文献。

disciplines.name: 运动解剖学
disciplines.intro: 从骨骼、关节、肌肉与神经出发，理解动作如何产生、力如何传递、哪些结构在承担负荷。

notes.title: 肩胛骨与肩胛胸壁
notes.summary: 肩胛骨是肩带的活动平台：它通过肩胛胸壁在胸廓上滑动，并由前锯肌、斜方肌、菱形肌、肩胛提肌等协同完成上回旋、后缩、前伸和稳定。盂肱关节的稳定还依赖肩袖。
points: 上回旋：前锯肌 + 下斜方肌；下回旋：菱形肌 + 肩胛提肌 + 上斜方肌。
胸椎伸展/旋转不足会改变肩胛上回旋，影响过顶与推拉动作。
肩胛运动障碍是观察，不是诊断；疼痛是多因素的。
评估可看：肩胛观察、墙面滑手、肩胛俯卧撑、胸椎旋转，并结合负荷史。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (shoulder/neck).

notes.title: 髋关节与髋铰链
notes.summary: 髋关节是球窝关节，承担负重与力传递；髋伸由臀大肌/腘绳肌，髋外展与骨盆稳定由臀中肌，髋屈由髂腰肌/股直肌等。髋铰链是髋主导、脊柱中立的动作模式。
points: 髋活动度（屈/伸/内外旋）影响深蹲、硬拉、步态与腰椎负荷。
臀中肌负责单腿站立/步态骨盆稳定；无力常与膝/腰代偿相关。
“髋屈肌紧”不一定是短缩，可能是保护性紧张；拉伸不是唯一解。
训练：髋铰链、分腿蹲、单腿罗马尼亚硬拉、侧向走；渐进负荷。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (hip).

notes.title: 膝关节：胫股与髌股
notes.summary: 膝关节由胫股和髌股关节组成；股四头肌通过髌骨/髌腱伸膝，臀肌与足踝影响下肢力线。髌股疼痛与负荷、股四头/臀肌力量、疼痛敏感相关，不是单纯“磨损”。
points: 髌股关节对负荷敏感；逐步增加屈膝角度和训练量。
股四头/臀肌力量是髌股疼痛的一线；髋/踝活动度也要看。
“膝盖不能过脚尖”是误区；控制负荷和动作质量更重要。
红旗：交锁、明显肿胀、不能负重、发热、外伤后畸形。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guideline: Patellofemoral Pain (2019).
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.

notes.title: 脊柱稳定与核心
notes.summary: 脊柱稳定由被动结构（椎体/韧带）、主动结构（多裂肌、腹壁、膈肌、盆底）和神经控制共同完成；胸腰筋膜参与力传递。核心训练的目标是抗伸展、抗旋转、抗侧屈和呼吸-腹压协调。
points: 核心不是“练腹肌”，而是躯干稳定与力传递。
呼吸/膈肌/盆底协调影响腹内压与腰椎稳定。
大多数腰痛不需要影像；保持活动 + 力量 + 疼痛教育是一线。
红旗：鞍区麻木、大小便障碍、发热、夜间痛、进行性无力。
sources: Hartvigsen J, et al. Lancet Low Back Pain Series, 2018.
NICE NG59. Low back pain and sciatica.
Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.

notes.title: 肩复合体：盂肱、肩胛胸壁与肩袖
notes.summary: 肩不是单一关节：盂肱关节负责大范围活动，肩胛胸壁提供活动平台，肩锁/胸锁关节参与微动；肩袖在活动中提供压缩与稳定。过顶动作需要胸椎、肩胛、肩袖协同。
points: 肩袖四肌：冈上、冈下、小圆、肩胛下；稳定肱骨头。
肩胛上回旋由前锯肌+下斜方主导；肩肱节律约 2:1（个体差异）。
胸椎伸展/旋转不足会迫使肩胛/盂肱代偿。
评估：疼痛弧、外旋/内旋力量、肩胛观察、胸椎活动。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (shoulder).

notes.title: 肘与腕：屈伸、旋前旋后与肌腱
notes.summary: 肘关节完成屈伸，前臂完成旋前旋后；肱二头肌/肱肌/肱三头肌与腕屈伸肌群共同参与推拉与握持。外上髁是腕伸肌起点，内上髁是腕屈肌起点，肌腱病与负荷相关。
points: 外上髁痛（网球肘）多与腕伸肌/握力负荷相关；内上髁相反。
腕中立位握力更强；腕伸肌离心训练是常用康复。
肘/腕活动度影响卧推、划船、推举。
评估：抗阻伸腕/屈腕、握力、肘关节活动度。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (elbow).

notes.title: 踝与足：背屈、足弓与推进
notes.summary: 踝关节负责背屈/跖屈，距下关节负责内外翻；足弓由骨、韧带、足底筋膜和足内在肌共同维持。小腿三头肌推进，胫后肌维持内侧纵弓，腓骨肌提供外侧稳定。
points: 踝背屈约 10–20°（屈膝）；不足会影响深蹲/弓步/跑。
提踵训练小腿；短足训练足内在肌；单腿平衡训练本体感觉。
无症状扁平足不需要“矫正”；有症状先评估负荷/鞋具。
评估：靠墙踝背屈、提踵、单腿平衡、足弓观察。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (ankle).

notes.title: 骨盆与骶髂：力传递与稳定
notes.summary: 骨盆环由髋骨、骶骨与骶髂关节组成；骶髂关节微动，稳定依赖韧带、臀肌、腹壁、盆底与胸腰筋膜。骨盆是下肢与躯干之间力传递的枢纽。
points: 臀大肌/臀中肌、腹壁、盆底共同参与骨盆稳定。
骨盆前倾/后倾是描述，不是诊断；疼痛多因素。
产后/盆底问题先做专业评估。
评估：单腿站立、臀肌力量、髋活动度、SIJ 集群（需专业）。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Vleeming A, et al. Movement, Stability & Lumbopelvic Pain.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.

notes.title: 肌肉架构：羽状角、纤维长度与力臂
notes.summary: 肌肉的生理横截面积影响最大力，纤维长度/羽状角影响速度与力量-长度关系，力臂影响关节力矩。不同动作会改变肌肉受力角度与长度，训练选择要匹配目标。
points: 羽状肌（如股四头）力量大、速度相对低；长纤维肌速度更快。
力臂随关节角度变化；深蹲/硬拉/腿举的力矩不同。
个体解剖差异大，不要用单一“标准动作”套所有人。
评估：动作舒适度、力量曲线、关节活动度。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Lieber RL. Skeletal Muscle Structure, Function & Plasticity.

notes.title: 肌腱与韧带：传递、储能与稳定
notes.summary: 肌腱把肌肉力传到骨骼，可储存/释放弹性能力；韧带限制关节过度活动并提供本体感觉。两者都是结缔组织，适应比肌肉慢，负荷管理是关键。
points: 肌腱病通常是负荷相关，不是单纯“发炎”；渐进负荷是主线。
韧带损伤分度；急性期保护，随后恢复活动度/力量/本体感觉。
肌腱/韧带适应需要数周–数月；不要突然加量。
红旗：明显肿胀、不能负重、关节不稳、交锁。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines.
Brukner P, Khan K. Clinical Sports Medicine, 5th ed.

notes.title: 胸椎与胸廓：呼吸与肩胛的平台
notes.summary: 胸椎、肋骨与胸骨构成胸廓；胸椎伸展/旋转影响肩胛上回旋与过顶动作，肋骨运动参与呼吸。久坐、胸椎僵硬会限制肩/颈。
points: 胸椎伸展/旋转不足常与肩胛/肩代偿相关。
呼吸时肋骨应向前后左右扩张；过度胸式呼吸可能影响颈肩。
训练：胸椎旋转、伸展、呼吸练习；避免暴力扳动。
评估：坐姿胸椎旋转、仰卧呼吸、肩胛观察。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Gray's Anatomy, 41st ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (neck/shoulder).

notes.title: 步态与跑步：支撑、摆动与负荷
notes.summary: 步态周期分为支撑相与摆动相；髋、膝、踝协同吸收与推进。跑步时地面反作用力、步频、步幅、鞋具和跑量共同决定负荷。
points: 臀肌/小腿/足内在肌参与吸收与推进；力量是基础。
跑量增加遵循渐进原则；突然加量是常见诱因。
步频/步幅调整可改变关节负荷，但不是人人需要改。
评估：单腿蹲、提踵、髋外展、跑姿观察。
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
Brukner P, Khan K. Clinical Sports Medicine, 5th ed.

disciplines.name: 运动生理学
disciplines.intro: 理解肌肉、神经、能量系统与恢复如何对训练刺激作出适应，以及为什么“练多少、练多频、怎么恢复”决定结果。

notes.title: 肌肥大：机械张力与蛋白平衡
notes.summary: 肌肥大主要由机械张力驱动，代谢应激和肌肉损伤是辅助因素；训练后肌肉蛋白合成升高，长期净蛋白平衡决定增长。个体差异大，增长慢。
points: 渐进超负荷；每个肌群每周约 10–20 组有效容量（因人而异）。
蛋白质 1.6–2.2 g/kg/d；热量充足或轻度盈余。
睡眠/恢复不足会抵消训练刺激；避免过量有氧影响恢复。
新手/中级每月肌肉增长有限，体重上涨通常包含脂肪。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Schoenfeld BJ, et al. Strength and hypertrophy adaptations. J Appl Physiol / Sports Med.
ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise (2017).

notes.title: 力量增长的神经适应
notes.summary: 力量增长的早期（数周）主要来自神经适应：运动单位募集增加、放电频率提高、拮抗肌抑制减少、协同改善；肌肥大需要更长时间。
points: 技术学习/动作模式决定早期力量表现。
力量测试进步不等于肌肉增长；不要只看体重。
大重量低次数与中等次数都可增力，专项性不同。
主项组间休息 2–3 分钟，保证质量。
sources: Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Journal of Applied Physiology / MSSE reviews.

notes.title: 能量系统与训练强度
notes.summary: ATP-PC 供能约 0–10 秒，糖酵解约 10 秒–2 分钟，氧化系统供能长时低强度；训练强度/间歇决定主要系统。
points: 力量/爆发：ATP-PC；组间 2–3 分钟。
增肌训练：糖酵解/混合；30–90 秒休息常见。
有氧：氧化系统；zone 2 可说话但不能唱歌。
“燃脂心率”不是魔法；总能量平衡更重要。
sources: Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.

notes.title: 恢复、疲劳与超量恢复
notes.summary: 训练是刺激，恢复才是适应；睡眠、蛋白质、总热量、压力管理、deload 决定恢复。疲劳积累会降低表现和动作质量。
points: 睡眠 7–9 小时；规律作息。
训练后 24–48 小时酸痛常见；持续加重或关节痛要调整。
每 6–8 周 deload，或按表现/疲劳减量。
HRV/静息心率/主观精力可辅助，但不要过度依赖。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Sports Medicine / J Appl Physiol recovery reviews.

notes.title: 运动单位、肌纤维类型与募集
notes.summary: 运动单位由 α 运动神经元与其支配的肌纤维组成；肌纤维大致分 I（慢肌）与 II（快肌）。按 Henneman 大小原则，低强度先募集小运动单位，高强度/快速动作逐步募集大运动单位。
points: 力量训练同时依赖募集数量与放电频率。
低负荷高次数可增肌，但接近力竭才充分募集高阈值单位。
肌纤维类型可塑性有限；训练专项性影响表现。
评估：力量-速度、疲劳曲线、动作质量。
sources: Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.
Enoka RM. Neuromechanics of Human Movement.

notes.title: VO₂max 与有氧能力
notes.summary: VO₂max = 心输出量 × 动静脉氧差，受中枢（心搏量、血容量）和外周（毛细血管、线粒体、氧化酶）因素限制。有氧训练提高心肺与代谢能力。
points: zone 2 打基础；高强度间歇提高 VO₂max，但恢复成本高。
有氧能力与健康、恢复、训练容量相关。
个体差异大；不要只看手表估算。
评估：场地测试/实验室；结合静息心率、配速/功率。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

notes.title: 乳酸阈与训练区
notes.summary: 乳酸是糖酵解产物也是燃料/信号，不是“疲劳毒素”。乳酸阈（LT1/LT2）描述血乳酸开始上升/快速上升的强度，用于划分训练区。
points: LT1 附近可长时间维持；LT2 附近接近“临界速度”。
zone 2 训练提高脂肪氧化/有氧基础；阈值训练提高耐受力。
乳酸值受采血/设备影响，不能只看单次数值。
评估：递增负荷测试、配速/功率曲线、主观用力。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Journal of Applied Physiology reviews.

notes.title: 肌肉损伤与 DOMS
notes.summary: 不习惯的离心/高强度运动可造成微损伤与延迟性肌肉酸痛（DOMS），常在 24–72 小时达峰；重复同样刺激会减弱反应（重复效应）。DOMS 不是乳酸堆积。
points: 渐进增加负荷/次数，尤其离心动作。
轻活动、睡眠、蛋白质、热量支持恢复。
DOMS 期间可训练其他部位或降低强度；锐痛/关节痛要区分。
不是“越酸越有效”。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Sports Medicine reviews on DOMS.

notes.title: 同期训练：力量与有氧的干扰
notes.summary: 力量与有氧同周期训练可能产生干扰效应（AMPK/mTOR 等），但取决于剂量、顺序、恢复与训练水平；合理安排可以共存。
points: 同一天训练时，力量放前面；有氧用低强度/短时。
避免高强度有氧紧接大重量下肢训练。
蛋白质/热量充足、睡眠足够可减轻干扰。
目标优先：增肌期少做大量 HIIT；耐力期保留力量。
sources: MSSE / Journal of Applied Physiology concurrent training reviews.
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.

notes.title: 热环境、出汗与水合
notes.summary: 运动时产热增加，靠出汗蒸发散热；脱水会降低血容量、心搏量与表现，严重时中暑。热适应（1–2 周）提高出汗效率与血浆容量。
points: 失水约 2% 体重即可影响表现；训练前后称重可估算出汗率。
长时间/大量出汗补电解质（钠）；不要只喝大量白水。
热适应循序渐进；高温下降低强度/缩短时长。
红旗：意识模糊、停止出汗、高热——立即降温就医。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

notes.title: 停训与重返训练
notes.summary: 停训后神经/肌肉/有氧能力会下降，但下降速度不同：有氧与耐力下降较快，力量/肌肉保留较久；重返训练需要渐进，不能直接回到原量。
points: 1–2 周主要影响神经/技术；4 周以上肌肉/有氧更明显。
停训期间可做少量维持训练（力量/步行）。
重返：先降 30–50% 量，2–3 周加回。
不要用“补课”方式一次练太多。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Sports Medicine detraining reviews.

notes.title: 热身与后激活增强（PAP）
notes.summary: 热身提高体温、神经驱动与组织顺应性；高强度预激活可产生后激活增强（PAP），但需要合适强度与恢复，否则变成疲劳。
points: 一般热身 5–10 分钟 + 动态活动 + 专项 ramp-up。
PAP：大重量/爆发预激活后休息数分钟，再做专项表现。
普通健身者不必追求复杂 PAP；做好 ramp-up 即可。
热身不足/过度都会影响表现。
sources: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research reviews.
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.

disciplines.name: 筋膜学
disciplines.intro: 筋膜是结缔组织网络，参与力传递、滑动、感觉与机械转导。这里把“筋膜链”当作模型使用，不把它当诊断标准。

notes.title: 筋膜的结构与功能
notes.summary: 筋膜是遍布全身的结缔组织网络（胶原、弹性蛋白、基质、成纤维细胞等），包裹肌肉、器官、神经和血管；它参与力传递、滑动、感觉和机械转导。它不是一层“膜”，也不是万能解释。
points: 筋膜有连续性、滑动性和黏弹性；长期负荷可改变其性质。
筋膜含伤害感受器，但“筋膜粘连”不是所有疼痛的原因。
手法/拉伸可短期改善 ROM/疼痛，长期结构改变证据有限。
证据等级 B/C；避免“筋膜刀/整骨万能”说法。
sources: Myers TW. Anatomy Trains, 4th ed.
Findley TW, Schleip R. Fascia Research.
Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies.

notes.title: 肌筋膜链（解剖列车）
notes.summary: 解剖列车用肌筋膜链描述身体连续性：浅背线、浅前线、侧线、螺旋线、深前线、臂线等。它是描述性模型，不是已被证实的独立解剖结构。
points: 浅背线：足底→小腿→腘绳→竖脊肌→颅顶；与后链相关。
深前线：舌→颈深→胸→腰大肌→盆底→内收肌→胫骨后肌。
臂线：胸/背→肩→臂；与推拉/过顶相关。
用链条思考训练，但不要用它做诊断。
sources: Myers TW. Anatomy Trains, 4th ed.
Journal of Anatomy / Connective Tissue Research (fascia continuity).

notes.title: 筋膜的力传递与弹性
notes.summary: 肌腱/筋膜/腱膜把肌肉产生的力传到骨骼和相邻结构；弹性组织可储存/释放能量（如跳跃、跑步）。刚度/顺应性受负荷和训练影响，但适应较慢。
points: 力量训练提高肌腱刚度/耐受；渐进负荷。
弹性训练（跳跃/落地）提高拉长-缩短周期效率；需要基础力量。
拉伸增加 ROM，但不一定改变肌腱结构。
疼痛/损伤时管理负荷，而不是只拉筋。
sources: Myers TW. Anatomy Trains, 4th ed.
Journal of Applied Physiology / MSSE tendon adaptation reviews.

notes.title: 筋膜训练与手法证据
notes.summary: 泡沫轴、手法、拉伸可短期改善活动度和疼痛感知，但“打破粘连/排毒”缺乏证据；长期改变需要力量+负荷+时间。
points: 泡沫轴 30–60 秒/部位，疼痛 3/10 以内。
拉伸 30–60 秒；训练前动态、训练后静态。
力量训练是改变组织耐受的主线。
手法是辅助，不是替代。
sources: Myers TW. Anatomy Trains, 4th ed.
Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies.
JOSPT / BJSM manual therapy reviews.

notes.title: 筋膜的神经支配与疼痛
notes.summary: 筋膜含 Aδ/C 纤维、交感神经末梢与感受器，可能参与伤害感受与疼痛敏化；但疼痛是多因素的，不能把“筋膜粘连”当作所有疼痛的原因。
points: 筋膜疼痛可表现为弥散、牵涉、压痛；需排除神经/关节/内脏。
手法/针刺短期可能调节疼痛感知，长期结构改变证据有限。
疼痛教育+渐进负荷仍是主线。
证据 B/C；避免“筋膜粘连必须松开”的绝对说法。
sources: Findley TW, Schleip R. Fascia Research.
Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies.

notes.title: 胸腰筋膜与腰-臀力传递
notes.summary: 胸腰筋膜（TLF）是多层结缔组织，连接背阔肌、臀大肌、腹壁、竖脊肌与骶骨；它参与躯干-下肢力传递与腰椎稳定，但具体机制仍有争议。
points: TLF 分层（前/中/后层），与腹内压、核心稳定相关。
背阔肌-臀大肌链在硬拉/深蹲/行走中参与力传递。
训练：髋铰链、核心抗旋转、臀肌力量；不要只“松筋膜”。
证据 B/C；腰痛多因素。
sources: Vleeming A, et al. Movement, Stability & Lumbopelvic Pain.
Findley TW, Schleip R. Fascia Research.
Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.

notes.title: 足底筋膜与足弓
notes.summary: 足底筋膜从跟骨到趾骨，维持内侧纵弓并在步态中参与“绞盘机制”（windlass）；足底筋膜炎通常与负荷、足弓/小腿/足内在肌相关。
points: 典型：晨起第一步/久坐后第一步足跟痛。
小腿拉伸、足底筋膜拉伸、提踵、短足、负荷管理。
鞋具/足弓支撑短期可辅助；无症状扁平足不需处理。
红旗：红肿热痛、发热、糖尿病足、不能负重。
sources: JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (plantar heel pain).
Brukner P, Khan K. Clinical Sports Medicine, 5th ed.

notes.title: 髂胫束：结构、争议与负荷
notes.summary: 髂胫束是阔筋膜张肌/臀肌筋膜延续的厚腱膜，不是可随意拉长的“筋”；髂胫束综合征更与跑量、髋控制、膝外侧负荷相关。
points: 臀中肌/髋外展控制、跑量、步频/步幅是常见因素。
暴力滚压/拉伸 ITB 证据有限，可能刺激局部。
训练：臀中肌、单腿控制、逐步加跑量。
证据 B/C；外侧膝痛需排除半月板/关节线。
sources: JOSPT / BJSM iliotibial band syndrome reviews.
Brukner P, Khan K. Clinical Sports Medicine, 5th ed.

notes.title: 结缔组织的负荷适应
notes.summary: 肌腱/筋膜等结缔组织对机械负荷产生适应（胶原合成/排列/刚度变化），但比肌肉慢；年龄、激素、营养与负荷史影响适应速度。
points: 渐进负荷是主线；突然加量易出问题。
肌腱/筋膜适应需要数周–数月，不要期待“一次手法”改变结构。
蛋白质/维生素 C/能量支持胶原合成；证据有限但合理。
证据 B；个体差异大。
sources: Connective Tissue Research reviews.
Journal of Applied Physiology tendon adaptation reviews.

notes.title: 筋膜手法/泡沫轴的证据
notes.summary: 泡沫轴、手法、筋膜刀等可短期改善活动度与疼痛感知，但“打破粘连/排毒/重置筋膜”缺乏可靠证据；效果多与神经/血流/触觉调节有关。
points: 泡沫轴 30–60 秒/部位，疼痛 3/10 以内。
手法后配合主动运动，效果更持久。
不要用暴力/大面积淤青；有凝血/皮肤问题慎用。
证据 B/C；不是替代力量训练。
sources: Journal of Bodywork and Movement Therapies.
JOSPT / BJSM manual therapy reviews.

notes.title: 黏弹性、蠕变与拉伸
notes.summary: 筋膜/肌腱具有黏弹性：持续低负荷会产生蠕变（长度增加），快速负荷更偏弹性；温度、水合、负荷历史影响行为。
points: 静态拉伸 30–60 秒可短期增加 ROM，但不等同永久延长。
热身提高组织温度/顺应性；冷环境更需热身。
长期 ROM 改善更多来自耐受/神经因素。
证据 B；避免暴力拉伸。
sources: Findley TW, Schleip R. Fascia Research.
Journal of Biomechanics reviews.

notes.title: 本体感觉：肌梭、腱器官与筋膜
notes.summary: 本体感觉来自肌梭、高尔基腱器官、关节感受器、皮肤与筋膜；它支撑平衡、动作控制与损伤预防。筋膜的具体贡献仍有争议。
points: 单腿平衡、闭眼平衡、不稳定面训练可改善本体感觉。
踝/膝损伤后本体感觉训练是康复重点。
力量训练本身也改善本体感觉/运动控制。
证据 B；不要神化“筋膜本体感觉”。
sources: Neuroscience / motor control reviews.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines.

disciplines.name: 营养学
disciplines.intro: 从能量平衡、蛋白质、碳水、脂肪与补剂出发，理解如何支持训练、恢复与体成分目标；优先食物，补剂只做补充。

notes.title: 能量平衡与 TDEE
notes.summary: 体重变化由长期能量平衡决定；TDEE = BMR + 活动 + 食物热效应。7700 kcal/kg 是粗略近似，实际受适应生热、组织成分影响。
points: 用 7 天平均体重趋势调整，而不是单日波动。
蛋白质/力量训练保护瘦体重。
不要追求过快速度；平台期先看依从性和活动量。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
ISSN Position Stands.

notes.title: 蛋白质：总量、分配与来源
notes.summary: 增肌/力量训练者蛋白质 1.6–2.2 g/kg/d 足够（ISSN 一般 1.4–2.0，减脂/高强度可更高）；每餐 0.25–0.4 g/kg，约 30–40g，分布 3–5 餐。
points: 优质蛋白：蛋/奶/肉/鱼/大豆；亮氨酸是重要信号。
训练后不必“30 分钟窗口”，全天总量更重要。
减脂期提高蛋白（1.8–2.4 g/kg）保护肌肉。
肾功能正常者高蛋白安全；肾病患者需医生。
sources: ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise (2017).
ACSM/AND/Dietitians of Canada Position Stand.
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

notes.title: 碳水与训练表现
notes.summary: 碳水支持训练表现和糖原恢复；摄入量随训练量 3–10 g/kg/d；纤维 25–35g/d。训练前后安排碳水有帮助，但总能量/总量优先。
points: 力量训练前 1–2 小时碳水；训练后正餐。
高纤维食物增加饱腹；训练前避免过多纤维。
“碳水恐惧”不必要；看总量和来源。
糖饮料/精制糖控制，不等于完全不吃碳水。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Sports Medicine / J Appl Physiol carbohydrate reviews.
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

notes.title: 脂肪、微量营养素与补剂
notes.summary: 脂肪 20–35% 总热量，保证必需脂肪酸；维生素 D 缺乏才补，铁/钙/维生素 B12 按饮食风险；肌酸 3–5g/d 是证据最扎实的运动补剂之一。
points: 脂肪过低影响激素/吸收；不必极低脂。
维生素 D 先检测；不要盲目大剂量。
肌酸：3–5g/d，无需冲击；注意水合。
补剂是补充，不是替代饮食；选择第三方检测。
sources: ISSN Position Stand: Creatine Supplementation (2017).
ACSM/AND position stands.
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

notes.title: 进餐时机：训练前后与蛋白分布
notes.summary: 总能量与总蛋白优先；训练前后安排碳水/蛋白有帮助，但“30 分钟窗口”被夸大。把蛋白均匀分布到 3–5 餐更实用。
points: 每餐 30–40g 蛋白；训练前 1–2h 碳水+蛋白。
训练后 1–2h 内正餐即可；不必立刻喝 shake。
睡前蛋白（酪蛋白/牛奶）可选。
证据 A/B；个体耐受优先。
sources: ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise (2017).
ACSM/AND position stands.

notes.title: 运动补剂：哪些证据较强
notes.summary: 证据较强的运动补剂：肌酸、咖啡因、β-丙氨酸（特定高强度）、硝酸盐（特定耐力）、维生素 D（缺乏者）。大多数“燃脂/睾酮”补剂证据弱。
points: 肌酸 3–5g/d；咖啡因 3–6mg/kg（按耐受）；β-丙氨酸 4–6g/d 分次。
选择第三方检测产品；注意比赛禁用清单。
补剂是补充，不能替代饮食/训练/睡眠。
证据 A/B；个体反应差异大。
sources: ISSN Position Stands (creatine, protein, beta-alanine).
Australian Institute of Sport Supplement Framework.

notes.title: 低能量可用性（LEA/RED-S）
notes.summary: 长期能量摄入不足以支持训练与生理功能，会出现低能量可用性，影响激素、骨、免疫、情绪与表现；不是“越少吃越好”。
points: 能量可用性 =（摄入−运动消耗）/瘦体重；长期过低有风险。
女性、耐力/体重级运动员风险更高；月经紊乱/反复伤病是警示。
处理：增加能量摄入、降低过量运动、保证蛋白/碳水/睡眠。
证据 A/B；需要专业评估。
sources: IOC consensus on relative energy deficiency in sport (RED-S).
ACSM/AND position stands.

notes.title: 减脂期保留肌肉
notes.summary: 减脂期保留肌肉的关键：温和赤字、足够蛋白、力量训练、睡眠与恢复；过快减重会丢肌肉/影响表现。
points: 力量训练维持强度/容量；有氧适量。
监测：体重趋势、腰围、力量、精力。
sources: ISSN Position Stand: Diets and Body Composition.
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

notes.title: 膳食纤维与肠道
notes.summary: 膳食纤维 25–35g/d，支持肠道菌群、饱腹与血糖；增加纤维要循序渐进并补水，训练前避免过多高纤维食物。
points: 来源：蔬菜/水果/全谷/豆类；多样化。
突然大量增加会胀气；分次/逐步。
训练前 1–2h 少纤维/少油。
证据 B；肠道症状明显时看医生/营养师。
sources: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
Nutrients reviews.

notes.title: 水合与电解质
notes.summary: 水合影响血容量、体温调节与表现；长时间/大量出汗需要补钠等电解质，但不要过量喝水导致低钠血症。
points: 日常 2–3L（按体重/气候/出汗调整）。
训练前后称重估算出汗率；每丢失 1kg 补约 1–1.5L。
超过 60–90 分钟高强度/大量出汗考虑电解质。
证据 A/B；尿液颜色可粗略参考。
sources: ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.
Guyton & Hall. Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed.

notes.title: 植物性饮食与增肌
notes.summary: 植物蛋白可以支持增肌，但需要关注总蛋白、亮氨酸、B12、铁、锌、omega-3 与热量；豆类/大豆/谷物搭配可提高氨基酸谱。
points: 蛋白 1.8–2.2g/kg；大豆/豌豆/豆类搭配。
B12 需补充；铁/锌关注；omega-3 可考虑藻油。
植物饮食纤维高，训练前注意胃肠耐受。
证据 B；个体差异大。
sources: ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise (2017).
American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.

notes.title: 酒精与恢复
notes.summary: 酒精会影响睡眠、蛋白合成、水合与恢复，且提供空热量；不是必需品，训练日/恢复期尽量控制。
points: 剂量越大影响越明显；不要用酒精助眠。
训练后大量饮酒可能影响蛋白合成/恢复。
酒精有利尿作用，注意水合/电解质。
证据 B；个体差异/文化因素。
sources: Sports Medicine / JISSN alcohol and recovery reviews.
ACSM/AND position stands.

cross.title: 卧推时肩胛内侧缘不适：四学科整合分析
cross.summary: 水平推（卧推/俯卧撑/推举）时肩胛内侧缘不适很常见，但原因不是单一的“菱形肌紧”。需要从解剖、生理、筋膜、营养/恢复四个层面交叉看，先排除红旗。

sections.title: 运动解剖学视角
sections.body: 肩胛内侧缘是菱形肌、肩胛提肌、前锯肌等附着区；水平推要求肩胛后缩/稳定，前锯肌离心控制肩胛前伸/上回旋，菱形肌/斜方肌协同。胸椎伸展不足、肩袖控制差、肩胛稳定肌耐力不足会让内侧缘负荷增加；长胸神经/C5-C7 神经根受激惹也可表现为肩胛/上肢症状。

sections.title: 运动生理学视角
sections.body: 负荷突然增加、组数/重量过大、肩胛稳定肌耐力不足、疲劳后动作变形，都会让局部组织负荷超标；疼痛敏感、睡眠不足、压力会放大症状；DOMS 常在 24–48 小时出现，但持续锐痛/夜间痛要警惕。

sections.title: 筋膜学视角
sections.body: 肩胛周围筋膜与臂线、螺旋线、浅背线连续；胸腰筋膜/背阔肌-臀肌链可能影响肩胛位置与力传递。筋膜链是描述性模型，不是诊断；不要只“松解菱形肌”，要同时看肩胛控制与负荷。

sections.title: 营养与恢复视角
sections.body: 总能量、蛋白质、水合、睡眠影响恢复；没有哪种食物能“消除肩胛痛”。减脂过快/能量不足会增加疲劳和受伤风险；训练日保证碳水与蛋白，恢复日保证睡眠。

cross.integrated: ① 先减量 20–30%，停疼痛动作 1–2 周；② 肩胛俯卧撑、墙面滑手、前锯肌推、面拉、划船，2–3 组无痛范围；③ 胸椎伸展/旋转；④ 卧推改中立握/哑铃/地板卧推，控制肩胛后缩；⑤ 疼痛不超过 3/10、24 小时不加重；⑥ 2–4 周无改善，或出现翼状肩/麻木/无力，转物理治疗/骨科/神经评估。
redFlags: 翼状肩/肩胛内侧明显突出
夜间痛/发热/不明原因体重下降
双侧症状/大小便异常（颈髓红旗）
cross.evidence: B/C（机制 + 临床推理；不是诊断算法）
sources: Neumann DA. Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System, 3rd ed.
JOSPT Clinical Practice Guidelines (shoulder/neck).
Myers TW. Anatomy Trains, 4th ed.（模型，非诊断标准）
ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed.

cross.title: 跑步膝（髌股疼痛）：四学科整合
cross.summary: 跑步膝前痛常见，但不是“膝盖磨坏了”。需要从解剖、负荷生理、筋膜/髋踝链、营养恢复四个层面交叉看，先排除红旗。

sections.title: 运动解剖学视角
sections.body: 髌股关节承受股四头拉力与髌骨滑动；髋外展/外旋控制、股四头力量、踝背屈与足弓都会改变膝前负荷。膝内扣、步幅过大、下坡跑可能增加髌股压力。

sections.title: 运动生理学视角
sections.body: 跑量/速度突然增加、恢复不足、疼痛敏感与睡眠压力会放大症状；髌股疼痛是负荷相关，不是单纯结构损伤。逐步加量、力量与耐受训练是主线。

sections.title: 筋膜学视角
sections.body: 髂胫束/阔筋膜、髌骨支持带、小腿筋膜与臀肌筋膜连续；但“筋膜粘连”不是唯一解释。训练臀中肌/小腿/足内在肌比暴力滚压更可靠。

sections.title: 营养与恢复视角
sections.body: 能量不足、蛋白不足、水合/睡眠差会影响恢复与受伤风险；没有单一食物能治跑步膝。减脂过快会降低恢复能力。

cross.integrated: ① 调整跑量/速度（先减 30–50%），避免下坡/突然加量；② 髋外展/外旋、股四头、提踵/足内在肌，2–3 组无痛；③ 步频/步幅小幅调整，先观察 2 周；④ 疼痛≤3/10、24h 不加重；⑤ 明显肿胀/交锁/打软/夜间痛→骨科。
sources: JOSPT CPG: Patellofemoral Pain (2019)
Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine
Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System

cross.title: 久坐腰痛：四学科整合
cross.summary: 久坐后腰痛很常见，多数是非特异性腰痛；不是“坐姿一定错”。需要从解剖、负荷生理、筋膜/髋胸链、营养恢复四层面看，先排红旗。

sections.title: 运动解剖学视角
sections.body: 腰椎、髋、胸椎与核心共同承担负荷；久坐使髋屈肌/胸椎活动减少，臀肌/核心耐力可能下降。骨盆前倾是描述，不是诊断。

sections.title: 运动生理学视角
sections.body: 静态负荷、缺乏活动、睡眠/压力与恐惧回避会影响疼痛；保持活动+渐进力量+疼痛教育是一线。多数不需要影像。

sections.title: 筋膜学视角
sections.body: 胸腰筋膜连接背阔肌/臀肌/腹壁/竖脊肌，参与力传递；但“筋膜粘连”不是唯一原因。髋铰链/核心训练比单纯松解更可靠。

sections.title: 营养与恢复视角
sections.body: 总能量、蛋白、水合、睡眠影响恢复；减脂过快/能量不足会增加疲劳。没有单一食物能治腰痛。

cross.integrated: ① 每 30–45 分钟起身 2–3 分钟；② 步行/髋铰链/死虫/鸟狗/侧平板/臀桥；③ 逐步硬拉/分腿蹲；④ 疼痛教育+睡眠；⑤ 红旗（鞍区麻木/大小便障碍/发热/夜间痛/进行性无力）→就医。
sources: Lancet Low Back Pain Series (2018)
NICE NG59
JOSPT Low Back Pain CPG

cross.title: 踝扭伤后反复不稳：四学科整合
cross.summary: 踝内翻扭伤后反复“打软/不稳”常见；需要从韧带解剖、本体感觉/力量生理、筋膜/小腿链、营养恢复四层面看，先排除骨折。

sections.title: 运动解剖学视角
sections.body: 外侧韧带（ATFL/CFL）与腓骨肌、胫后肌、足内在肌共同稳定踝/足；距骨倾斜/前抽屉可评估松弛，但急性期受疼痛影响。

sections.title: 运动生理学视角
sections.body: 扭伤后本体感觉/腓骨肌反应下降，反复扭伤风险增加；平衡/力量训练与渐进负重是核心。急性期先排除骨折（Ottawa 规则）。

sections.title: 筋膜学视角
sections.body: 小腿筋膜/腓骨肌筋膜/足底筋膜连续；筋膜链是模型，不是诊断。提踵/短足/单腿平衡比单纯拉伸更可靠。

sections.title: 营养与恢复视角
sections.body: 蛋白/能量/水合/睡眠支持组织修复；没有单一补剂能“修复韧带”。恢复期避免过度制动。

cross.integrated: ① Ottawa 规则排除骨折；② 保护+渐进负重；③ 踝背屈/提踵/腓骨肌/短足/单腿平衡；④ 2–4 周逐步跑跳；⑤ 反复不稳/明显松弛→骨科/物理治疗。
sources: JOSPT CPG: Ankle Ligament Sprains (2021)
Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine
Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System

cross.title: 增肌平台期：训练/生理/营养/恢复
cross.summary: 增肌平台期不是“基因到头了”，常见原因是容量/强度不足、恢复不够、热量/蛋白不足或测量误差；需要四学科一起看。

sections.title: 运动解剖学视角
sections.body: 动作选择/活动范围/力臂影响肌肉张力；长期同一动作可能适应。可换动作角度、增加拉伸位负荷、调整器械。

sections.title: 运动生理学视角
sections.body: 机械张力是主轴；容量 10–20 组/肌群/周、RIR 1–3、渐进超负荷。睡眠/压力/同期有氧过多会限制适应。

sections.title: 筋膜学视角
sections.body: 结缔组织适应较慢；不要频繁换计划。肌腱/筋膜需要渐进负荷；泡沫轴/拉伸是辅助，不是增肌手段。

sections.title: 营养与恢复视角
sections.body: 热量盈余 5–15%、蛋白 1.6–2.2g/kg、碳水支持训练；体重 2–3 周不涨先加 100–200 kcal。测量误差/水合会干扰判断。

cross.integrated: ① 记录 4 周训练/体重/围度；② 每肌群容量是否达标；③ 主项是否渐进；④ 热量/蛋白/睡眠；⑤ 每 6–8 周 deload；⑥ 仍无变化再换计划/找教练。
sources: ACSM Guidelines, 11th ed.
Schoenfeld BJ, et al. hypertrophy reviews
ISSN Position Stand: Protein and Exercise (2017)

articles.title: Effects of In-Season Contrast Strength Training on Jump Performance and Sprint Ability in Female Field Hockey Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Ramiro Chilingirian-Padrón, Tania Álvarez-Yates, Oscar García-García
articles.abstract: Chilingirian-Padrón, R, Álvarez-Yates, T, and García-García, O. Effects of in-season contrast strength training on jump performance and sprint ability in female field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The purpose of this study was to examine the effects of a 6-week in-season contrast strength training program incorporating sport-specific tasks on neuromuscular performance in sub-elite female field hockey players. Twenty-five athletes completed a pre-post single-cohort intervention integrated into their regular team schedule. Each session consisted of 3 sequential blocks: (a) a high-load strength exercise targeting maximal strength or hypertrophy (70-85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]); (b) a biomechanically related explosive action performed at low load (∼30% 1RM) and high execution velocity; and (c) a high-speed sport-specific task. Jump performance was assessed using bilateral and unilateral countermovement jumps (CMJs) and free arm CMJ, whereas sprint ability was evaluated through 10- and 20-m sprints. A mixed-model repeated-measures analysis of variance was used to determine the effects of the intervention, with Time (Pre, Post) as within-subject factor and Playing Position (defenders, midfielders, forwards) as between-subject factor, with the level of significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements were observed in all jump and sprint assessments: jump performance increased by 5.7-29.6%, whereas sprint ability improved by 1.6-1.9%. These findings indicate that 6 weeks of contrast strength training incorporating high-speed sports-specific tasks performed during the competitive season elicited meaningful improvements in stretch-shortening cycle-related jump performance and sprint ability in sub-elite female field hockey players.

articles.title: Athletic Performance Adaptations: Just Training Sprints or Combining Sprints With Three Different Strength Training Methods?
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Glenn Trane, Stein Edgar Rodahl, Olav Melhus Gomo et al.
articles.abstract: Trane, G, Rodahl, SE, Gomo, OM, Mehus, HA, Helgerud, J, and Unhjem, RJ. Athletic performance adaptations: Just training sprints or combining sprints with three different strength training methods? J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-In this exploratory study, we compared the effects of combining maximal strength training (MST), hypertrophy training (HT), or explosive strength training (EST) with sprint running vs. sprint running alone in control (CON). Fifty-eight recreationally active, nonstrength-trained men and women were randomized to 8 weeks, 3 sessions/week of MST (4 × 4 squats at ≥ 85% 1 repetition maximum [1RM]), HT (3 × 8-12 squats at ∼70-80% 1RM), EST (4 × 6-7 squat jumps at body weight), or CON (no strength training). All 4 groups performed 2 weekly 6 × 25-meter sprints. Maximal and explosive strength, sprint running performance, endurance performance determinants, and 30-second Wingate test cycling performance were evaluated. Leg press maximal voluntary isometric force (MVIF) improved more after MST (+14.5%) than after EST (+5.2%, p = 0.004) and CON (p ≤ 0.001), and more after HT (+10.6%) than CON (p = 0.008). The squat dynamic rate of force development improved more after MST (+37.4%) and HT (+36.0%) than CON (p = 0.014 and 0.002). Moreover, 0-25-meter sprint time improved more after MST (-0.11 s) and HT (-0.10 s) than CON (p = 0.019 and 0.042). Running economy improved more after MST (-2.5%) than CON (p = 0.026). Wingate test average power output improved more after MST (+6.6%) and HT (+6.9%) than EST (p = 0.020 and 0.010) and CON (p = 0.016 and 0.009). Peak power output improved more after MST (+11.8%) and HT (+10.1%) than CON (p = 0.011 and 0.040). ΔMVIF was associated with performance changes. Integrating sprint training with high-load strength training improved maximal and explosive strength and athletic performance more than sprint training alone, whereas this was not observed in EST. Performance improvements were attributed to enhanced maximal strength. Given the exploratory study design and the use of Fisher's least significant difference post hoc tests for between-group comparisons, these findings should be interpreted with caution and regarded as hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: Effects of Ballistic and Traditional Half-Squat Training With Light Loads on Strength, Jump, and Sprint Performance in Young Rugby Players: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Santiago Zabaloy, Piotr Zmijewski, Tomás T Freitas et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study examined the effects of two 6-week in-season training interventions using light loads (30%-40% 1-repetition maximum) and contrasting strategies: (1) ballistic jump squat (JS) and (2) traditional half squat on strength, jump, and sprint performance in youth rugby players. METHODS: Twenty-five highly trained players completed the randomized controlled trial, training 3 times per week alongside regular rugby practice and competition. Performance assessments included half-squat 1-repetition maximum, mean propulsive velocity, squat jump, countermovement jump, and 30-m sprint speed at 3 time points. RESULTS: Both groups improved maximal strength and jump performance, with greater gains observed in the JS group (≈7% vs 4% for strength, ≈16% vs 8% for jump performance). The JS group also showed specific improvements in relative strength and heavy-load mean propulsive velocity, whereas the half-squat group improved mean propulsive velocity at lighter loads. A significant group × time interaction was found for countermovement jump, favoring the JS condition. Despite these neuromuscular improvements, sprint performance decreased in both groups, with no between-group differences. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that light-load ballistic training may provide a more effective stimulus for improving strength and power qualities during the in-season period, likely due to its velocity-oriented and fully accelerative nature. However, strength-power gains alone appear insufficient to prevent decreases in sprint performance under congested fixture schedules. From a practical standpoint, incorporating light-load ballistic exercises may enhance neuromuscular performance while minimizing fatigue, but additional sprint-specific training is required to maintain or improve sprint speed in youth rugby players.

articles.title: Moderate-Intensity Interval Training Is Sufficient to Increase Muscle Mitochondrial Respiratory Capacity and Exercise Tolerance in Young Untrained Men.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Jerzy A Zoladz, Marcin Grandys, Barbara Pakula et al.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is considerable evidence that physical activity can stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in muscles, enhance maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate, improve physical fitness, and help maintain overall health in humans. On the other hand, there is growing evidence that excessive training load may have a detrimental effect on mitochondria and glucose homeostasis. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that moderate-intensity interval training (MIIT) would be sufficient to increase muscle mitochondrial oxidative capacity and exercise tolerance in untrained healthy people. METHODS: Eleven young, healthy, untrained males took part in this study. They performed a 7-week endurance training program (MIIT) on a cycle ergometer, composed of 4 sessions per week, each lasting 40 min. Before and after the MIIT training program, a pulmonary maximal oxygen consumption (V̇O2max) as well as lactate threshold (LT) were determined and a muscle biopsy from the m. vastus lateralis was taken to evaluate the level of muscle proteins related to energy metabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis, and to measure the muscle's maximal mitochondrial respiration rate. RESULTS: The training resulted in an increase of skeletal muscle homogenate V̇O2max (by ~50%, P=0.001), due to increased mitochondrial mass and the enrichment of mitochondria with the individual respiratory chain complexes. The MIIT increased the power output at the lactate threshold (PO at LT) by ~43 W (P=0.001) and the pulmonary V̇O2max by 7% (P=0.01) and had no adverse effect on blood glucose homeostasis. CONCLUSIONS: MIIT, which is a less intense form of training than the commonly used types of interval training, effectively induces a range of beneficial muscular and systemic adaptations that contribute to improvement of physical fitness and maintenances good health in humans.

articles.title: Summary of the 2026 Professionals in Nutrition for Exercise and Sport "10 Questions/10 Experts" Session-Are Sports Nutrition Guidelines Too Elite Focused for Recreational Athletes?
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Thorben Aussieker, Louise M Burke, Judith Haudum et al.
articles.abstract: This article provides a synopsis of the 10 Questions/10 Experts session at the 2026 American College of Sports Medicine Annual Meeting, which examined whether sports nutrition guidelines are equally applicable from recreational to elite athletes. Each speaker considered the validity of a given common "myth" statement and provided an evidence-based opinion to support, bust, or qualify propositions addressing the following questions: (a) Are sports nutrition guidelines based primarily on studies of elite athletes, and are they too serious for recreational athletes? (b) Do recreational marathon runners need the same in-race carbohydrate recommendations as elite marathon runners? (c) Must recreational athletes consume 1.6 g·kg-1·day-1 of protein to benefit from exercise training? (d) Does nitrate supplementation benefit elite and recreational athletes equally? (e) Do recreational athletes need a structured fluid intake plan? (f) Is sodium bicarbonate loading relevant only to elite athletes? (g) Do recreational and elite athletes require more micronutrients than suggested by the Recommended Dietary Allowances? (h) Is eating after 8:00 p.m. detrimental to performance or recovery in recreational athletes? (i) Are recreational athletes at greater risk for suboptimal vitamin D status because indoor occupations reduce sunlight exposure? and (j) Should recreational athletes train with low carbohydrate availability to amplify adaptation? This article describes the content of each presentation, including the most important evidence, practical implications, and conclusions identified by the presenters.

articles.title: Performance and Physiological Responses to Strength Training Programs in Elite Judo Athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Bruno T Campos, João Gabriel D S Rodrigues, Cesar C Cal Abad et al.
articles.abstract: Campos, BT, Rodrigues, JGdS, Cal Abad, CC, Bachi, ALL, dos Santos, CMM, Tritto, AC, Kons, RL, Penna, EM, and Prado, LS. Performance and physiological responses to strength training programs in elite judo athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study compared the effects of 2 short-term strength training models, block planning (BP) and undulating planning (UP), on performance, physiological, and perceptual responses in elite judo athletes. We hypothesized that BP would induce greater physiological strain due to the concentration of training stimuli. Eighteen judokas (14 men and 4 women) were randomly assigned to BP (n = 9) or UP (n = 9) for 4 weeks, performing 6 weekly strength sessions alongside technical-tactical training. Performance outcomes included countermovement jump (CMJ), muscle power (back squat and bent-over row), and the Special Judo Fitness Test (SJFT). Monitoring variables included internal load, heart rate variability (HRV), and well-being, while physiological markers included creatine kinase, tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and cortisol. Data were analyzed using 2-way repeated-measures ANOVA (p < 0.05). Both groups improved SJFT performance (p < 0.01), with no between-group differences. Block planning increased lower-limb peak power (p = 0.01; d = 0.90), whereas UP showed no meaningful change. Upper-limb power and CMJ did not change in either group. Internal load showed different temporal patterns between models. Block planning presented higher HRVcv values (p = 0.04), indicating greater autonomic perturbation. Creatine kinase and TNF-α increased over time in both groups (p ≤ 0.05), while cortisol showed an interaction without clear post hoc differences. In conclusion, BP improved lower-limb power but increased physiological strain, whereas UP elicited similar judo-specific improvements with lower recovery demands. These findings highlight the importance of training organization for balancing performance and recovery in elite judo athletes.

articles.title: Biomechanical link between knee osteoarthritis and lumbar spine loading: An experimental and simulation-based analysis.
articles.authors: Ali Jamshidian, Alireza Rouyin, Hamed Nazemi et al.
articles.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) and low back pain (LBP) frequently co-occur, yet their biomechanical link remains unclear. This exploratory study investigated whether KOA gait is associated with altered trunk muscle forces and lumbar loading. Motion-capture and ground-reaction-force data were collected from eight individuals with mild-to-moderate medial KOA and ten healthy controls. Participant-scaled OpenSim models were used to estimate trunk muscle forces and lumbar joint reaction forces (JRFs). Between-group comparisons used Mann-Whitney U tests with false-discovery-rate correction. Walking speed did not differ between groups, whereas stride length was shorter in KOA (q = 0.033). Proximal kinematic differences were limited: no pelvic variable remained significant after correction, and only mean thoracic lateral bending differed (q = 0.032), with a small absolute magnitude. Mean knee angle differed between groups (q = 0.014), with additional differences in peak knee and ankle kinematics (q ≤ 0.006). Model-predicted mean and peak multifidus, longissimus, and iliocostalis forces were greater in KOA, whereas internal oblique forces were lower (all q < 0.05). Mean and peak lumbar compression were greater in KOA at all six levels from T12-L1 to L5-S1 (all raw p < 0.001; q < 0.05), and anterior-posterior JRFs were greater at selected levels. These higher muscle forces and JRFs, despite limited group-level proximal kinematic differences, may reflect attenuation or cancellation of heterogeneous individual gait adaptations during averaging, even though these adaptations may still influence internal mechanical demands.

articles.title: Lower-Body Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations in Response to Concurrent Training in Trained Young Males.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Miguel Gomes, Mara Costa, Pedro Pezarat-Correia et al.
articles.abstract: Gomes, M, Costa, M, Pezarat-Correia, P, and Mendonca, GV. Lower-body strength and hypertrophy adaptations in response to concurrent training in trained young males. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined the interference effect of concurrent training (CT) on maximal and explosive strength and muscle morphology in trained young males. Thirty subjects were randomly assigned to endurance training (E), resistance training (R), or CT for 11 weeks. The intervention comprised 2 mesocycles: weeks 1-5 emphasizing maximal strength, and weeks 6-11 targeting explosive strength. Assessments were conducted at baseline, mid-training, and post-training, and included leg-press maximal voluntary isometric contraction (MVIC), rate of force development (RFD), countermovement jump kinetics, and vastus lateralis cross-sectional area and pennation angle. Maximal voluntary isometric contraction increased only in the R group (18.4 ± 10.2%, p = 0.015). Peak RFD improved in both R (31.8 ± 23.2%) and CT (23.1 ± 27.9%), although with distinct time courses: R improved progressively across both mesocycles, whereas CT improved only during the second. Early-phase RFD (0-50 ms) increased in the R group from mid-training onward, whereas the CT group improved only from mid- to post-training (38.3 ± 40.4%, p = 0.021), accompanied by greater quadriceps electromyographic activity (p < 0.05). No changes in RFD were observed in E during training. Countermovement jump positive impulse improved in both R (12.7 ± 9.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 8.3%, p < 0.05), with no evidence of interference in jump-related explosive performance. Cross-sectional area increased in both R (17.0 ± 13.0%) and CT (8.8 ± 9.4%, p < 0.05). Pennation angle increased in CT (10.1 ± 12.9%) and R (18.6 ± 15.1%). These findings indicate that, although CT may limit MVIC development and delay early-phase RFD adaptations, it does not hinder explosive performance when resistance training is oriented toward rapid-strength development. Thus, CT can be effectively implemented in trained individuals when resistance training is periodized to emphasize neural-driven explosive or hypertrophy-related adaptations.

articles.title: Ergocycling-Based Repeated-Sprint Training in Hypoxia Performed at Either 3,000 m or 2,000 m Similarly Impacts Overground Performance in Under-18 Field Hockey Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Dorian Le Moan, Jean Slawinski, Léa Lecru et al.
articles.abstract: Le Moan, D, Slawinski, J, Lecru, L, Braize, E, Brocherie, F, and Bouten, J. Ergocycling-based repeated-sprint training in hypoxia performed at either 3,000 m or 2,000 m similarly impacts overground performance in under-18 field hockey players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to compare the effects of 2 levels of hypoxic stress during ergocycling-based repeated-sprint training in hypoxia (RSH) on overground repeated-sprint ability (RSA). Fifteen highly trained under-18 male field hockey players performed a 3-week training program with 6 ergocycling-based RSH sessions (3 × 6 10-s "all-out" sprints with 20-second intraset passive recovery and 5-minute interset rest; 2 sessions per week) under moderate (MH, FiO2 14.5%, simulated altitude of 3,000 m, n = 8) or low normobaric hypoxia (LH, FiO2 16.3%, 2,000 m, n = 7). Peak (PPO) and mean power output (MPO) were recorded during each RSH session. At Pre- and Postintervention, overground sprinting horizontal force-velocity profiles and RSA test (6 × 20-m "all-out" sprints interspersed by 20 seconds) were performed. Ergocycling-based PPO (p < 0.001) and MPO (p = 0.015) improved significantly for both groups from training 1 to 6. However, overground theoretical maximal force and theoretical maximal power remained unchanged (both p > 0.377), and theoretical maximal velocity (p = 0.026) was significantly decreased for both groups. Although no significant effect (time, group, interaction) was observed for overground RSA best time and sprint decrement (all p > 0.139), RSA total time decreased (p = 0.048) in both MH and LH (-1.1 ± 2.9% and -0.9 ± 1.0%), indicating performance enhancement, irrespective of the hypoxic stress. Using moderate or low normobaric hypoxic stress during a 3-week ergocycling-based RSH intervention resulted in similar improvement during training, albeit with limited, but not negligible, transferability effect in overground performance.

articles.title: Combined time-restricted feeding and resistance training enhance tirzepatide-induced improvements in adiposity and whole-body insulin sensitivity in female mice.
articles.authors: Ana Paula Azevêdo Macêdo, Luciana Renata da Conceição de Mattis, Robson Damasceno de Lima et al.
articles.abstract: Tirzepatide is a dual agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors with potent effects on body weight regulation, glucose homeostasis and metabolic health. However, its interaction with dietary and exercise interventions as well as its impact on obesity and hepatic metabolic pathways, particularly in females, remain unclear. Here, we tested whether tirzepatide, alone or combined with time-restricted feeding (TRF) or resistance training, modulates energy balance, strength performance, adipose tissue remodelling, insulin sensitivity and hepatic lipid accumulation in female mice. Female Swiss mice after 10 weeks of obesity induction were treated with tirzepatide, TRF or resistance training for 8 weeks. Tirzepatide was administered subcutaneously using a dose-escalation protocol. TRF consisted of a 12 h feeding window, and resistance training was performed as stair climbing on alternating days. Body weight, caloric intake and feed efficiency were monitored longitudinally. Glucose homeostasis was assessed by intraperitoneal glucose and insulin tolerance tests. Adipose depots, skeletal muscle and liver mass were quantified, and hepatic lipid accumulation was evaluated by histology and RT-qPCR of lipogenic metabolism genes. Tirzepatide reduced body weight gain and feed efficiency, consistent with a negative energy balance. When combined with TRF and resistance training, tirzepatide accelerated weight loss, and the addition of resistance training further enhanced this effect, bringing body weight close to control levels. These effects were associated with reduced adipose mass and adipocyte hypertrophy, indicating improved adipose tissue remodelling. Resistance training improved strength performance and increased skeletal muscle mass. Tirzepatide combined with TRF, with or without resistance training, improved glucose tolerance in female mice. All interventions reduced hepatic lipid accumulation. Collectively, tirzepatide, particularly in combination with TRF and resistance training, exerts enhanced metabolic benefits on obesity, insulin sensitivity and metabolic regulation in female mice. KEY POINTS: Tirzepatide combined with time-restricted feeding and resistance training produced greater reductions in body weight and adiposity in obese female mice. Combined interventions improved whole-body insulin sensitivity more effectively than isolated strategies. Resistance training preserved skeletal muscle mass during tirzepatide-induced weight loss. All interventions similarly reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and lipogenic gene expression. Tirzepatide-based therapies enhanced systemic metabolic health without additional hepatic benefits from combined interventions.

articles.title: Central and Peripheral Fatigue Following Free-Weight and Smith Machine Squat Training: Neuromuscular Efficiency in Knee Extensors.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Daniel Marcos-Frutos, Antonio Martos-Arregui, Amador García-Ramos et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Free-weight (FW) and machine-guided exercises have been shown to promote similar strength and hypertrophy adaptations. Under such conditions, the exercise modality that induces less fatigue may be considered more efficient and advantageous for training prescription. PURPOSE: To compare the mechanical, perceptual, and neuromuscular fatigue induced by a squat strength training session performed with FW or a Smith machine (SM). METHODS: Nineteen young strength-trained men (age = 23.5 [3.8] y; strength training experience = 4.7 [2.4] y) completed 2 sessions in a randomized order, each involving 4 sets of 9 repetitions at 70% 1-repetition maximum and differing only in the squat modality (FW or SM). Mechanical fatigue was assessed by velocity loss during training and by pre-post changes in isometric force; perceptual fatigue was assessed by subjectively estimated repetitions in reserve and neuromuscular fatigue (ie, peripheral and central fatigue components) via the twitch interpolation technique during isometric unilateral knee extension. RESULTS: No fatigue differences were observed for velocity loss or perceptual fatigue variables (P = .136-.313). In contrast, most peripheral and central fatigue variables showed significant posttraining differences (P < .001-.021), with FW squats promoting greater posttraining peripheral and central fatigue. CONCLUSIONS: Given the comparable adaptations typically reported for FW and SM exercises, the SM squat may represent a more efficient option for promoting strength adaptations while minimizing neuromuscular fatigue in knee extensors.

articles.title: Aerobic exercise preconditioning enhances skeletal muscle resistance and recovery after contusion: involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis.
articles.authors: Wei Wang, Zhao Tian, Peijin Li et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Compared with passive recovery after injury, exercise preconditioning may provide an active strategy for improving the subsequent response of skeletal muscle to injury. This study aimed to investigate the effects of aerobic exercise preconditioning (AEP) on skeletal muscle injury (SMI) and post-injury repair, with particular focus on the involvement of the SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and changes in PGC-1α acetylation. METHODS: This study initially investigated the effects of continuous aerobic exercise on skeletal muscle in healthy mice. Subsequently, the influence of AEP on injury severity and regenerative repair of the gastrocnemius muscle was examined in mice with SMI. Western blotting was used to determine the expression levels of SIRT1 and PGC-1α proteins, immunoprecipitation was performed to assess the acetylation status of PGC-1α, and qRT-PCR was used to analyze the expression of genes associated with mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers and muscle regeneration. Finally, the involvement of SIRT1 signaling in the AEP-associated response to SMI was further examined using the pharmacological SIRT1 inhibitor EX527. RESULTS: Continuous aerobic exercise was associated with increased SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling and changes in mitochondrial biogenesis-related markers in the gastrocnemius muscle of healthy mice. AEP was associated with reduced injury-related changes and an improved post-injury repair profile in mice with SMI. During the early stage after injury, AEP was accompanied by sustained SIRT1/ PGC-1α signaling and reduced PGC-1α acetylation. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 with EX527 partially attenuated the AEP-associated protective and reparative effects on the injured gastrocnemius muscle. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that AEP establishes an adaptive state in skeletal muscle that is associated with reduced injury-related damage and an enhanced post-injury reparative response. The SIRT1/PGC-1α axis and altered PGC-1α acetylation may contribute to these AEP-associated effects.

articles.title: Food as Biological Information: A Testable Dietome Framework for Precision Nutrition and Whole-Food Meal Design.
articles.authors: Mohammad Nazrul Islam Bhuiyan
articles.abstract: Nutrition science has established the importance of energy, essential nutrients, dietary patterns, and food matrices, yet researchers often study these dimensions separately from the biological systems that transform and interpret a meal. This Perspective proposed the Dietome as a testable, systems-level description of food-derived inputs and the Informational Nutrition Framework (INF), comprising encoding, transmission, decoding, execution, and biological memory. The framework integrates sensory perception and eating behaviour with digestion, microbial metabolism, host signalling, and context-dependent responses. Its novelty is not the claim that food contains a literal code, but the proposal to connect food composition and structure to measurable, falsifiable predictions about meal-level responses. Evidence from personalized postprandial prediction, foodome network analysis, microbial short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-associated chromatin regulation, and computational diet modelling illustrates both opportunity and limitations. A worked meal example shows how to evaluate minimally processed foods and their combinations before considering engineered formulations. The Perspective also identifies sustainability, developmental nutrition, and food-allergy prevention as domains requiring cautious, evidence-specific application. Dietary microRNAs and long-term nutritional memory remain less established than conventional nutrient and microbial-metabolite pathways. The framework should therefore be judged by prospective validation, causal evidence, clinical utility, cultural acceptability, and environmental performance, not by terminology alone.

articles.title: Female Soccer Players at High Risk of Injury Maintained Improved Knee Abduction Load 6 Months After Neuromuscular Training Program.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.authors: Jeffrey B Taylor, Thomas J Hockenjos, Anh-Dung Nguyen et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate immediate and long-term (retention) improvements in knee abduction moment (KAM) following a neuromuscular training (NMT) program with augmented biofeedback in individuals at high and low risk for injury. DESIGN: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial. METHODS: One hundred fifty adolescent female soccer players were enrolled in a 6-week NMT program and randomized to biofeedback training groups: NMT + Hip-focus (NMT+H), NMT + Knee-focus (NMT+K), or NMT with a sham biofeedback. NMT was completed 3 times each week with augmented biofeedback delivered once per week. Standard 3-dimensional motion analysis of a drop vertical jump over artificial turf with embedded force platforms was performed at baseline (PRE), immediately following training (POST), and 6 months post training (RET). Baseline measures of KAM were used to stratify participants into low- (n = 87, 12.7 ± 2.2 years, 153.0 ± 11.4 cm, 47.2 ± 11.8 kg) and high-risk (n = 44, 14.0 ± 1.8 years, 161.6 ± 5.8 cm, 53.5 ± 9.2 kg) groups, based on a previously determined cut point. A mixed-design analysis of variance with between-group factors of risk (high, low) and training group (NMT+H, NMT+K, NMT), and a repeated within-group factor of session (PRE, POST, RET) were used for the analysis. RESULTS: A significant interaction was identified between risk and session (P < .001). Within training groups, the high-risk group had a significant reduction in KAM from baseline to posttest, and from baseline to 6 months (PRE: -37.5 ± 9.0 N m; POST: -25.2 ± 11.4 N m; RET: -29.4 ± 14.5 N m). There were no changes in the low-risk group (PRE: -12.2 ± 6.2 N m; POST: -12.2 ± 7.6 N m; RET: -12.9 ± 8.7 N m). CONCLUSION: Female soccer players with knee biomechanics that put them at high risk for anterior cruciate ligament injury had improved KAM following an NMT program. The changes in KAM remained at 6 months after training. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(10):689-698. Epub 28 Aug 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.14125.

articles.title: Large-Scale Evaluation of Performance and Biological Maturation in Post-PHV Youth Soccer Players: Sprinting, Jumping, Aerobic Fitness, and Functional Movement.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Anna Akbaş, Victoria Hadyk, Piotr Bryk et al.
articles.abstract: Akbaş, A, Hadyk, V, Bryk, P, Mazzei, S, Stanula, A, and Juras, G. Large-scale evaluation of performance and biological maturation in post-PHV youth soccer players: Sprinting, jumping, aerobic fitness, and functional movement. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to provide an integrated developmental profile of adolescent soccer players by examining how chronological age, biological maturation, and functional movement quality interact to shape sprint, jump, and aerobic fitness performance. A total of 246 male athletes (U15-U17) from 5 elite youth soccer academies completed sprint, jump, change-of-direction (COD), and aerobic tests alongside Functional Movement Screen (FMS) and Y-Balance Test (YBT) assessments. Maturity offset (years from peak height velocity, PHV) was used to estimate biological age, and group differences were analyzed using analysis of variance and analysis of covariance, with statistical significance set at p ≤ 0.05. Significant improvements with age were observed in sprinting, jumping, and aerobic fitness (p < 0.001); however, after controlling for PHV, differences in jumping and COD performance were no longer significant, whereas sprint performance and aerobic fitness remained age-dependent. Functional movement and balance showed small age-related differences that were largely explained by maturational variation. Weak and inconsistent correlations between FMS, YBT, and performance (|r| ≈ 0.20-0.35) suggested partial independence between movement quality and motor output. Notably, in older players, higher scores in mobility-related FMS components were associated with slower sprinting, a pattern that may reflect-rather than cause-reduced mechanical efficiency associated with greater flexibility. These findings indicate that post-PHV players are not a homogeneous group and support the use of maturity-informed, multidimensional athlete monitoring to guide individualized training even after PHV.

articles.title: Manuscript Clarification for: "Li H, Yang Q, Wang B. Effects of different training-intensity distribution models on maximal oxygen uptake and time-trial performance in endurance athletes: a Bayesian network meta-analysis. J Strength Cond Res 40: e755-e764, 2026.".
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Michael Rosenblat, Gunnar Treff, Stephen Seiler

articles.title: Lean Body Mass Accounts for the Sex Dimorphism of the Circulatory System and Aerobic Exercise Capacity in Humans.
articles.authors: Xinyu Liu, Meihan Guo, David Montero
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lean body mass (LBM) strongly associates with the capacity to deliver and consume oxygen in pilot studies performed in adults with low LBM. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to test whether LBM generally accounts for the phenotype of the circulatory system and hence its sex dimorphism in humans. METHODS: Healthy women and men (n = 294, 50% female) matched by age and physical activity throughout the adult lifespan (aged 18-78 years) were included. Body composition (dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry), hemoglobin mass/intravascular volumes (carbon monoxide rebreathing), cardiac structure/function/hemodynamics (ultrasound, continuous blood pressure), and aerobic exercise capacity (cycle ergometry, metabolic cart, power meter) were assessed in standardized conditions. Linear regression analyses assessed the relationship of LBM with study variables in each sex. Sex comparisons were performed in non-LBM-matched (n = 294) and LBM-matched (n = 70) individuals. RESULTS: Lean body mass linearly associated with the majority of hematological, hemodynamic, cardiac, and exercise capacity variables in women and men. The slopes of the regression lines did not differ between sexes, with women falling in the lower and men in the upper range of the overall relationship of LBM with these variables. Accordingly, in non-LBM-matched individuals, marked sex differences were observed in >90% of variables. In LBM-matched individuals, no cardiac-related variable (left ventricular structure and function, blood pressure, systemic vascular resistance, aerobic capacity) differed between women and men. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac structure and function, blood pressure, vascular resistance, and aerobic exercise capacity are statistically accounted for by LBM in humans, irrespective of sex. The sex dimorphism of the circulatory system strongly associates with the metabolically active mass, rather than sex.

articles.title: Joint-specific kinematic deviations in asymptomatic flatfoot using biplane fluoroscopy.
articles.authors: Andrew C Peterson, Tradd Rector, Elizabeth K Bowman et al.
articles.abstract: Asymptomatic flatfoot (AFF) is characterized by structural features of a medial arch collapse in the absence of pain, yet its dynamic biomechanical characteristics remain understudied. This study aimed to quantify and compare three-dimensional, multi-joint foot and ankle kinematics between individuals with AFF and healthy controls during walking and heel rise tasks using biplane fluoroscopy. Twenty-three participants (13 controls, 10 AFF) underwent weightbearing computed tomography to generate subject-specific bone models. Dynamic in vivo kinematics of the tibia, fibula, talus, and calcaneus were captured using biplane fluoroscopy during walking and heel rise. Joint kinematics for the tibiotalar, subtalar, tibiofibular, and talofibular joints were calculated using model-based tracking and analyzed using statistical parametric mapping. Range of motion (ROM) was also compared between groups. No significant differences in joint kinematics were observed between groups during walking. Walking ROM differences were observed only before FDR correction and were therefore interpreted as exploratory. During heel rise, AFF maintained a more everted subtalar position after SPM FDR correction and demonstrated reduced sagittal plane ROM at the tibiotalar and talofibular joint after ROM FDR correction. These findings indicate that significant group differences were detected during heel rise but not during walking within separate task specific analyses. These task dependent differences provide insight into biomechanical adaptations associated with AFF morphology, although longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these differences are related to future symptom development or deformity progression.

articles.title: An anatomically based functional upper cervical spinal unit tested under low quasi-static loading for use in an omnidirectional surrogate neck.
articles.authors: Sarah Romani, Paris Vakiel, Peter A Cripton
articles.abstract: Safety devices designed to prevent spinal cord and traumatic brain injuries are often evaluated using anthropometric test devices (ATDs). However, commonly used ATD necks lack biomechanical fidelity under multiplane loading, particularly during low-speed head impacts and axial loading. This study aimed to develop an anatomically-accurate upper cervical spine (UCS) surrogate that exhibits biofidelic kinematic responses under quasi-static flexion-extension, lateral bending, and axial torsion-a preliminary step toward a full neck surrogate capable of simulating complex multiplane loading. CT scans of a healthy 31-year-old male were used to generate vertebral geometry. Based on similarity to cadaveric ligament properties, woven cotton was selected as a ligament surrogate material. Anatomical landmarks were used to define ligament attachment points, and an adjustable attachment system enabled in-situ tensioning. The resulting UCS model was evaluated against post-mortem human subject data under quasi-static loading, assessing neutral zone (NZ), range of motion (ROM), repeatability, and helical axis of motion (HAM) using the CORA method. ROM and NZ values across all joints and degrees of freedom were within one standard deviation of literature values. The model demonstrated excellent repeatability (CORA:0.87-0.97), good biofidelity in flexion-extension (CORA:0.69-0.75; C0-C1 unloading:0.47), good-to-excellent in lateral bending (CORA:0.75-0.94), and fair-to-good in axial rotation (CORA:0.44-0.65). The mean HAM location aligned with cadaveric data in axial rotation and was slightly anterior during flexion-extension. Overall, the UCS model exhibited strong repeatability and biofidelity, supporting its potential as a preliminary component of a full cervical spine surrogate for future multiplane biomechanical research.

articles.title: Leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation during time trial exercise: Effects of acute hypobaric hypoxia and biological sex.
articles.authors: Anders Aagaard Hansen, Marcos Martin-Rincon, Bjarne Rud et al.
articles.abstract: Hypoxia reduces exercise performance, yet it remains unclear how biological sex and altitude influence substrate utilisation during prolonged maximal exercise. Twenty-two trained cyclists and triathletes (10 females) completed 30 min time trials (TTs) at low altitude (normoxia; ∼400 m) and moderate altitude (hypoxia; ∼2800 m in a hypobaric chamber) in counterbalanced order. Whole-body metabolism was estimated from indirect calorimetry, whereas leg glucose uptake and substrate utilisation were derived from arterial and femoral venous blood samples and leg blood flow (thermodilution). Muscle biopsies were obtained from vastus lateralis to measure glycogen utilisation. Across altitudes, females displayed a higher fractional utilisation of V ̇ O 2 max during the TTs. TT performance was decreased in hypoxia, and the proportional decrease was smaller in females (-14%) than in males (-18%). Whole-body substrate utilisation was similar between sexes in normoxia. However, males showed a large decrease in carbohydrate oxidation in hypoxia, whereas females displayed only a modest decrease. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia: estimated glycogen oxidation decreased, with no change in absolute fat or blood glucose oxidation. However, across altitudes, females showed greater carbohydrate contributions, originating primarily from blood glucose rather than muscle glycogen. Estimates of fat contribution were uncertain but suggested a lower contribution in females than in males. In conclusion, females exercised at a higher relative intensity and derived relatively more energy from blood glucose. Males and females had similar leg metabolic responses to hypoxia, with the lower power output and metabolic rate in hypoxic TTs primarily regulated by reduced estimated glycogen oxidation. KEY POINTS: Substrate utilisation during exercise is affected by altitude, sex, training status, food intake and relative intensity. Whether sex- and altitude-related differences in substrate utilisation persist during an ecologically valid maximal time trial in the fed state in trained males and females is unknown. Acute hypobaric hypoxia (∼2800 m) decreased 30 min time trial performance compared to normoxia (∼400 m) in both sexes, with a larger decrement in males. Females completed the time trials at a higher relative intensity than males in normoxia and hypoxia. Hypoxia reduced total metabolic rate primarily by decreasing estimated muscle glycogen oxidation, with no change in fat or blood glucose oxidation. The resulting changes in substrate partitioning were similar between sexes. Across altitudes, females derived relatively more energy from blood glucose despite similar muscle glycogen utilisation between sexes, whereas uncertain estimates suggested a lower contribution of fat in females than in males.

articles.title: The Respiratory Compensation Point Predicts 19.2-km Cycling Performance in Trained Male Cyclists.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Yuet L I So, Robin Faricier, Nasimi A Guluzade et al.
articles.abstract: So, YLI, Faricier, R, Guluzade, NA, Belfry, GR, Murias, JM, and Keir, DA. The respiratory compensation point predicts 19.2-km cycling performance in trained male cyclists. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study tested the hypothesis that the step-ramp-step (SRS)-corrected cycling power output (PO) at the respiratory compensation point (RCP) predicts cycling time-trial performance and explored the independent and collective contributions to trial time of 4 physiological variables derived from single or repeated SRS protocols: peak oxygen uptake (V̇o2peak), cycling economy, RCP, and fatigue resistance. Twenty-eight trained male cyclists completed an SRS protocol before and after a 19.2-km virtual time trial (∼30 minutes) on their personal road bikes using a smart trainer. V̇o2peak, cycling economy, and SRS-corrected PO at RCP were derived from the pre-time-trial SRS protocol. Fatigue resistance was quantified as the change in peak ramp PO from pre- to post-time trial. Independent and multilinear regression evaluated the predictive strength of each variable. Relative SRS-corrected RCP (W·kg-1) showed the strongest independent correlation with time-trial completion time (r = -0.61, p < 0.001). Relative V̇o2peak (mL·kg-1·min-1) and cycling economy (%) were also moderately associated with time-trial performance (r = -0.42, p = 0.03; and r = -0.55, p < 0.001, respectively), whereas fatigue resistance was not significantly correlated. In the multilinear regression analysis, SRS-corrected RCP uniquely explained 30.9% of the model's total predictive variance (r = 0.68, p < 0.01) followed by cycling economy (21.3%), ΔPOpeak (2.1%), and absolute V̇o2peak (3.3%). Among trained male cyclists, relative PO at SRS-corrected RCP is a strong and independent predictor of ∼30-minute time-trial performance. The SRS protocol provides a practical, single-session method to assess key physiological determinants of endurance performance, with valuable applications for training prescription and athlete monitoring.

articles.title: Cold fluid ingestion does not enhance exogenous carbohydrate oxidation during prolonged endurance exercise in the heat.
articles.authors: Loïs Mougin, Ben Will, Coen C W G Bongers et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the effects of ingesting cold versus warm carbohydrate beverages on exogenous carbohydrate oxidation and time-trial performance during prolonged cycling in the heat. Eleven trained, non heat-acclimated cyclists [21 ± 3 yr; 69.3 ± 8.3 kg; peak oxygen uptake ([Formula: see text]): 64.7 ± 5.0 mL/kg/min] completed two trials comprising 100 min of submaximal cycling at 50% Wpeak followed by a time trial in a hot environment (36.2 ± 0.3°C; 55 ± 3% relative humidity). Participants ingested a 15% dextrose solution enriched with [U-13C] glucose (60 g/h; bolus every 20 min) provided either cold (COLD; 4.0 ± 1.6°C) or at room temperature (WARM; 35.8 ± 0.5°C). Heart rate and rectal temperature were lower in COLD than in WARM during the 100-min exercise (P ≤ 0.006), whereas skin temperature did not differ between conditions. Average (40-100 min) exogenous carbohydrate oxidation (COLD: 0.50 ± 0.10 vs. WARM: 0.51 ± 0.10 g/min; P = 0.80), peak exogenous carbohydrate oxidation, total carbohydrate and fat oxidation, and blood glucose, lactate, and insulin concentrations did not differ between trials (all P ≥ 0.34). Sweat losses and body mass changes were unaffected by condition (P ≥ 0.40). Time-trial performance was not different between COLD and WARM (P = 0.38). Despite attenuating cardiovascular and thermal strain, ingesting a cold carbohydrate beverage during exercise in the heat did not enhance exogenous carbohydrate oxidation, substrate utilization, or performance compared with a warm beverage.NEW & NOTEWORTHY This study showed that, despite reducing cardiovascular and thermal strain, ingesting a cold (4°C) versus warm (36°C) carbohydrate beverage did not enhance exogenous carbohydrate oxidation, substrate utilization, or time-trial performance during prolonged cycling in the heat. These findings suggest that beverage temperature is not a relevant factor for optimizing carbohydrate availability during exercise under heat stress, and that athletes can select beverage temperature based on palatability and preference rather than for metabolic benefit.

articles.title: Effects of creatine supplementation on lean mass, muscle size and muscle performance during immobilisation and rehabilitation: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Jedd Pratt, Darren G Candow, Eric S Rawson et al.
articles.abstract: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) supplementation has established benefits in exercising populations; however, its efficacy during disuse and subsequent rehabilitation remains unclear. This systematic review assessed the effects of CrM supplementation on muscle size, lean mass and muscle performance (strength, power, endurance) during periods of disuse and rehabilitation. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to March 2026 following PRISMA guidelines. Six randomised placebo-controlled trials were included (n = 118, mean ages: 15-24 years, disuse model: 1-2 weeks limb-immobilisation). Two studies reported comparable reductions in quadriceps cross-sectional area (CSA; assessed via CT or NMR imaging) between CrM and placebo during disuse (-5.6% vs. -5.5%; -11.0% vs. -9.4%), whereas two reported smaller reductions from CrM supplementation in lower-limb lean mass (-5.6% vs. -8.9%) or preserved upper-limb lean mass (0.9% vs. -3.7%) (assessed via bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) or dual energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)). These contrasting findings may reflect limitations of BIA/DXA, including hydration effects, rather than preservation of muscle tissue. Effects on muscle performance were inconsistent, with favourable findings from CrM supplementation in upper- but not lower-limb models. Four studies included recovery, three of which used resistance-based rehabilitation. Two reported greater increases with CrM supplementation across quadriceps CSA (21.3% vs. 14.3%), lower-limb lean mass (5.6% vs. 3.8%), power (52.2% vs. 35.2%) and strength (28.7% vs. 22.8%). Current evidence does not unanimously support CrM supplementation as an effective countermeasure to mitigate disuse-induced muscle atrophy, lean mass loss or declines in muscle performance. Whether CrM supplementation meaningfully influences rehabilitation following disuse, particularly in older adults and clinical populations at greater risk of disuse atrophy and incomplete recovery, warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
articles.authors: Dimitrios I Bourdas, Eleftherios Mylonis, Natalia Kompodieta et al.
articles.abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

articles.title: Post-Exercise Thermal Interventions and Nocturnal Sleep in Athletes: A Narrative Review of the Potential Underlying Physiological Mechanisms.
articles.authors: Panagiotis G Miliotis, Shona L Halson, Toby Mundel et al.
articles.abstract: Sleep is essential for optimal performance and recovery in athletes. Post-exercise cold exposure, including cold water immersion and cryotherapy, is typically used to enhance recovery, but its effects on sleep remain unclear. Emerging evidence also suggests that post-exercise heat exposure, including sauna and hot water immersion before sleep may improve both objective and subjective sleep outcomes. However, the effectiveness of post-exercise thermal interventions for improving nocturnal sleep in athletes specifically has not yet been comprehensively evaluated. This narrative review synthesizes the current evidence and discusses the potential physiological mechanisms by which post-exercise thermal interventions may influence nocturnal sleep in athletes. Despite methodological heterogeneity, existing research indicates that post-exercise thermal interventions may influence the subsequent nocturnal sleep of athletes through multiple and varying interacting mechanisms. For example, cold exposure close to bedtime (< 2 h) may disrupt sleep by reducing the distal-to-proximal skin temperature gradient (DPG), thereby increasing sleep onset latency and shortening sleep duration. In contrast, when applied more than 2 h before bedtime, cold exposure may improve sleep by augmenting parasympathetic tone and/or reducing muscle soreness and associated nocturnal movement. Although it remains unclear whether post-exercise heat exposure improves sleep via autonomic modulation or reduced muscle soreness, existing evidence indicates that sleep may be facilitated by an increased DPG. Moderating factors such as sex, time of day, environmental temperature, bedding microclimate, acclimatization status, and training load may influence the effects of post-exercise thermal interventions on sleep and should be investigated in future studies.

articles.title: Characterising the Internal and External Load During Warm-Up, Match Play and Training in Soccer Substitutes: A Systematic Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Christopher Curtis, Mark Russell, Samuel P Hills et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Shorter match-play exposure for soccer substitutes relative to those who start matches has implications in the days before, during and following match play concerning their training, preparatory and recovery/compensatory practices. Specifically, characterising the internal and external loading of substitute players throughout a weekly microcycle can facilitate evidence-based recommendations aimed at optimising their performance readiness. OBJECTIVES: This systematic scoping review aimed to map and characterise the internal and external loading associated with warm-up, match play and training in soccer substitutes. METHODS: Prior to literature searches being conducted, a Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome, Study design (PICOS) statement was formed. Online database (PubMed, SPORTDiscus, Scopus and Web of Science) searches were performed according to PRISMA Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) protocols. Studies were eligible if internal or external characteristics of soccer substitutes were measured in training or match-play scenarios. After calibration exercises, two authors independently quality assessed each study, with Cohen's kappa undertaken to assess inter-rater agreement. A scoping review methodology was selected because of the methodological and conceptual heterogeneity across studies, which precluded meaningful meta-analysis. RESULTS: A total of 5135 studies were identified, 66 of which met study criteria. Substantive inter-rater agreement was observed (κ = 0.939, p < 0.001) during the quality assessment of included studies. Soccer substitutes' body temperature, and thus several aspects of physical performance, may not be maintained at time of pitch entry (body temperature pre-pitch entry ~ 37 °C vs match play > 38 °C). Substitutes may experience lower absolute physical loading during training and match day (e.g. match-day 'top up' activity: ~ 17 min; total distance: ~ 1700 m) but during match play, substitutes typically cover higher relative total distances (~ 109 to ~ 137 m·min-1), high-speed running (~ 9.8 to ~ 13.5 m·min-1) and sprinting distance (~ 3.8 to 5.0 m·min-1) compared with players who started the match. Substitutes playing in the second-half exhibit increased heart rates compared with full-match players (84% vs 81% maximum heart rate); however, this remains lower than the first-half heart rate responses of full-match players (84% vs 86% maximum heart rate). CONCLUSIONS: This systematic scoping review summarises current evidence and key findings relating to the internal and external characteristics of soccer substitutes during warm-up, match play and training that can be used in practice to inform player welfare and sport science support within these cohorts. Chiefly, during match-day warm-ups, soccer substitutes' body temperature and physical performance responses may not be maintained, despite typical substitute-specific match-day practices being employed. Similarly, soccer substitutes were frequently reported to demonstrate higher relative total distance, high-speed running and sprinting outputs compared with starting players. Further research is needed to better understand performance demands, longitudinal adaptations, contextual influences and female-specific responses in soccer substitutes.

articles.title: Platelet Mitochondrial Bioenergetics in Adolescents at Risk of MASLD Following High-Intensity Interval Training.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Jeny E Rivera, Emir Tas, Craig Porter et al.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent cardiometabolic disorder in adolescents with obesity associated with insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and increased cardiovascular disease risk. Platelets contribute to inflammatory and vascular processes implicated in cardiometabolic disease, yet little is known regarding platelet mitochondrial bioenergetics in adolescents at risk for MASLD or their response to exercise training. This study characterized platelet mitochondrial respiration in adolescents at risk of MASLD and examined the effects of four weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) according to MASLD status (n=10 MASLD; n=17 non-MASLD). MASLD was defined as intrahepatic triglyceride (IHTG) content ≥5% by magnetic resonance imaging.
