RESULTS: A strong association was observed between IAD and 0- to 10-m sprint time (r = .805, P < .001). No significant associations were observed between IAD and vertical jump performance or anthropometric variables (all P > .10), whereas 20-m sprint time demonstrated moderate associations with jump performance. No significant positional differences were identified for IAD; however, goalkeepers exhibited a nonsignificant tendency for faster 0- to 10-m times without corresponding differences in IAD. CONCLUSION: IAD represents a timing-derived performance metric of early acceleration structure. While derived from shared temporal components with sprint time, it provides additional insight into how acceleration is distributed during the initial phase of sprinting. Expression in normalized form may support athlete profiling and monitoring in applied environments where advanced biomechanical assessment is not feasible.

articles.title: Protein restriction amplifies nucleus accumbens dopamine responses to protein-rich food during operant feeding in male mice.
articles.authors: Hamid Taghipourbibalan, Stefan W Huijgens, K Linnea Volcko et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Animals strongly defend protein intake, but how protein status shapes moment-to-moment reward signalling in mesolimbic circuits remains unclear, particularly when the effort required to obtain food varies. OBJECTIVE: We tested whether dietary protein restriction altered nucleus accumbens (NAc) core dopamine signalling when mice worked for food of differing nutritional value in the home cage. METHODS: Under surgical anaesthesia, male C57BL/6 mice (n=12; ∼12 weeks old at diet initiation) were injected in the NAc core with a virus expressing the fluorescent dopamine sensor GRABDA and implanted with fibre-optic cannulas. In food-access tasks, nose pokes delivered either chow (protein-containing) or sucrose pellets. Across sessions, pellets required either one nose poke (FixedRatio1) or an increasing number (ProgRatio). Fibre photometry measured dopamine release for both pellet types and schedules during three dietary phases: non-restricted diet (NR1; 18% protein), protein-restricted diet (PR; 4%), and restored non-restricted diet (NR2), with 1 week of adaptation between phases. Behavioural and photometry data were analysed using repeated-measures ANOVA. RESULTS: Home-cage food intake remained stable, but bodyweight gain fell markedly during PR and partially recovered in NR2 (+10.1% NR1 vs. +1.2% PR vs. +6.0% NR2, p<.001). Nose poking increased during PR under both schedules, most robustly for chow pellets (188% and 261% increases under FixedRatio1 and ProgRatio, respectively; ps<.01). Neural effects were more selective. During FixedRatio1, pellet delivery evoked a larger NAc dopamine response to chow than sucrose specifically during PR (p=.001); no pellet-type difference occurred during NR1 or NR2 (ps>.05). During ProgRatio, dopamine responses at pellet delivery and retrieval did not differ between pellet types in any phase (all ps>.05). CONCLUSIONS: Protein restriction did not globally amplify reward-related behaviour or dopamine signalling. Instead, it selectively biased NAc dopamine according to the animal's nutritional status, nutrient context, and task demands.

articles.title: Generating standing posture finite element models of the spine with radiation-free imaging.
articles.authors: Federica Incatasciato, Peter P G Lafranca, Timothy Tin-Yan Lee et al.
articles.abstract: Finite element (FE) modelling is a powerful tool for investigating spinal biomechanics. Subject-specific finite element models of the spine are commonly built from supine data obtained from CT images, with harmful radiation and without soft-tissue structures. However, a more accurate evaluation of vertebrae and intervertebral disc loading requires the analysis of the subject in upright posture. In this study we propose a radiation-free alternative to create subject-specific standing FE models by combining supine MRI with ultrasound-based 3D spinal curvature assessment in standing posture. Subject-specific supine FE models of T3-L5 were created from synthetic CT (AI-generated from MRI) of 8 children. Dedicated spinal ultrasound was used to detect the positions of the vertebral laminae, which were used as input to convert the FE model from supine to standing. RMSE was found within 1 mm for the fitted vertebral levels. Validation against conventional radiographic measurements showed no statistical difference in sagittal alignment between the two imaging modalities in the lumbar and mid-to-lower thoracic parameters. In addition, the distance between the vertebral centroids measured from radiographs and from the upright FE model in sagittal and coronal plane was found to be less than 6 mm for the fitted levels. In conclusion, we demonstrate the feasibility of using completely radiation-free imaging as an alternative to CT and bi-planar X-ray to build subject-specific, upright, detailed FE models.

articles.title: Dietary threonine requirement of healthy older adults >60y stratified by age and sex in a repeated measures design1.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Alyssa Paoletti, Wala Naeem, Paul B Pencharz et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current dietary guidelines for most of the world recommend increased plant protein consumption to improve health and support environmental sustainability. Threonine is an indispensable AA required for protein and mucin synthesis which is present in low concentrations in plant proteins. Threonine requirement is needed to guide dietary planning and assessment of protein adequacy particularly in those consuming predominantly plant-based protein diets. However, no data exist on dietary threonine requirement in older adults. OBJECTIVES: 1) Determine the threonine requirement in older adults using the indicator amino acid oxidation (IAAO) method in a repeated measures design. 2) compare the derived estimates based on age: 60-69y and 70-79y and sex. METHODS: The threonine requirement was determined using the IAAO method with L-[1-13C] phenylalanine as the indicator. Twenty-two older adults >60 y (n = 10 males and n = 12 females) were randomly assigned to receive up to 7 threonine intakes (5 to 35 mg/kg/d). The mean threonine requirement was determined from oxidation of L-[1-13C] phenylalanine (F13CO2) using a two-phase linear mixed effect model. The 95% CI was calculated using parametric bootstrap. The overlap of the 95% CI between the 2 age groups were used to compare the requirement estimates. The null hypothesis was accepted if the interval contained zero. RESULTS: There was no effect of sex on the threonine requirement. However, the threonine requirement for adults 60-69y and 70-79y were 11 mg/kg/d (R2m = 0.10, R2c = 0.81; 7.70, 14.30 mg/kg/d) and 17.9 mg/kg/d (R2m = 0.44, R2c = 0.64; 13.23, 22.57 mg/kg/d) respectively with those 70-79y having a higher requirement than those 60-69y ( -1.18, -12.62). CONCLUSIONS: The result of the current study demonstrates that AA needs among older adults change within decades of age. This should be integrated into future AA recommendations for accurate planning and assessment of protein nutrition in the elderly. The trial was registered at Clinical Trials Registry: # NCT02008955, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06225648.

articles.title: Can Graded Blood Flow Restriction Pressure Enhance and Prolong Postactivation Performance Enhancement Induced by Plyometric Jumps?
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Liang Wang, Chengyu Ke, Olivier Girard et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study investigated whether adding blood flow restriction at graded arterial occlusion pressures (AOPs) during plyometric jumps can enhance and prolong postactivation performance enhancement. METHODS: Twenty-one resistance-trained men completed 40 maximal plyometric jumps under 4 conditions: jumps alone or combined with blood flow restriction at 50%, 60%, or 70% AOP. Countermovement jump (CMJ) and squat jump (SJ) height were assessed at baseline and at 15 seconds, 4, 8, and 12 minutes postexercise. RESULTS: Significant condition × time interactions were observed for both CMJ height (P = .01, ηp2=.13) and SJ height (P < .001, ηp2=.14). The 70% AOP condition produced significant performance improvements across all time points (P < .01, g = 0.36-0.53). At 50% and 60% AOP, performance improved at 15 seconds and 4 minutes (P < .01, g = 0.19-0.40), with CMJ effects persisting to 8 minutes but disappearing by 12 minutes in both jumps. The control condition showed a transient CMJ improvement at 15 seconds (P = .046, g = 0.20) but no SJ change. Compared with other conditions, 70% AOP outperformed control at 4 and 12 minutes for CMJ and at 12 minutes for SJ, and exceeded 50% AOP at 15 seconds in both tests. CONCLUSION: Plyometric jumps combined with 70% AOP produced a greater and more sustained postactivation performance enhancement response than jumps alone, suggesting that blood flow restriction may serve as a potential adjunct to enhance the acute effects of plyometric conditioning activities.

articles.title: How Fast Is Thin Air? Empirical Altitude Adjustments for Indoor Track-and-Field Performance.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Atle G Guttormsen, Simen Guttormsen
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: In this study, we analyze the effects of altitude on athletic performance for running events and speed-dependent jumping events at indoor meets, and we evaluate whether the NCAA's altitude adjustment process is accurate. METHODS: We analyzed 688,625 running results and 215,933 jumping results from NCAA indoor competitions at 382 different indoor venues. We estimated altitude effects using athlete × season fixed effects. For running events 200 m and longer, we included a banked-track indicator to separate altitude from the mechanical advantage of a banked oval. RESULTS: Altitude improved sprint times by 0.3% to 0.5%/1000 m and jumping marks by 0.5% to 0.7%/1000 m. Pole vault improvements (0.66%-0.69%/1000 m) matched the quadratic speed-to-height prediction (h ∝ v2). For distance events, the altitude penalty (added time) rose from 0.5% to 0.9%/1000 m at 800 m to 2.7% to 3.0%/1000 m at 5000 m; the drag-oxygen crossover lay between 400 m and 800 m. The women's 800 m was penalized approximately twice as severely as the men's (0.92 vs 0.50%/1000 m). NCAA sprint corrections accounted for only 42% to 71% of the observed effects. CONCLUSIONS: NCAA sprint corrections under-correct sharply once track banking is accounted for; the 800 m requires sex-specific adjustments; and the absence of any field-event correction is a clear gap in the existing system.

articles.title: Baseline Testosterone Stratification Reveals Divergent Hormonal Adaptations in Men and Women Undergoing Basic Combat Training.
articles.authors: Nicole M Sekel, Brittany Bozzini, Katelyn Guerriere Aaron et al.
articles.abstract: This study examined whether hormonal and body composition responses to 10-weeks of U.S. Army Basic Combat Training (BCT) differ by baseline testosterone and sex. Methods: Male (n=97) and female (n=105) trainees were stratified at baseline as having LOW (men <10.4 nmol/L; women <0.82 nmol/L) or NORMAL baseline testosterone. We measured serum total and free testosterone, sex hormone binding globulin (SHBG), luteinizing hormone (LH) and estradiol (E2) at weeks 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 9 and cortisol weekly; dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) assessed body composition at week 0 and 9. Linear mixed models tested time and group effects; generalized linear models related baseline testosterone status and testosterone area under the curve with changes in body composition. Results: In LOW women, testosterone increased at each timepoint (all p<0.01), reaching concentrations 53% higher at week 9 compared to week 0 (30.2± 7.8 vs 19.7± 3.2 ng/dl). In men, testosterone increased (LOW: +76%; NORMAL: +23%) across BCT (all p<0.05), except at week 2. Among LOW men, concentrations stabilized by week 4 (344.8± 81.4 ng/dl) and remained normal. Cortisol was highest at baseline and declined in all men and in NORMAL women. LH and E2 remained stable in both sexes, while SHBG declined only in women, independent of baseline testosterone. Neither baseline testosterone nor cumulative exposure were associated with changes in lean or fat mass. Conclusions: SHBG and cortisol trajectories differed by sex and baseline testosterone status. Testosterone changes were sex specific, reflecting an anabolic training environment in men and modest increased androgen availability in LOW women.

articles.title: Associations between countermovement jump impulse and running kinetics following ACL reconstruction.
articles.authors: Sami Ghani, Eve-Merina Lucron, Long Yiu Chan et al.
articles.abstract: Persistent deficits in lower-limb loading are commonly observed following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence running biomechanics. Countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse can provide a phase-specific measure of force-time characteristics to reflect limb loading capacity; however, its relationship with running kinetics remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify phase-specific CMJ impulse following ACLR and examine associations with vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) metrics during treadmill running at the return-to-running phase. Forty-two participants performed three unilateral and bilateral CMJs on dual force plates and ran at 8 km/hr on an instrumented treadmill. Concentric, eccentric braking, and landing impulses were calculated. Running variables included weight acceptance rate, weight acceptance peak force, and maximum applied force. Inter-limb differences were assessed using Wilcoxon/paired t-tests. Impulse-vGRF relationships were analysed using Pearson/Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression. The ACLR limb exhibited significant deficits across all unilateral and bilateral CMJ phases, except for unilateral landing impulse. Deficits were greatest for unilateral concentric impulse (Δ1.3Ns·kg-0.67, d = 1.49, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force limb symmetry index (LSI) was explained by unilateral concentric impulse LSI (adjusted R2 = 0.25, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric impulse (adjusted R2 = 0.38, p < 0.001). Weight acceptance peak force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric and landing impulses (adjusted R2 = 0.37, p < 0.001). No meaningful relationships were observed for eccentric impulses or weight acceptance rate metrics. These findings indicate that jump impulse testing may provide clinically relevant indicators of running kinetics.

articles.title: 3D development of the mouse pelvic girdle: Insights into the musculoskeletal system and vasculature.
articles.authors: Serena C Fernandopulle, Mark A Wright, Nina St Hillaire et al.
articles.abstract: The mouse (Mus musculus) pelvis features an elongated ilium and triangular pubis and ischium characteristic of a small quadruped, whereas humans possess a short, broad, bowl-shaped pelvis specialized for bipedal locomotion and childbirth. Mice are widely used to model osteoporosis, hip dysplasia, and other pelvic pathologies, yet in utero mouse pelvic development has been incompletely characterized, limiting cross-species interpretation. Here, we integrate 3D micro-CT and histology to generate a comprehensive atlas of mouse pelvic development from embryonic days 12.5-18.5 (E12.5-E18.5), focusing on the ilium, hip joint, and sacroiliac joint. We show that E14.5 is a critical stage, when the hip and sacroiliac joints form. We identify a sequential developmental program in mice in which joint cartilage forms first, followed by muscle-cartilage interaction, and, subsequently, extensive blood vessel growth. In contrast to the transversely oriented, developmentally delayed iliac growth and ossification described in recent studies of the human bipedal pelvis, the mouse ilium follows an earlier, centrally initiated, longitudinal ossification pattern. Overall, our atlas provides an essential quadrupedal reference for interpreting human pelvic development, evolution, and disease models.

articles.title: Acute Sodium Bicarbonate Supplementation Enhances 10-km Outdoor Track Running Performance in Recreational Female Runners.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Selin Aktitiz, Yasemin Güzel, Muhammed Mustafa Atakan et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated the effects of acute sodium bicarbonate (SB) supplementation co-ingested with a carbohydrate-rich meal on 10-km running performance and gastrointestinal symptoms in recreational female runners under field-based conditions. Twenty-one healthy women (33.6 ± 4.6 years; body mass index 20.8 ± 1.3 kg/m; maximal oxygen uptake 48.6 ± 2.0 ml·kg-1·min-1) completed two 10-km outdoor track running time trials (TTs) in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Participants ingested either SB (0.3 g/kg body mass [BM]) or placebo (PLA; 0.03 g/kg BM table salt), together with a standardized carbohydrate-rich meal (1.5 g/kg BM), 90 min before exercise during the same phase of the menstrual cycle. Blood pH, bicarbonate [HCO3-], and [lactate] were measured before, and 1, 3, 5, and 7 min after the TTs; performance time was recorded. Gastrointestinal symptoms were recorded at 30, 60, and 90 min after SB and PLA ingestions. Blood pH (7.47 ± 0.03 vs. 7.42 ± 0.04, p < .001) and [HCO3-] (27.7 ± 1.4 vs. 22.2 ± 1.5 mmol/L, p < .001) were higher at rest and remained elevated postexercise following SB compared with PLA (p < .05 for all time points). TT completion time improved after SB compared with PLA (3,046.1 ± 208.7 s vs. 3,078.4 ± 206.8 s; p = .011). No significant differences in gastrointestinal symptoms scores were observed between conditions (p > .05 for all). In conclusion, acute co-ingestion of 0.3 g/kg of SB with a carbohydrate-rich meal is a practical and well-tolerated strategy to achieve higher resting blood [HCO3-] and pH as well as to improve 10-km TT running performance in recreational female runners.

articles.title: Baseline Food Supply-Based Dietary Scores and Ischemic Heart Disease Mortality: A Longitudinal Cross-Country Study.
articles.authors: Saya Nosaka, Fumiya Kawase, Tomoko Imai et al.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: National food environments may be associated with cardiovascular risk, but how their association with country-level ischemic heart disease (IHD) mortality differs across diet-quality indices remains unclear. We compared six food supply-based dietary scores calculated using 2010 food data in relation to annual IHD mortality from 2010 to 2021. Methods: We conducted a longitudinal study of 148 countries with populations ≥ 1 million. Using 2010 FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheet data, we calculated the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score, the Alternative Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS), Traditional Japanese Diet Score (TJDS), Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI), and Quantitative Index for Dietary Diversity (QUANTIDD). The outcome was age-standardized IHD mortality during 2010-2021. Associations between time-invariant baseline dietary scores and annual IHD mortality were assessed using multivariable-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Effect sizes were expressed as mortality rate ratios (MRRs) per 1-standard deviation (SD) higher score; model fit was compared using Akaike information criterion (AIC) weights and marginal R2, and effect estimates were compared pairwise. Results: Higher DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality. MRRs per 1-SD higher score were 0.914 (95% confidence interval, 0.849-0.983) for DASH and 0.908 (95% confidence interval, 0.838-0.985) for AHEI. No significant associations were observed for MDS, TJDS, PHDI, or QUANTIDD. DASH had the highest AIC weight (0.434), followed by AHEI (0.341), with a slightly higher marginal R2 for DASH. Pairwise comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in effect estimates between DASH and AHEI or between either of these scores and the other dietary scores. Conclusions: Higher baseline DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality during 2010-2021, with similar effect estimates per 1-SD higher score and broadly comparable model fit. However, direct pairwise comparisons revealed no statistically significant differences in standardized effect sizes between these scores (DASH and AHEI) and the other dietary scores. These findings suggest that the relevance of dietary scores may depend on the outcome and analytic context rather than the superiority of a single index. Because this was an ecological study, these findings should not be interpreted as individual-level causal effects.

articles.title: Animal-source foods in infancy contribute to higher dietary quality.
articles.authors: Saralyn F Foster, Deborah Jacobvitz, Marcela R Abrego et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Few studies have characterized infant animal-source food introduction and intake longitudinally to determine whether these foods are associated with dietary quality or growth at 12-months of age. OBJECTIVE: Describe patterns and determinants of animal-source food consumption during complementary feeding and evaluate associations between animal-source foods with dietary quality and growth. METHODS: Mothers And careGivers Investing in Children (MAGIC) randomized trial is a complementary feeding intervention with responsive feeding coaching (MAGIC-FEED) compared to an attention control (MAGIC-SAFE), and an exploratory arm (MAGIC-FEED+FOOD) including food provision along with MAGIC-FEED. 135 mother-infant-caregiver triads in the Austin, Texas, United States enrolled at age 5-months, received virtual intervention visits at age 6, 7, 8 and 10 months, and had anthropometrics measured at 12-months. Diet was assessed repeatedly from 5-12-months with a 7-day food-frequency questionnaire and 24-hour diet recall from which infant dietary quality index (IDQI, range 0-1) was calculated. Descriptive statistics and covariate adjusted linear regression evaluated patterns of intake and associations between intervention arm or dietary components with dietary quality and growth. RESULTS: Overall, animal-source food intake increased from age 6 through 12 months. At age 12-months, more infants consumed egg (72%), poultry (77%) and beef (68%) and less consumed fish (30%) and pork (25%) in the prior 7-days. MAGIC-FEED was not associated with IDQI and had limited effects on animal source food consumption. In covariate-adjusted models, poultry (β=0.12, 95%CI 0.04,0.19) egg (β=0.06, 95%CI 0.01,0.12) and beef (β=0.07, 95%CI 0.01,0.13) predicted higher IDQI across infancy, compared to non-consumers. at 12-months of age. Poultry consumers predicted higher IDQI (β=0.14, 95%CI: 0.05,0.23), and pork consumers had higher length-for-age Z-scores (β=0.48, 95%CI: 0.03,0.92) at age 12-months. CONCLUSIONS: MAGIC-FEED was not associated with animal source food intake. Poultry, beef, and eggs as complementary foods were associated with higher dietary quality, and pork was associated with linear growth. Clinical Trial Registry number and website where it was obtained NCT04177472; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04177472.

articles.title: Dietary fibre intake and suicide in Japanese adults: the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Akiko Nanri, Tetsuya Mizoue, Atsushi Goto et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary fibre intake has been reported to be inversely associated with depression in a meta-analysis. However, most studies were cross-sectional, and none examined the association with suicide, a severe outcome of depression. We investigated the association of dietary fibre intake with suicide risk among Japanese adults. Participants were 40 630 men and 48 178 women aged 44-76 years who responded to the second survey (baseline of the present study) of the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (1995-1998). Dietary fibre intake was assessed using a validated FFQ. Hazard ratios of suicide through December 2018 were estimated using Cox proportional hazard regression analysis. During a mean follow-up of 18·7 years, we identified 459 deaths from suicide. Dietary fibre intake was associated with lower suicide risk after adjustment for covariates, including intakes of vitamin B12, vitamin D, Ca, Zn and n-3 PUFA. The multivariable-adjusted hazard ratio for suicide of the highest v. lowest quartile of total dietary fibre intake was 0·65 (95 % CI 0·46-0·93). Similar inverse associations were observed for vegetable and fruit fibre intake but not cereal or bean fibre. However, these associations were substantially attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for nutrients highly correlated with dietary fibre intake, including folate, vitamin B6, Mg and Fe; the corresponding value for total dietary fibre intake was 0·85 (95 % CI 0·55-1·31). Our findings suggest that greater consumption of foods rich in dietary fibre and related nutrients, rather than dietary fibre per se, may play a protective role against suicide.

articles.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Markers of Healthy Aging: A Systematic Review of Biological and Functional Outcomes.
articles.authors: Mirko Marino, Cristian Del Bo', Martina Frigerio et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Aging involves molecular, cellular, and functional changes that increase vulnerability to chronic disease, cognitive decline, frailty, and loss of independence. Mediterranean-style dietary patterns are generally rich in plant foods, unsaturated fats, fiber, and bioactive compounds, but their composition varies across studies and may include modified or multicomponent interventions. OBJECTIVE: This Systematic Review evaluated associations between Mediterranean-style dietary adherence and related interventions and markers of healthy aging, including biological aging biomarkers, cognition, frailty, physical performance, and overall health status. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published during 2013- 2025. Searches were conducted in April 2025 and updated in August 2025. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251107773). DATA EXTRACTION: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies in adults were eligible if they assessed Mediterranean-style dietary patterns or interventions and reported aging-related biomarkers or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently conducted study selection and data extraction. DATA ANALYSIS: Eleven studies were included: 5 RCTs, 4 prospective cohort studies, and 2 cross-sectional studies. Greater adherence was associated with better cognitive performance and slower memory decline in some studies. Favorable findings were also reported for telomere dynamics, epigenetic age, and inflammatory biomarkers. Improvements in frailty and physical performance were mainly observed in interventions combining dietary modification with physical activity. Heterogeneity in dietary definitions, adherence measures, intervention components, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The evidence suggests that favorable associations exist between Mediterranean-style dietary patterns and selected markers of healthy aging but does not establish uniform or causal effects. Interpretation is limited by methodological heterogeneity, self-reported dietary exposure, and the inclusion of modified or multicomponent interventions. Long-term studies using standardized dietary definitions, harmonized outcomes, objective adherence measures, and designs capable of isolating diet-specific effects are needed. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251107773].

articles.title: Exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme environments and space analogues: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Gustavo S O Lima, Kaline V F Dinis, Leonardo P Silva et al.
articles.abstract: This scoping review synthesized evidence on physical activity/exercise and physiological monitoring in isolated, confined and extreme (ICE) environments, with emphasis on Antarctic missions and space analogues. ICE exposures combine cold stress, confinement, disrupted light-dark cycles and psychosocial strain, which can challenge musculoskeletal integrity, cardiovascular regulation, sleep/circadian function and cognition. Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched Web of Science, Embase, Scopus and PubMed/Medline, complemented by grey literature and AI-assisted citation chasing. Eligible reports included human studies in ICE/analogue settings that implemented or quantified physical activity/exercise and/or physiological monitoring. Seventeen studies published between 2003 and 2025 met inclusion criteria and were mapped across ICE characteristics, exercise protocols, monitoring technologies, outcomes and research gaps. Exercise was reported as a potential countermeasure to attenuate selected aspects of deconditioning and support sleep and psychophysiological adaptation, particularly in bed rest and simulated confinement studies. Antarctic field studies more often characterized spontaneous physical activity, sleep/activity rhythms and field-adapted monitoring. Assessment strategies varied, ranging from self-reported logs and actigraphy in operational field settings to laboratory-grade measures in bed rest and simulated confinement studies. Overall, exercise emerged as a pragmatic, domain-specific countermeasure against deconditioning in ICE settings, with effectiveness varying by modality and physiological target. However, heterogeneity in exposure characterization, exercise dose and monitoring methods, despite feasible wearable-based capture of behavioural and physiological signals, limited comparability and mechanistic inference. Future ICE research should prioritize harmonized reporting, standardized monitoring and longitudinal designs linking exercise exposure to physiological, behavioural and operational outcomes.

articles.title: Anatomical and histological characterization of the heart of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber).
articles.authors: Beatriz Rosa Silva, Maria Gabriela Aparecida Farias Pereira, Max Alex Santos Ferreira et al.
articles.abstract: Detailed information on the cardiac morphology of the scarlet ibis (Eudocimus ruber) remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the gross and microscopic anatomy of this species' heart and provide morphometric data. We examined six specimens (three males and three females) using gross anatomical analysis, morphometry, conventional radiography, three-dimensional scanning, light microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy. The mean heart mass was 5.93 ± 1.49 g (n = 6), corresponding to 1.10 ± 0.23% of body mass, and the mean radiographic cardiothoracic ratio was 66.90 ± 5.78% (n = 3). Macroscopic examination identified three venae cavae: the right and left cranial venae cavae and the caudal vena cava. The left atrioventricular valve had two cusps with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, whereas the right atrioventricular valve had a single muscular fold. Histological examination identified uninucleated and binucleated Purkinje fibers in the subendocardial region, extending into myocardial muscle bundles. The base of the aorta showed hyaline cartilage containing chondrocytes and chondroblasts, with no bone tissue identified in the examined sections. These findings provide anatomical, morphometric, and histological data on the heart of E. ruber and a basis for future comparative studies of avian cardiac morphology.

articles.title: Feedforward neuromuscular control and dynamic postural stability in people with chronic ankle instability during single-leg landing.
articles.authors: Tsz Yin Li, Zhuoran Wang, Reece Cascoe et al.
articles.abstract: Individuals with chronic ankle instability(CAI) show deficits in neuromuscular control and postural stability. While feedback mechanisms are well-studied, feedforward mechanisms during dynamic tasks remains underexplored. This study compared feedforward neuromuscular control and dynamic postural stability among CAI, coper and healthy groups. Fifteen CAI(23.5 ± 2.9 years, 11 M/4F), fifteen coper(24.1 ± 3.4 years, 12 M/3F) and fifteen healthy participants(25.5 ± 3.5 years, 11 M/4F) performed single-leg drop landings from 30 cm. Total centre of pressure movement during 1-second and 3-second(TOTEX1s&TOTEX3s), mediolateral sway distance(DML), peak vertical GRF(peak vGRF) and root-mean-square of mediolateral GRF in the first 0.4 s(RMS_ML_0.4) were recorded via force plate. Surface electromyography recorded muscle activity 200 ms before landing among tibialis anterior(TA), peroneus longus(PL) and gastrocnemius lateralis(GL). Pre-activation timing was calculated using the Teager-Kaiser energy operator(TKEO). Statistical analysis involved one-way ANOVA(α = 0.05) and Tukey post-hoc testing. Compared to healthy participants, CAI individuals displayed earlier TA(270 ± 73 ms vs. 85 ± 53 ms, p < 0.001) and PL(260 ± 87 ms vs. 102 ± 62 ms, p < 0.001) pre-activations, alongside higher TA activity(76 ± 27% vs. 35 ± 19%, p < 0.001) but lower PL activity(38 ± 14% vs. 77 ± 23%, p < 0.001). Higher RMS_ML_0.4(6.7 ± 1.3%BW vs. 5.6 ± 1.0%BW, p = 0.037), DML(55.6 ± 15.7 mm vs. 39.5 ± 9.0 mm, p < 0.001) and peak vGRF(334 ± 44%BW vs. 286 ± 59%BW, p = 0.041)were observed as well. Coper showed earlier GL pre-activation(169 ± 57 ms vs. 108 ± 67 ms, p = 0.021), increased activity(155 ± 40% vs. 97 ± 29%, p < 0.001) and decreased DML(42.7 ± 7.0 mm vs. 55.6 ± 15.7 mm, p = 0.008) compared to CAI individuals. CAI exhibited postural control deficits and ineffective feedforward control, shown by lower PL activity despite early pre-activation. Rate of force production training is advised. Increased GL activation may serve as a compensatory response in copers after initial ankle sprain.

articles.title: Menu Evaluation Tools in Food Services: An Integrative Review.
articles.authors: Lívia Bacharini Lima, Emanuele Batistela Dos Santos, Raquel Braz Assunção Botelho et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: The growing demand for meals outside the home has boosted the food service sector, but there are constant concerns regarding the nutritional quality of the meals offered. In this scenario, menus play a strategic role in promoting health and in defining population dietary patterns. OBJECTIVE: This integrative review aimed to identify the instruments used to evaluate menus in food service settings across different contexts and target audiences. DATA SOURCES: This is an integrative review with a systematic search in the LILACS, Scopus, PubMed, and Web of Science databases, with controlled and uncontrolled descriptors. Original studies published between 2003 and 2025 that described the development of menu evaluation instruments aimed at healthy food service were included. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted on the characteristics of the instruments, including target population, food service setting, scope, evaluation approach, assessment perspectives, number of items, country of development, and validation status. DATA ANALYSIS: Data were summarized using descriptive statistics, including absolute and relative frequencies. A total of 29 studies were included, with a predominance of instruments aimed at children's menus (55.2%) and with a qualitative approach (72.4%). Brazil had the largest number of developed instruments, followed by Spain, the United States, and Portugal. Only 58.6% of the instruments presented some type of validation. The instruments varied in scope (menu or menu + context), evaluation method (qualitative, quantitative, or qualitative-quantitative), and the number of perspectives covered, with 10.3% multidimensional (ie, having 4 or more dimensions). CONCLUSION: The review showed advances in evaluating menus for the child population and in incorporating sustainability as an analytical parameter. However, gaps remain in validation and the development of multidimensional instruments, underscoring the need for validated and adapted tools to promote healthier, more sustainable menus.

articles.title: Physical activity partly inhibits autonomic imbalance, immune dysfunction and quality of life induced by chronic shiftwork in policemen.
articles.authors: Hélida C Aquino-Santos, Jeanne S Tavares-Vasconcelos, Anamei Silva-Reis et al.
articles.abstract: Chronic shiftwork can impair autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune homeostasis. However, the interaction between occupational status and physical activity level in military police officers remains incompletely understood. This cross-sectional factorial study included 102 men stratified according to occupational status and physical activity level: physically active military police officers (PMP; n = 26), physically inactive military police officers (PMNP; n = 26), physically active civilians (CVP; n = 25) and physically inactive civilians (CVNP; n = 25). Quality of life, perceived stress, sleepiness, haematological parameters, cytokines and heart rate variability were assessed. Physical activity improved several Short-form questionnaire (SF-36) domains, particularly Physical Functioning and General Health. Military police officers demonstrated lower mean normal-to-normal intervals and lower high-frequency power than civilians, indicating differences in resting autonomic cardiovascular modulation associated with occupational status. Serum interleukin-10 concentrations were significantly lower in military police officers, whereas interleukin-2, interleukin-17 and interferon-γ did not differ significantly according to occupational status. Haemoglobin levels and platelet counts demonstrated significant occupational status × physical activity interactions. Perceived stress scores were lower in military police officers than in civilians. Chronic occupational exposure to shiftwork was associated with altered autonomic cardiovascular regulation and immune regulation in military police officers. Regular physical activity improved quality of life somewhat; however, several physiological alterations remained predominantly associated with occupational status, reinforcing the importance of occupational strategies targeting circadian health and physiological resilience. These findings highlight the physiological complexity of chronic shiftwork exposure in tactical occupational populations.

articles.title: Validation of the GERY Protein Intake Screening Test among community-dwelling oldest-olds in Finland.
articles.authors: Riikka T Niskanen, Aava Ranta, Heli Salmenius-Suominen et al.
articles.abstract: Protein intake is often suboptimal among older adults, which may lead to protein-energy malnutrition, sarcopenia and frailty. A need exists for a simple, efficient and feasible protein-specific dietary assessment tool. Thus, a novel protein screening test, adapted to the Finnish cultural context, was developed. The aim of this study was to validate a novel protein screening test against a 1-d food record among Finnish older adults. Data were collected as part of the Helsinki Aging Study. The sample (N 140) consisted of Finnish community-dwelling oldest-old individuals (age range 80-100 years) with sufficient cognitive ability for at-home dietary assessment. A 1-d food record and the protein screening test were completed on one habitual eating day. Validity was assessed using the food record as a reference, with suboptimal protein intake defined as <1·2 g/kg BW/d. A Bland-Altman plot and concordance correlation coefficient (0·87, 95 % CI: 0·83-0·91) demonstrated good agreement between the methods. Sensitivity (0·85, 95 % CI: 0·72-0·94), specificity (0·81, 95 % CI: 0·71-0·88), area under receiver operating characteristic curve (0·90, 95 % CI: 0·85-0·95) and positive likelihood ratio (4·40, 95 % CI: 2·86-6·77) indicated strong diagnostic performance of the protein screening test. An optimal cut-off for the screening test to identify suboptimal protein intake was assessed at <1·00 g/kg BW/d. The novel protein screening test has good concurrent validity with the food record in identifying Finnish community-dwelling oldest-olds with suboptimal protein intake. It shows diagnostic potential for identifying individuals with suboptimal intake and to engage in targeted intervention.

articles.title: Dietary Inflammatory Index and cardiorespiratory fitness among older adults living in the community: a cross-sectional analysis.
articles.authors: Bi-Xia Huang, Zi-Hui Huang, Si Chen et al.
articles.abstract: The optimal dietary recommendation for healthy ageing remains unclear. This study examined the association between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) and cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) in Chinese community-dwelling older adults. Data were drawn from the Guangzhou Nutrition and Health Study's 3rd and 4th follow-up visits (2017-2021). DII was calculated from a Seventy nine-item validated FFQ, and CRF was assessed on a cycle ergometer using a submaximal constant work rate protocol. VO2max was estimated via the Åstrand-Ryhming Nomogram with age correction, and relative intensity was expressed as percentage of predicted maximal heart rate (%HRmax). Favourable CRF was defined as sex-specific VO2max in the top quartile or %HRmax < 85 %. Among 906 participants (615 women, 291 men; mean age 65·9 ± 5·4 years), those in the lowest DII tertile (anti-inflammatory diet) had higher VO2max than those in the highest tertile (P-trend = 0·048) and greater odds of favourable CRF (OR 1·81, 95 % CI 1·22-2·70), while no significant associations were observed for %HRmax (P-trend = 0·356; OR 1·31, 95 % CI 0·94-1·84). Associations between lower DII and higher VO2max were stronger among physically active participants (P-interaction = 0·049). Compared with consistently high DII, both transition to a low-inflammatory diet (OR 3·01, 95 % CI 1·20-7·51) and persistent adherence to such a diet (OR 2·49, 95 % CI 1·28-4·87) were associated with favourable CRF. These findings suggest that an anti-inflammatory diet is associated with better CRF in older adults, with potential synergistic benefits from physical activity.Trial registration: This trial was registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT03179657.

articles.title: High-intensity interval training modulates the SIRT1-P16 pathway, inflammatory markers, and oxidative stress in the liver of D-galactose-treated male rats.
articles.authors: Beydolah Shahouzehi, Homa Jafari, Farzaneh Rostamzadeh
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Aging contributes to progressive hepatic dysfunction, characterized by increased oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and mitochondrial impairment, which collectively exacerbate metabolic decline. This study examined the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on the SIRT1-P16 axis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory markers in a D-galactose (D-gal )-induced aging model in male Wistar rats. METHODS: Twenty-eight rats were assigned to four groups: Control (CTL), HIIT, D-gal, and D-gal+HIIT. Aging model was induced via daily subcutaneous injections of D-galactose (150 mg/kg) for eight weeks, while HIIT was performed on a treadmill five times per week over the same period. Gene expression and protein levels were measured by Real-time PCR and Western blot, respectively. Antioxidant and oxidant, and inflammatory markers were determined via colorimetric and ELISA methods. RESULTS: Gene expression analysis showed that D-gal significantly downregulated the expression of AMPK, SIRT1, and PGC-1α, whereas HIIT was associated with increased expression of these markers. Western blot analysis confirmed a reduction and elevation in SIRT1 and P16 protein, respectively, in the D-gal group, which were reversed following HIIT. HIIT also ameliorated the increase in the levels of malondialdehyde, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α and the decrease in the SOD and GPx activities. CONCLUSION: Concurrent HIIT attenuated D-galactose-induced hepatic molecular and biochemical alterations associated with aging. These effects were accompanied by changes in SIRT1-P16-related markers, improved redox balance, and reduced inflammatory responses, supporting the potential of HIIT as a non-pharmacological strategy for promoting liver health during aging.

articles.title: Reliability and analytical validity of the MX3 hydration testing system during exercise in the heat.
articles.authors: Xiujing Zhao, Brendon P McDermott, Zachary J McKenna et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The MX3 Hydration Testing System provides portable saliva osmolality (SOsm) measurements, but its between-day reliability and analytical validity against a laboratory reference osmometer remain unclear. This study evaluated MX3 reliability and analytical validity and examined whether measurement performance differed between direct tongue and collected-saliva sampling approaches. METHODS: Twenty healthy, physically active adults (10 females) completed one 30-min familiarization trial and two 120-min self-paced exercise trials in the heat. SOsm was measured using MX3 directly from the tongue and from collected saliva samples and compared with a laboratory freezing-point depression osmometer (OSMO1). Between-day reliability was evaluated using the coefficient of variation (CV), intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and Bland-Altman analysis. Analytical validity was assessed using linear regression, CV, and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Direct tongue measurements demonstrated poor between-day reliability (CV = 31-35%; ICC = - 0.003-0.053), whereas collected-saliva measurements demonstrated lower variability and moderate reliability (CV = 17-18%; ICC = 0.618-0.663). Collected-saliva measurements were strongly related to OSMO1 across all measurement conditions (R2 = 0.570-0.821; all p < 0.001), with mean biases ranging from - 23.9 to - 25.9 mOsm/kg and 95% limits of agreement (LoA) ranging from - 75.4 to 27.1 mOsm/kg. In contrast, direct tongue measurements showed weaker and less consistent relationships with OSMO1 (R2 = 0.001-0.282; p = 0.005-0.804), greater variability (CV = 36-51%), and larger negative biases (- 31.3 to - 52.0 mOsm/kg), with 95% LoA ranging from - 134.4 to 30.4 mOsm/kg. Agreement between the two MX3 sampling approaches was limited, particularly following exercise. CONCLUSION: Collected-saliva MX3 measurements demonstrated better between-day reliability and analytical performance than direct tongue measurements, although systematic disagreement with the reference osmometer remained. MX3 measurement performance differed between saliva sampling approaches, supporting further validation of the collected-saliva approach.

articles.title: Acute and Chronic L-Carnitine Supplementation Enhances Endurance Performance Without Consistent Effects on Substrate Oxidation in Active Individuals: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Hilal Eryiğit, Yasemin Güzel, Süleyman Bulut et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to systematically evaluate the effects of acute and chronic L-carnitine supplementation on endurance performance and substrate oxidation during exercise among active individuals. METHODS: This systematic review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. A total of 647 studies were initially retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Ovid MEDLINE, EBSCO Open Dissertations, EBSCO Academic Search Ultimate, and SPORTDiscus databases, with searches conducted from database inception to February 1, 2026. Randomized placebo-controlled crossover and parallel-group trials were eligible for inclusion. Studies meeting the inclusion criteria were assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, with the crossover-specific version applied to randomized crossover trials. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies met the inclusion criteria. Overall, 15 (83%) studies were rated as having some concerns, three (17%) were classified as having a high risk of bias, and none were judged to be at low risk of bias. Ten studies investigated acute L-carnitine supplementation (2-15 g), seven studies examined chronic supplementation (2-3 g/day for 2-24 weeks), and one study evaluated both acute and chronic supplementation (3 g on a single day and over 2 weeks). Both acute and chronic L-carnitine supplementation were associated with improvements in endurance performance following acute supplementation and chronic supplementation. By contrast, no significant changes in fat oxidation during exercise were reported after either acute (2-4 g ingested 120-180 min before exercise) or chronic supplementation (2 g/day for 2-4 weeks). CONCLUSIONS: L-carnitine may enhance selected endurance performance outcomes among active individuals; however, its reputation as a "fat-burning" ergogenic aid is not supported by current evidence, following short-term supplementation.

articles.title: Key Physical Predictors of Maximal Velocity Sprinting in Australian Track and Field Athletes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Timothy A Sayer, Nicholas Cross
articles.abstract: Sayer, TA, and Cross, N. Key physical predictors of maximal velocity sprinting in Australian track and field athletes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to identify the key physical predictors of maximal velocity (MaxV) sprinting at 20 and 60 meters among highly trained Australian track sprinters. Twenty-four athletes (mixed sample: 12 male, 12 female, 68.90 ± 8.77 kg, 1.74 ± 0.08 m) completed a battery of strength and dynamic tests followed by maximal 60-meter sprints. Best-subset multiple linear regression (up to 5 predictors), evaluated by leave-one-out cross-validation, was used to model MaxV at each distance. The 60-meter MaxV model was highly significant, F (5,18) = 50.39, p < 0.001, explaining 93.3% of the variance (R2 = 0.93, adjusted R2 = 0.92, SEE = 0.19), with countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse (β = 0.78, p < 0.001), isometric leg-press peak force (β = 0.43, p = 0.001) and CMJ stiffness (β = 0.40, p < 0.001) the strongest positive contributors. The 20 meter MaxV model was also significant, F (5,18) = 28.12, p < 0.001, explaining 88.6% of the variance (R2 = 0.89, adjusted R2 = 0.86, SEE = 0.18), with single-leg drop jump (SLDJ) eccentric impulse (β = 0.87, p < 0.001) and CMJ power (β = 0.46, p < 0.001) the strongest contributors. Single-leg drop jump reactive strength index and isometric quadriceps force were significant within both models but carried suppressor (sign-reversed) coefficients. These results indicate that vertical jump force time qualities, particularly CMJ impulse and power, isometric leg-press force, and SLDJ eccentric impulse, are key physical components of MaxV sprinting and should be prioritized by coaches when assessing and developing sprint athletes.

articles.title: Effect of Energy Restriction Combined with Probiotic Supplementation on Body Weight and Adiposity-Related Parameters in Adults with Overweight or Obesity: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Marcus V L Dos Santos Quaresma, Camila Guazzelli Marques, Ana Carolina Oumatu Magalhães et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Gut microbiota modulation has been proposed as an adjunct strategy for obesity management, but the additional effects of probiotics during energy restriction (ER) remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether probiotic supplementation combined with ER improves body weight and adiposity-related outcomes in adults with overweight or obesity compared with ER alone. DATA SOURCES: This systematic review and meta-analysis followed the PRISMA guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and LILACS were searched through August 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing ER plus probiotics with ER alone or ER plus placebo. DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently screened the studies and extracted the data. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was body weight (BW); secondary outcomes were Body Mass Index (BMI), fat mass (FM), body fat percentage (BF%), waist circumference (WC), and fat-free mass (FFM). DATA ANALYSIS: Nineteen randomized controlled trials involving 1343 participants were included, of which 16 contributed to the meta-analysis. Interventions lasted 3-20 weeks, probiotic doses ranged from 1.8 × 106 to 1.5 × 1011 colony-forming units / day, and ER ranged from fixed deficits of 300-1000 kcal/day to relative reductions of 20% to 30%. Random-effects models showed no additional effect of probiotics on BW (mean difference [MD], -0.41 kg; 95% CI, -1.21 to 0.40), BMI (-0.12 kg/m²; -0.39 to 0.15), BF% (-0.63%; -1.52 to 0.26), WC (-0.33 cm; -1.06 to 0.39), or FFM (0.03 kg; -0.18 to 0.24). A small reduction in FM favored ER plus probiotics (-0.34 kg; -0.60 to -0.08; P = .016) and remained significant after excluding high-risk-of-bias studies. CONCLUSION: Adding probiotics to ER does not meaningfully enhance weight loss or body composition outcomes. Although FM was modestly reduced, the magnitude of the reduction was small, and its clinical relevance remains uncertain across the included randomized clinical trials overall. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD42024619326.

articles.title: The paracondylar process: anatomical relationships and clinical implications.
articles.authors: Beitris Chiu, Nigel Williams, Hong Kuan Kok et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The paracondylar process (PCP) is a rare and infrequently reported anatomical variant, where the incomplete separation of the lowest occipital sclerotome (proatlas) and uppermost cervical sclerotome results in a complete bony projection that meets with an epitransverse process of the atlas. We report a case that highlights the imaging and anatomical relationships of the PCP, particularly with the vertebral artery (VA), which has been given little attention in literature despite its important symptomatic and neurosurgical implications. CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old male presented with longstanding limitation to neck movement, left‑sided headaches and occasional dizzy spells. Cervical computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a bony strut projecting inferiorly from the skull base, laterally adjacent to the left occipital condyle, articulating with the epitransverse process of C1. Though CT angiography was not performed, close examination of the course of the left vertebral artery on the soft tissue CT windows demonstrated an intimate relationship of the artery coursing immediately medial to the bony process in its V3 segment. We present a three-dimensional reconstruction prepared via segmentation and close reading of the soft tissue CT to illuminate the expected course of the vertebral artery and its' relationship to the PCP. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the anatomical and clinical significance of the paracondylar process (PCP), with a particular focus on its relationship with the vertebral artery. Whilst rare, this finding carries important clinical implications if surgical resection is to be contemplated.

articles.title: Cortical bone geometry and static gravitational loads in neosauropod dinosaurs: Implications for biomechanical constraints on terrestrial gigantism.
articles.authors: Tito Aureliano, Aline M Ghilardi, Holly N Woodward et al.
articles.abstract: Sauropod dinosaurs achieved unprecedented terrestrial gigantism, raising questions about the biomechanical limits of bone under extreme gravitational loads. We estimated static gravitational pressures (Pg) on appendicular cortical bone in neosauropods, including diplodocoids, brachiosaurids, and titanosaurs. We did this by measuring cortical thickness, estimating body masses, and calculating pressures on limb bones. We compared the results with the theoretical fracture thresholds of composite cortical bone (~150-200 MPa) and pure crystalline hydroxyapatite (~1000 MPa). In the largest specimens, Pg remained two orders of magnitude below the compressive strength of hydroxyapatite. These estimates are a conservative lower bound because they assume simultaneous four-limb support. They are also substantially lower (>15 MPa) than the functional failure threshold of composite cortical bone. Dynamic behaviors raise these values: during slow locomotion, a single hindlimb may briefly support the entire hindquarter load, and the weight distribution between fore- and hindlimbs varies markedly with center-of-mass position. Even so, rearing on the hindlimbs in the largest titanosaurs (>25 metric tons) would remain within safe limits defined by composite-bone failure thresholds. Neosauropod lineages show distinct biomechanical strategies. Diplodocoids kept a posteriorly positioned center of mass compatible with facultative bipedal rearing. Brachiosaurids shifted it cranially through neck and forelimb hypertrophy. Titanosaurs reached extreme sizes through enhanced secondary bone remodeling and extensive postcranial pneumatization. Cortical thickening is consistently associated with increasing gravitational loads across Neosauropoda. However, this static model does not test whether it was the primary evolutionary response, compared with other strategies such as trabecular densification and postcranial pneumaticity.

articles.title: Supplementation with fortified balanced energy-protein during pregnancy and lactation and infant growth outcomes in southern Nepal: a community-based 2×2 factorial randomized trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Tsering P Lama, Parul Christian, Yunhee Kang et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Small-for-gestational age birth and infant linear growth faltering are prevalent in South Asia. The World Health Organization recommends balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplementation in pregnancy for undernourished populations, but evidence on the extension of supplementation through lactation to improve infant growth remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the effect of daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy and lactation on infant mean length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and secondary growth outcomes at 6 months of age. METHODS: MINT (Maternal Infant Nutrition Trial) was a 2x2 factorial, household randomized, unblinded efficacy trial to assess a daily fortified BEP supplement during pregnancy and/or lactation compared to no supplement on birth and infant growth outcomes in Sarlahi, Nepal. A modified intention-to-treat analysis estimated the effects of supplementation on infant growth outcomes using linear and Poisson regression models. Models without and with adjustment for birth size were used to estimate the overall effect and the effect independent of birth size, respectively. RESULTS: Among 1,554 mothers and 1,568 infants randomized after delivery, there was no interaction between pregnancy and lactation supplementation on the primary infant growth outcome. Neither BEP supplementation during pregnancy nor lactation had an effect on mean infant LAZ at 6 months (unadjusted mean difference for pregnancy: 0.01 [95% CI: -0.10, 0.12]; for lactation -0.02 [95% CI: -0.13, 0.09]). Significant differences were not observed for any secondary outcomes: mean weight-for-length z-scores, weight-for-age z-scores, infant weight, length, head circumference, mid-upper arm circumference or prevalence of stunting, wasting, and underweight at 6-months or for a subset of infants at 12-months. Null effects persisted after adjustment for birth size. CONCLUSIONS: In rural Nepal, daily fortified BEP supplementation during pregnancy or early lactation did not improve linear or ponderal growth of infants at 6- or 12-months. To reduce the burden of early infant growth faltering, alternative strategies should be considered. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT03668977. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03668977?term=nct03668977&rank=1.

articles.title: Relationship between muscle pathology and tendon collagen organization in patients undergoing below-knee amputation.
articles.authors: Jennifer A Zellers, Sophia McSpedon, Jeremie L A Ferey et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Muscles and tendons are routinely studied in isolation, limiting our understanding of how treatments or pathologies in one component of the musculotendinous unit affect or co-occur in the other. The purpose of this cross-sectional study was to examine baseline relationships between muscle and tendon components. METHODS: Tendon and muscle specimens were obtained from individuals undergoing lower extremity amputation (age range: 37-65). Tensile mechanical testing with quantitative polarized light imaging quantified tendon mechanical properties and collagen alignment. Muscle biopsies obtained from the same muscle-tendon unit were assessed with histology (i.e. area fractions of extracellular matrix, intramuscular adipose tissue, neuropathy, and centrally nucleated fibers). Relationships in intramuscular/intratendinous lipid were assessed, and distributions of type I and III collagen tendon matrix components were evaluated. RESULTS: Statistically significant bivariate correlations were observed between muscle pathology (extracellular matrix, intramuscular adipose tissue, and neuropathy) and tendon collagen organization. Muscles with greater areas of pathology were connected to tendons with more aligned collagen. Muscle extracellular matrix and intramuscular adipose tissue explained the most variance in tendon collagen organization. There was no relationship between intramuscular and intratendinous lipid, and both lipid and collagen III were primarily within the intrafascicular and perivascular space within the tendon. CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to our hypothesis, muscle-tendon units with greater muscle pathology had tendons with more aligned collagen. These findings highlight the importance of assessing both tendon and muscle characteristics, as dysfunction in one component may not be shared with the other component.

articles.title: An observational study of food-related emotional expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating in the UK adult population.
articles.authors: Jenna R Cummings, Zoé Colombet, Emma Boyland
articles.abstract: According to expectancy theory, people eat food that they expect will bring positive emotions. The present research aimed to identify food and non-alcoholic beverages UK adults most expected to bring positive emotions; test influences of high fat, salt and/or sugar (HFSS) and branding on expectancies; and investigate associations of expectancies with diet quality and comfort eating (i.e. eating induced by negative emotions). A representative sample of UK adults (n 1203; Mage = 47 years; 52 % women; 87 % white) viewed food and non-alcoholic beverage images and completed the Anticipated Effects of Food Scale-Brief, a food frequency questionnaire, and questions about comfort eating and sociodemographic background. We ranked means of positive expectancies, conducted multilevel modelling to test influences of HFSS and branding on expectancies and examined correlations among expectancies, diet quality and comfort eating. Participants more strongly expected eating branded HFSS (e.g. Cadbury Twirl chocolate) v. generic non-HFSS (e.g. prawn curry) would result in positive emotions [b = 0·10, se = 0·04, p = ·02, 95 % CI (0·02, 0·18)]. Greater positive expectancies for HFSS - branded and generic - were associated with worse diet quality, especially positive expectancies for ice cream sundaes, fizzy drinks and chocolate (rs = -0·14 to -0·19, ps < ·001). Greater positive expectancies for HFSS and negative expectancies for HFSS and non-HFSS were associated with more frequent comfort eating (rs = 0·08 to 0·30, ps < ·05). Targeting positive HFSS expectancies through food environment policy and behavioural programmes may be a promising strategy for improving diet quality and reducing comfort eating in the UK adult population. Adults who comfort eat may also benefit from challenging negative expectancies for all foods.

articles.title: MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties across testing positions and their associations with maximal strength.
articles.authors: Shani Herszfang, Noam Avitan, Alon Kalron
articles.abstract: The MyotonPRO is increasingly used to quantify skeletal muscle mechanical properties; however, hamstring measurements may vary across testing positions, and the relationships between these measurements and maximal strength remain unclear. This study investigated differences in MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties of the biceps femoris and semitendinosus across four testing positions and examined their exploratory associations with maximal isometric hamstring strength. Thirty healthy adults (18 males, 12 females; age 27.4 ± 4.9 years) underwent MyotonPRO assessment in the prone position, prone with the knee flexed to 90°, bilateral standing, and single-leg standing. Oscillation frequency, dynamic stiffness, logarithmic decrement, relaxation time, and creep were measured in both muscles. Maximal isometric hamstring strength was assessed using the End Range Hamstring Strength Test with handheld dynamometry. MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties differed significantly across testing positions, with large position effects (partial η2 = 0.355-0.822). Stiffness and oscillation frequency generally increased toward weight-bearing positions, whereas relaxation time and creep decreased; logarithmic decrement showed a less consistent pattern. Exploratory correlation analyses showed moderate-to-strong associations between maximal hamstring strength and stiffness, frequency, and relaxation time, as well as creep (|r| = 0.38-0.67), whereas logarithmic decrement showed weaker and more variable associations. In an exploratory hierarchical regression, adding logarithmic decrement to the selected stiffness measure increased R2 from 0.440 to 0.500, but the incremental change was not statistically significant (ΔR2 = 0.060, p = 0.082). These findings indicate that MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties differ across testing positions and should therefore be interpreted within standardized testing conditions.

articles.title: Effects of acetaminophen ingestion on the torque-duration relationship and fatigability during intermittent exercise in patients with type 1 diabetes.
articles.authors: Nadia Fekih, Amal Machfer, Achraf Ammar et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the effects of acute ingestion of acetaminophen (ACT) on the magnitude of exercise-induced peripheral fatigue (ΔPtw) in patients with type 1 diabetes (T1D). In a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind design, 22 males (11 T1D and 11 control (CTR) completed 60 maximum voluntary contractions 60 min after ingesting 1 g of acetaminophen (ACT) or 1 g of placebo (PL) on two separate visits. Central and peripheral fatigue were assessed from pre- to post-exercise changes in quadriceps voluntary activation (ΔVA) and potentiated twitch force (ΔPtw), respectively. Critical torque (CT) was defined as the mean force produced during the final 12 contractions, and work performed (W') was computed as the impulse performed above CT. Maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), VA and Ptw decreased after exercise in both groups, with no significant difference between PL and ACT condition. Compared to PL, ACT increased root mean square/Mmax and CT values in the T1D (+21% and 8% respectively) and CTR groups (+40% and +19%; respectively), with significant lower effect in the T1D compared to the CTR group (P < 0.05). No significant effect of ACT was observed for W' in the T1D (+7%) and CTR groups (+4%) (P = 0.68). These findings indicate that acute ACT ingestion increased CT and muscle activation during the repeated-MVC protocol in both groups, although the magnitude of these responses was smaller in the T1D than the CTR group.

articles.title: Large language models for gait classification and treatment recommendation in cerebral palsy.
articles.authors: Meltem Çelik, Sema Ertan-Birsel, Elif Demirci et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language model (LLM)-based artificial intelligence systems are increasingly being explored for the interpretation of clinical and biomechanical data. However, their ability to classify cerebral palsy gait patterns and support treatment-related decision-making remains unclear. RESEARCH QUESTION: How accurately can commonly used LLM-based AI systems classify sagittal gait patterns in children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy using kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait videos, and how well do their treatment recommendations agree with expert decisions? METHODS: Fifteen children with spastic diplegic cerebral palsy, including three cases from each Rodda sagittal gait pattern, were retrospectively evaluated. ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude independently classified each case using bilateral sagittal-plane kinematic graphs and three-dimensional skeletal gait model videos and provided treatment recommendations. Expert consensus served as the reference standard. Agreement was assessed using Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, together with classification accuracy. RESULTS: Classification accuracy was higher in the graph-based condition than in the video-based condition. Claude showed the highest graph-based performance (73.3% accuracy; κ=0.67), while ChatGPT and Gemini each achieved 46.7% accuracy (κ=0.33). Video-based accuracy decreased to 26.7% for ChatGPT and Gemini (κ=0.08) and 20.0% for Claude (κ=0.00). Inter-model agreement was fair for graph-based classification (κ=0.31) but poor for video-based classification (κ=-0.07). Treatment recommendation agreement was generally low across models and modalities. SIGNIFICANCE: Under the tested conditions, LLMs achieved higher accuracy with kinematic graphs, although the difference cannot be attributed to input modality alone. Graph-based classification showed promising performance; however, limited treatment concordance indicates that current LLMs should be considered supportive rather than independent clinical decision-making tools.

articles.title: "Markers of benefit": the influence of physiological and physical factors on the relationship between slow-paced breathing and heart rate variability.
articles.authors: Rabeea Maqsood, Susie Schofield, Anthony Michael James Bull et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Slow-paced breathing (SPB) improves autonomic balance and increases heart rate variability (HRV). The influence of combat-related traumatic injury (CRTI), baseline respiratory rate (RR), and physical function/activity on the relationship between SPB and HRV has not been examined previously and was the aim of this study. METHODS: We analysed the first follow-up data from the ongoing ArmeD serVices trAuma rehabilitatioN outComE (ADVANCE) Cohort study. Short-term HRV was measured using a single-lead electrocardiogram during five minutes of spontaneous breathing, followed by five minutes of SPB (six breaths/minute). We examined the effect modification of SPB on HRV by CRTI (yes/no), RR during spontaneous breathing (< 15/≥15 breaths/minute), weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire and physical function (6-minute-walk-distance; 6MWD). Linear models for panel data were run, adjusting for age, sampling rank, ethnicity, and cardiovascular and respiratory medication. RESULTS: A total of 962 male participants (median age: 37.6 years; n = 487 injured, n = 495 uninjured; mean 11years post-injury/deployment) with paired spontaneous-SPB HRV data were included. All short-term HRV measures increased during SPB when compared to spontaneous breathing. CRTI, 6MWD and MVPA did not significantly moderate the effect of SPB on HRV, but baseline RR ≥ 15 breaths/minute did, with Root-Mean-Square-Of-Successive-Difference (RMSSD) increasing from 15.57ms to 21.89ms (p < 0.001) during SPB. CONCLUSION: SPB improves HRV regardless of CRTI status. Those with higher baseline RR are more likely to obtain a significant improvement in HRV during SPB. SPB-based interventions may be introduced for the rehabilitation of military personnel following injury/deployment.

articles.title: Arboreal signals in the skeletal proportions of the Gorilla foot.
articles.authors: Elliot G Greiner, Christopher B Ruff, Andrea Lukova et al.
articles.abstract: Postcranial skeletal proportions in living apes have been linked to patterns of arboreal behaviors within and between populations, offering a comparative baseline for interpreting arboreal behavior in fossil hominoids. We quantified metatarsal and proximal phalangeal lengths across all five pedal rays in Gorilla, comparing western lowland gorillas (Gorilla gorilla gorilla), low- and high-elevation Grauer's gorillas (Gorilla beringei graueri), and two ecologically distinct mountain gorilla (Gorilla beringei beringei) populations: those of Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, Uganda, and the Virunga Massif (Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda). The Bwindi sample, assembled from individuals recovered by the Mountain Gorilla Skeletal Project between 2017 and 2025, represents the first substantial pedal dataset for this population. After separately scaling element lengths by estimated body mass and hindlimb length, Bwindi gorillas' third and fourth metatarsal lengths fell consistently between those of the more arboreal western lowland and highly terrestrial Virunga gorillas, while proximal phalangeal and hallux lengths varied little across populations. Additionally, Virunga gorillas showed longer second metatarsals compared to other populations, a feature we link to their strongly terrestrial locomotor habits. In comparing relative manual and pedal element lengths from the same individuals, metacarpals were relatively longer than metatarsals across all populations in rays 2-5, with this pattern reversed in the hallux; among these, only the second ray showed a significant interpopulation difference, with western lowland gorillas exhibiting relatively longer metacarpals than all other groups. Though interpopulation differences in the lengths of pedal elements were generally weaker than those found in the manual elements of the same individuals, these findings suggest that habitat-associated variation in foot morphology can be detected between populations of gorilla subspecies, underscoring the value of fine-grained, population-level skeletal comparisons for refining locomotor inference in the hominoid and hominin fossil record.

articles.title: Exercise-based rehabilitation interventions for kinesiophobia after total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.authors: Hongbo Wen, Ting Zhang, Tingting Xie et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Affecting 21-35% of patients after total knee arthroplasty (TKA), kinesiophobia critically impedes postoperative rehabilitation. Whether exercise-based interventions reduce kinesiophobia more effectively than routine postoperative rehabilitation remains unclear. METHODS: We systematically searched 11 databases from inception to July 11, 2026, for RCTs comparing exercise-based rehabilitation with routine postoperative rehabilitation in adults undergoing primary TKA. The primary outcome was kinesiophobia. Secondary outcomes included knee function, pain, balance, mobilization time, and adherence. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using RevMan 5.4. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Eleven RCTs (N = 1,096) were included. Exercise-based rehabilitation was associated with a reduction in kinesiophobia (SMD = - 1.22, 95% CI [- 1.72, - 0.72]; I2 = 93%; low certainty) and improvements in knee function (SMD = 1.19, 95% CI [0.67, 1.71]; I2 = 93%; low certainty). For pain, the ≤ 4-week pooled estimate (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.03, - 0.14]; I2 = 94%) was not interpretable due to extreme heterogeneity and was not robust: after exclusion of the single acute in-hospital trial, the confidence interval crossed zero (SMD = - 1.09, 95% CI [- 2.28, 0.09]). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses otherwise supported the directional conclusions for kinesiophobia and knee function, although effect sizes were unstable and certainty remained low. CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that exercise-based rehabilitation may be associated with reductions in kinesiophobia at ≤ 4 weeks and an interpretable 12-week improvement in knee function after TKA; the ≤ 4-week and ≥ 24-week functional subgroup estimates were not interpretable because of extreme heterogeneity, and the early pain signal was possible but non-robust. Effect sizes should be interpreted with caution due to substantial heterogeneity, risk of bias, and sensitivity to outlying studies. Well-designed, multicenter RCTs with rigorous blinding and standardized protocols are urgently needed.

articles.title: Dietary Supplement Use and Beliefs Among Athletes at the 2025 Canada Games.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jana Daher, Adriah Kate Sahajpal, Vijay Sahajpal et al.
articles.abstract: Dietary supplement use is widespread among athletes; however, limited data exist regarding supplement use and beliefs among Canadian youth athletes. This cross-sectional online study aimed to examine dietary supplement use and related beliefs among athletes competing at the 2025 Canada Games in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador. A total of 473 respondents participated in the survey. Of the 473 participants, 385 completed responses to the dietary supplement (DS) questions. Among participants who reported their sex, 125 were male and 189 were female. Overall, 36% of participants reported current dietary supplement use. Supplement use was significantly higher among males than females (47% vs. 23%, p < .001) and increased with age (p = .001). The most commonly reported supplements were protein powder (49%), sports drinks (46%), and creatine (45%). Primary reasons for use included maintaining good health (76%), increasing energy (54%), and promoting recovery (50%). Coaches (50%) and healthcare professionals (49%) were the most frequently reported information sources. Supplement users demonstrated significantly stronger positive beliefs regarding benefits of dietary supplements compared with non-users (all p < .001). Ordinal logistic regression showed that supplement users had greater odds of stronger agreement that supplements improve performance (OR = 5.50, 95% CI: 3.31-9.13, p < .001). These findings highlight the use of dietary supplements among Canadian youth athletes and support the need for targeted nutrition education to promote informed decision-making.

articles.title: Functional Adaptations for Load-Bearing in a Dermal Bone: The Pectoral Fin Spine of the Russian Sturgeon (Huso Gueldenstaedtii).
articles.authors: Esteban Marroquín-Arroyave, Joshua Milgram
