articles.abstract: Dermal bone, which forms a variety of skeletal structures and persists in a wide range of extant vertebrates, evolved prior to endochondral bone which forms all mammalian load-bearing long bones. Sturgeons (Acipenseriformes) are an early-diverging extant lineage of actinopterygians that retain prominent post-cranial dermal skeletal elements. They retain a long robust spine at the leading edge of the pectoral fin, called the pectoral fin spines (PFS). PFS are bone elements that are present in many extinct and extant species of non-tetrapod jawed fish. In this study, we characterize the structure (light, polarized, micro-computed tomography and scanning electron microscopy), composition (FTIR, TGA, BMD), and mechanical properties (3-point bending and microindentation) of the PFS of the Russian sturgeon (Huso gueldenstaedtii). The microstructure of the PFS is highly organized as it is formed by dermal osteonal bone and parallel fibered bone. Its microarchitecture, along with high material toughness, anisotropy, and substantial ash content, enables the PFS to bear loads and function in both locomotion and protection. In addition, we show an interconnected network of neurovascular canals and ornamentations, features also found in PFS of other non-tetrapod jawed fish. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dermal bone can form structurally organized, mechanically competent load-bearing elements and provide new insights into PFSs in ray-finned fish.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Oxysterol Signaling in Epigenetic Regulation and Therapeutic Development.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Yaping Wang, Shunlin Ren
articles.abstract: Oxysterols are oxygenated cholesterol derivatives with receptor-dependent and epigenetic activities. This review examines how mitochondrial cholesterol metabolism and oxysterol sulfation may connect lipid metabolism to DNA methylation and communication between hepatocytes and macrophages. Biochemical studies show that 25-hydroxycholesterol (25HC) and 27-hydroxycholesterol (27HC) activate DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), whereas their 3-sulfated derivatives inhibit the activities of DNMT1, DNMT3A, and DNMT3B. Cholestenoic acid (CA) has a concentration-dependent effect, activating DNMT1 at lower concentrations and inhibiting it at higher concentrations. In hepatocyte models, these activities are associated with altered promoter CpG methylation and expression of genes involved in lipid metabolism, inflammatory responses, and cell survival. The sulfated CA metabolite, 3β-sulfate-5-cholestenoic acid (3SCA), is secreted by hepatocytes and modifies inflammatory gene expression in macrophages. We propose an oxysterol epigenetic rheostat in which metabolite concentrations and sulfation influence DNMT activities. Published animal studies support protective effects of 25-hydroxycholesterol 3-sulfate in fatty liver disease, endotoxemia, and acetaminophen-induced liver injury. Its clinical formulation, larsucosterol, has shown favorable hepatic and metabolic signals in Phase 1b fatty liver studies and nominally significant mortality reductions in prespecified US Phase 2b alcohol-associated hepatitis (AH) analyses. These encouraging findings require confirmation because the overall Phase 2b primary endpoint was not met. Larsucosterol has received Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for AH and is currently being evaluated in a registrational Phase 3 trial.

articles.title: Confronting the Twin Divides: Data Bias and Infrastructure Gaps in AI-Driven Nutrition for the Global South.
articles.authors: Haddijatou Kadji Ceesay, Jean Claude Nahayo, Abdul Samad et al.
articles.abstract: Nutrition science is being rapidly transformed by artificial intelligence (AI). Yet, its application in the Global South, here defined as low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) primarily across Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, and Latin America, is constrained by two interrelated challenges: data bias (e.g., non-diverse datasets, imbalanced samples, and inadequate attention to demographic, cultural, and socioeconomic variation) and infrastructure gaps (e.g., intermittent connectivity, unreliable electricity, and limited device access). These issues are not merely technical but structural, ranging from non-diverse training sets and culturally mismatched food recognition systems to limited population-specific validation, which produce biased outputs when deployed in settings with substantially different dietary patterns and food environments. Weak digital infrastructure, the absence of data governance, and limited workforce capacity further undermine equitable deployment. The Food Recognition Assistance and Nudging Insights (FRANI) application, validated in Ghana, Vietnam, and Sri Lanka, demonstrates what is technically possible but also highlights the boundaries of current progress: more than 90% of AI models for malnutrition go unused in day-to-day clinical practice. Existing reviews map these domains separately. This commentary argues that integrating data bias and infrastructure gaps within a single analytical framework is essential for equitable AI-driven nutrition in the Global South, and it calls for actionable policy responses that prioritize local data sovereignty, infrastructure investment, and governance frameworks before algorithmic deployment.

articles.title: Ethical, methodological, and translational framework for animal studies in physical exercise research.
articles.authors: Ricardo A Pinho, Larissa C Marques, Lei Zhou et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental research involving physical exercise (PE) in animal models has contributed significantly to advancing knowledge in several areas, including physiology, biochemistry, and translational medicine. Despite the widespread use of these models, important concerns remain regarding methodological heterogeneity, limited experimental standardization, reproducibility of findings, and the translational validity of preclinical outcomes. In this context, the present article proposes an integrated decision-making framework for animal-based PE research. The framework complements existing guidelines linking ethical justification, animal welfare, experimental design, exercise prescription, and translational interpretation throughout the different stages of study development. The manuscript is based on international guidelines for animal experimentation, including ARRIVE 2.0, PREPARE, the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, AVMA recommendations, the APS Resource Book for the Design of Animal Exercise Protocols, and recent methodological recommendations for preclinical exercise research in metabolic and cardiovascular diseases. The topics address aspects related to ethical decision-making in the use of animal models, the principles of the 3Rs, selection of species, strain, sex, and age, sample size calculation, inclusion and exclusion criteria, translational validity, and the definition of exercise protocols, including intensity, frequency, duration, equipment, and experimental monitoring. This framework is intended to support more consistent experimental decisions, including selection, justification, and implementation, according to the research question, animal model, and intended translational inference.

articles.title: The Applied Sport Science of Professional Male Basketball: A Narrative Review of Current and Emerging Practices.
articles.authors: Matthew Morrison, Jonathon Weakley, Scott McLean et al.
articles.abstract: Basketball is a physically demanding intermittent team sport which requires a multifaceted approach to optimise player preparation, performance, health, and recovery. Quantifying the training and match demands of professional basketball players can help practitioners develop effective strategies for managing fatigue, monitoring training loads, and guiding physical preparation. Sleep and travel disruptions present additional challenges to practitioners and can have deleterious effects on recovery and readiness to compete. Nutrition is also an essential component supporting performance and recovery and should be individualised to the needs of each player. The inherent complexity of basketball requires practitioners to develop a holistic view that considers the interaction between tactical, technical, psychological, and physical basketball-related factors along with external factors from the greater basketball system (e.g., players, coaches, support staff, organisations, schedules, referees, and governing bodies) that can influence performance. Advances in technology continue to shape performance monitoring, injury-risk forecasting, and training methodologies, yet practitioners must be aware of potential risks such as player privacy concerns and the misuse of data. A comprehensive understanding of these factors provides valuable insights for practitioners to develop effective evidence-based strategies and frameworks for working with professional male basketball players.

articles.title: Development and validation of a questionnaire on food knowledge and perception of the Mediterranean diet: the ICARO food knowledge questionnaire.
articles.authors: Marika Dello Russo, Annarita Formisano, Marialaura Bonaccio et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Adherence to the Mediterranean diet has significantly declined over the last decades, particularly among younger generations, due to socioeconomic factors, increased consumption of ultra-processed foods and limited awareness of its positive effects on health. Addressing these barriers necessitates the enhancement of nutritional education and improved access to healthy food options. This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive questionnaire, the ICARO-Food Knowledge Questionnaire (I-FKQ), to assess food knowledge related to the Mediterranean diet among children, adolescents, and adults. SUBJECT/METHODS: In the context of the ICARO Study, we recruited a sample of 46 parents (for children), 111 adolescents, and 164 adults, from November 2023 to July 2024. Content validity was established through a review by an expert panel, which refined the questionnaire. Assessments of face validity indicated that the I-FKQ is manageable and user-friendly for online administration. Item analysis demonstrated acceptable difficulty and discrimination indices. RESULTS: High test-retest reliability was observed, with strong correlations in scores between the two testing occasions, indicating robust temporal stability. All constructs of the questionnaire demonstrated adequate Cronbach's α and Pearson's correlation coefficients. The overall internal consistency of the questionnaire was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.848), although Section 2 showed slightly lower reliability (Cronbach's α = 0.662). Construct validity, evaluated only in adults, was supported by expected differences in scores according to educational level. CONCLUSION: The I-FKQ demonstrated satisfactory overall psychometric properties and reliable temporal stability. However, while fundamental reliability and face validity parameters were confirmed across multiple age groups, construct validity was established exclusively within the adult population. This specific lack of structural validation currently restricts the full applicability of the instrument in pediatric and adolescent groups. Consequently, pending further psychometric evaluation in younger demographics, the I-FKQ is best suited to support educational and public health initiatives targeting adult populations.

articles.title: Saturated and Trans Fatty Acids Were Not Associated with All-Cause or Cause-Specific Mortality in a Japanese Population with Relatively Low Intakes: The Japan Public Health Center-Based Prospective Study.
articles.authors: Kumiko Kito, Junko Ishihara, Ayaka Kotemori et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines recommend that saturated fatty acids (SFAs) and trans fatty acids (TFAs) should comprise ≤10% and ≤1% of total energy intake, respectively. However, evidence of the mortality risk associated with increased TFA and SFA intake in populations with a relatively low fat intake is limited. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between total fat, SFA, TFA, monounsaturated fatty acid (MUFA), and polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) intake and all-cause and cause-specific mortality in a Japanese population. METHODS: We included 90,807 participants aged 45-74 years with no history of cancer or cardiovascular disease (CVD). Dietary assessment was performed using a validated food frequency questionnaire. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models for each quintile of dietary fat intake: total fat, SFA, MUFA, PUFA, TFA, industrially-derived TFA (i-TFAs), and ruminant-derived TFA (r-TFA). RESULTS: During a mean follow-up of 18.9 years, 22,618 deaths occurred. None of the analyses of fat intakes in quintiles showed a positive association with all-cause mortality for higher intakes of all fats, even for i-TF. In females, a nominally significant association was observed for all-cause mortality with PUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.92 [0.84-0.997]) and cancer mortality with MUFA (HR, Q5 vs. Q1 = 0.84 [0.73-0.97]).In females, higher intakes of total fat and MUFA were nominally associated with higher respiratory disease mortality, whereas a higher SFA intake showed a suggestive association (P for trend <0.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this study, neither SFA nor TFA intake was positively associated with all-cause mortality, and higher PUFA intake was inversely associated with all-cause mortality in females.

articles.title: Antenatal multiple micronutrients versus iron-folic acid supplementation and infant neurodevelopment: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Jitender Nagpal, Sarika Tyagi, Swapnil Rawat et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antenatal multiple micronutrient (MMN) supplementation reduces the risk of low birth weight and small-for-gestational-age birth compared with iron and folic acid (IFA), but whether the benefits extend to neurodevelopment remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: To estimate the effect of antenatal MMN compared with IFA on infant cognitive, motor, and language development up to 24 months of age. METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, OpenGrey, Wiley Online Library, and trial registers through June 10, 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing antenatal MMN with IFA and reporting infant neurodevelopment. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 and certainty with GRADE. Hedges g estimates were pooled with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model and Knapp-Hartung adjustment; cluster-trial variances were inflated by the design effect. RESULTS: Of 2,943 records, seven trials (8 reports; 5,331 infants for the cognitive comparison) were included. MMN and IFA did not differ in cognitive development (g = +0.02; 95% CI -0.06, +0.10; P = 0.53; I2 = 13%) or motor development (g = -0.02; 95% CI -0.09, +0.05; P = 0.49; I2 = 0%). Language showed a small, non-significant advantage for MMN that was not robust across sensitivity analyses (g = +0.07; 95% CI -0.00, +0.14; P = 0.06; I2 = 0%). All pooled point estimates were below the conventional threshold for a small, standardized effect of 0.2. Certainty was moderate for cognitive and motor outcomes and low for language. CONCLUSIONS: Antenatal MMN supplementation was associated with little to no difference in infant cognitive or motor development compared with IFA up to 24 months of age. The small language difference was not statistically significant, was not robust across sensitivity analyses, and is unlikely to be clinically important. PROTOCOL AND REGISTRATION: PROSPERO CRD420261392389. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261392389.

articles.title: Putting Performance First: Measuring What Matters in Sports Science Research.
articles.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance
articles.authors: Christopher J Stevens, Lee Taylor

articles.title: Effect of a health belief model-based nutrition education intervention on dietary diversity among adults on antiretroviral treatment in Ilu Abbabor Zone, Southwestern Ethiopia - ERRATUM.
articles.authors: Ebissa Negera Gemechu, Tefera Belachew Lemma, Kalkidan Hassen Abate

articles.title: Cross bridges, tendons and titin: evolving roles in muscle mechanics.
articles.authors: Kiisa Nishikawa, Stan L Lindstedt
articles.abstract: All fields of science evolve over time as interpretation of the evidence changes with the discovery of new facts, and muscle physiology is no exception. Ideas once thought preposterous may eventually become accepted dogma, as was the case for the sliding filament theory itself. The currently accepted sliding-filament - swinging cross-bridge paradigm views muscles as motors with static isometric force-length and isotonic force-velocity properties that necessarily limit their ability to store and recover viscoelastic energy. These limitations understandably led to the plausible explanation that tendons must be responsible for energy storage and recovery. However, recent advances in technology have enabled investigation of muscle properties in moving humans and other animals, providing significant new data on dynamic muscle function. Bridging the gap between laboratory studies of ex vivo muscle preparations and in vivo muscle mechanics has resulted in a paradigm shift toward the idea that muscles are tunable viscoelastic actuators that can harvest substantial energy from interactions with the environment. Here, we provide a somewhat chronological account of the contentious history of the field of muscle physiology and the evolution of ideas about muscle function, focusing particularly on muscle viscoelastic properties and energy storage. We argue that accumulating data position titin as a length- and activation-dependent viscoelastic element whose properties can be inferred from, and indeed are critical for, in vivo muscle function. We also provide ideas for future directions to stimulate progress in understanding titin's role in dynamic muscle function.

articles.title: The Fibular Artery Communicating Branch and Fibular Artery Dominance: An Anatomical Hazard for Posterior Approaches to the Ankle.
articles.authors: Annabelle Johnston McCarter, Chijioke Orji, Craig Wyatt et al.
articles.abstract: Open reduction of posterior malleolar fractures (PMFs) increasingly employs direct posterior approaches. The posterolateral and posteromedial approaches both develop the deep posterior compartment in the plane between the fibular and posterior tibial arteries, placing the fibular artery communicating branch (FACB) within the operative field; inadvertent injury to this branch has been associated with limb-threatening ischemia. This study quantified the prevalence of the FACB and of fibular artery dominance (FAD), a configuration in which the fibular artery provides the principal distal supply because the posterior tibial artery is atretic or absent, and considered the implications for surgical approach selection. In a single-center cross-sectional study, 916 consecutive lower-limb computed tomography angiograms performed over 1 year were screened; 726 met the inclusion criteria and were assessed by trained reviewers for the FACB, FAD, laterality and clinical indication. An FACB was identified in 280 patients (38.6%, 95% CI 35.1-42.2). Its prevalence varied with clinical indication (χ2 = 33.67, p < 0.001), being highest in peripheral vascular disease (45.1%) and lowest in other vascular referrals (16.4%). FAD occurred exclusively in FACB-positive limbs, in 28 patients (10.0% of FACB-positive limbs; 3.9% of the whole cohort, 95% CI 2.7-5.5), and its distribution did not differ by indication (Freeman-Halton exact p = 0.81). Because the FACB lies within the field of the posterolateral and posteromedial approaches but posterior and lateral to the medial-posteromedial (MPM) approach, the MPM approach avoids the at-risk plane. These findings support anatomically informed approach selection and caution when a posterolateral or posteromedial approach is planned, particularly in patients with peripheral vascular disease.

articles.title: Turkish Research Dietitians Prioritize Strengthening Traditional Methods Before Digital Transition: A Qualitative Study.
articles.authors: Merve Guney-Coskun, Michelle Weech, Rosalind Fallaize et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dietary assessment underpins nutrition research and practice. Food Frequency Questionnaires (FFQs) are used in epidemiology yet have limitations. Digital technologies are reshaping dietary assessment, with potential to improve scalability and standardization. Understanding how dietitians appraise traditional and emerging approaches is critical for guiding context-appropriate innovation. OBJECTIVE: This study explored research-focused Turkish dietitians' perspectives on (i) the strengths and limitations of FFQs, (ii) opportunities and barriers in transitioning to web-based FFQs, and (iii) the potential and challenges of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and biosensors, in dietary assessment, with Türkiye-specific considerations where relevant. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten PhD-qualified, research-focused dietitians in Türkiye, purposively sampled for dietary assessment expertise. Interviews were conducted online, transcribed, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Sample size was guided by thematic saturation; recruitment continued until no substantively new themes emerged across successive interviews. RESULTS: Participants valued FFQs as scalable tools for capturing habitual intake but noted limits in person-level detail, portion accuracy, and recall reliability. Culturally adapted food lists and portion imagery were perceived as priorities to improve validity. Web-based FFQs were viewed as a credible evolution offering efficiency and visual supports, though concerns centered on digital literacy, device access, and user guidance. Emerging tools such as AI-assisted image capture and wearable biosensors were considered promising for reducing memory bias and improving objectivity, but adoption was tempered by concerns over cost, usability, cultural fit, privacy, and governance. CONCLUSIONS: The perspectives of the Turkish research-focused dietitians interviewed in this study point to a staged pathway for innovation: first to strengthen FFQ content with cultural adaptation and visual supports; then digitize with safeguards for accessibility and data integrity; and finally pilot advanced technologies cautiously, under robust validation and ethical oversight. This phased approach could offer an acceptable pathway to modernizing dietary assessment while safeguarding credibility and equity.

articles.title: Maximum Deceleration Is Related to Players' Ability to Repeat High-Intensity Decelerations in a Match in Female Professional Soccer Players.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: David Martínez-Hernández, Paul A Jones, José M Oliva-Lozano et al.
articles.abstract: Martínez-Hernández, D, Jones, PA, Oliva-Lozano, JM, and Harper, DJ. Maximum deceleration is related to players' ability to repeat high-intensity decelerations in a match in female professional soccer players. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was twofold; First, to investigate positional differences in high-intensity decelerations (HID; < -3 m·s-2) and very high-intensity decelerations (VHID; < -4 m·s-2) in elite female soccer players. Second, to examine relationships between maximum deceleration (DMax) and the frequency of HID and VHID throughout competitive match play, reflecting players' capacity to perform these actions repeatedly. Twenty-four professional female outfield players (189 match files) from an English Women's Superleague club were tracked across 27 matches using 10-Hz Global Positioning System devices. Differences in deceleration metrics (DMax, HID, VHID) across positions were analyzed using 1-way analysis of variance and Bonferroni post hoc tests. Pearson's correlations assessed relationships between DMax, HID, and VHID across playing positions. Significant positional differences were observed. Central defenders had the lowest DMax and performed fewer HID and VHID actions than other positions, whereas central midfielder recorded the highest HID values. Maximum deceleration showed moderate-to-large correlations with HID (r = 0.35) and VHID (r = 0.52). Positional and individual variations influenced the strength of these relationships. This study provides novel evidence that maximal deceleration capacity is an important neuromuscular performance quality that distinguishes playing positions in elite women's soccer, with moderate-to-large associations with the ability to perform repeated HID and VHID supporting its relevance to match performance, particularly at higher intensities. These findings suggest that DMax may be an important quality to target through training, with potential implications for repeated deceleration performance. Practitioners should implement position-specific assessments and interventions to optimize deceleration capacity, especially as modern game demands continue to evolve.

articles.title: Intense unimanual contractions increase muscle excitation and local metabolic activity in the resting contralateral forearm.
articles.authors: Lee J Hinkle, Britton C Scheuermann, Carl J Ade et al.
articles.abstract: Intense unilateral muscle contractions evoke measurable activity within the contralateral neuroaxis, which can be detected with surface electromyographic activity in the resting homologous muscle. Physiological mirror activity (PMA), the unintentional increase in contralateral muscle excitation, has been implicated in cross-limb interactions and adaptations. Despite longstanding observations of PMA, it remains unknown whether this low-level muscle excitation influences local muscle metabolism. We addressed this question using a vascular occlusion test in 10 healthy adults. Surface electromyography and near-infrared spectroscopy-derived measures of tissue oxygen saturation and muscle oxygen consumption ( m V . O 2 ) were obtained from the resting left forearm during vascular occlusion at rest and during fatiguing unimanual contractions. PMA in the contralateral resting arm was greater during fatiguing unimanual contractions than during rest (mean difference: 8.9%, 95% CI: 4.1 to 13.8). This increase was accompanied by a steeper rate of tissue oxygen desaturation (mean difference: -0.132% s- 1, 95% CI: -0.227 to -0.037) and greater m V . O 2 (mean difference: 0.188 mL O2 min- 1 100 g- 1, 95% CI: 0.057 to 0.320). Greater PMA was associated with both a faster rate of oxygen desaturation (r = -0.85, 95% CI: -0.96 to -0.46) and greater m V . O 2 (r = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.28 to 0.94). These findings provide the first evidence that PMA is accompanied by increased local metabolic demand, consistent with a coupling between unintentional muscle excitation and oxygen extraction in the resting limb.

articles.title: Rethinking the application and adoption of NOVA classification in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a Southeast Asian food systems perspective.
articles.authors: C Jeyakumar Henry, M Aman Wirakartakusumah, E-Siong Tee et al.
articles.abstract: Ultra-processed foods have increasingly been associated with chronic disease risk in global analyses. The NOVA classification is positioned to influence dietary guidelines, food manufacturing, and public health policy worldwide. This paper argues that the NOVA classification, when applied without contextual adaptation, may be inappropriate for Southeast Asian food systems. It could misdirect policy interventions aimed at addressing both the double burden of under- and overnutrition. By labelling foods as UPFs, NOVA may obscure the essential role that certain processed foods play in improving nutritional outcomes and advancing public health. An overemphasis on the negative impact of processed and ultra-processed foods risks oversimplifying complex dietary patterns in Asia and other LMICs. It may also undermine nutritional gains achieved over the past four decades.

articles.authors: Mathilde Chataigner, Adrien Peltier, Elodie Bouvret et al.

articles.title: Hydroxyproline Enhances Branched-Chain Amino Acid Effects on Lifespan and Healthspan in Caenorhabditis elegans.
articles.authors: Linggao Liu, Ruiyun Wu, Ziwu Gao et al.
articles.abstract: Food-derived protein hydrolysates frequently contain both collagen-associated hydroxyproline (Hyp) and branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), but the biological consequences of their combination remain unclear. This study tested whether Hyp changes the effects of leucine (Leu), isoleucine (Ile), and valine (Val) on lifespan and healthspan-related phenotypes in Caenorhabditis elegans and whether these treatment effects are accompanied by coordinated microbial and metabolic remodeling. Amino acid concentrations that did not strongly disrupt bacterial food clearance were selected for lifespan, stress-resistance, motility, muscle-integrity, biochemical, microbiome, metabolomic, and transcriptomic analyses. Hyp+BCAA combinations improved lifespan- and healthspan-related phenotypes in a BCAA- and dose-dependent manner. The strongest combined treatments enhanced resistance to thermal and oxidative stress, preserved age-associated motility and muscle structure, reduced oxidative and lipofuscin-associated markers, and increased ATP-related readouts. Multi-omics profiling showed that these direct treatment effects were accompanied by distinct C. elegans-associated microbiota signatures, altered NAD precursor-related metabolites including nicotinic acid ribonucleoside (NaR), and a Leu+Hyp transcriptional response enriched for energy metabolism, proteostasis, and extracellular-matrix remodeling. Integrated microbiome-metabolome analysis identified a positive association between Rhodococcus abundance and NaR levels. These findings demonstrate that, under the tested culture conditions, Hyp+BCAA exposure improves longevity-related phenotypes and identifies microbial composition, NAD precursor metabolism, and host energy homeostasis as candidate, testable mediators.

articles.title: Maternal Mannan-Oligosaccharide improves intestinal resilience of weanling pigs via enhancing milk-mediated immune transfer.
articles.authors: Siyu Yuan, Zhenting He, Ronghua Yao et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal nutrition during late gestation and lactation influences milk composition and early-life intestinal development. Whether maternal mannan-oligosaccharide (MOS) supplementation enhances offspring resilience during weaning remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: The effects of maternal MOS supplementation on sow physiology, milk quality, offspring growth, and intestinal responses to an acute inflammatory challenge were evaluated. METHODS: Sixty sows received a control diet or 800 mg MOS/kg diet from gestation day 85 to lactation day 21 (n = 30/group). Reproductive outcomes (litter size, birth weight, subsequent estrus, insemination, conception, and farrowing) and litter outcomes (survival, daily gain, and weaning weight at 21 d) were recorded. Sow feces were collected on gestation day 109 for microbiota analysis, plasma and colostrum at farrowing and milk on lactation day 14 for antioxidant, inflammatory, nutrient, and immunoglobulin analyses, as applicable. At weaning, 24 piglets from 12 litters received saline or lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 100 μg/kg). Plasma and intestinal tissues were collected 6 h later for antioxidant, morphology, barrier, and inflammation measurements. Mixed models assessed maternal diet and, in piglets, maternal diet × LPS, with litter accounted for. RESULTS: Compared with controls, MOS increased sow lactation feed intake (5.68 vs 5.21 kg/d; P = 0.036), piglet daily gain (224.22 vs 195.35 g/d; P < 0.001), and weaning weight (6.67 vs 5.91 kg; P < 0.001). Colostral fat and IgA were 5.26% vs 3.80% and 5.37 vs 3.00 mg/mL, respectively; day-14 milk fat and IgA were 7.72% vs 5.19% and 0.43 vs 0.19 mg/mL (all P < 0.05). Relative to LPS-challenged controls, maternal MOS increased jejunal occludin protein (0.78 vs 0.44, normalized to β-actin) and decreased jejunal IL-1β (146.31 vs 169.77 pg/mL; both P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Maternal MOS supplementation improved milk-mediated nutritional and immune transfer and enhanced intestinal resilience of offspring during weaning-associated inflammatory stress in piglets.

articles.title: The ascending aorta and vascular profile in recreational masters runners: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Wioletta Sacharczuk, Rafał Dankowski, Dagmara Tritt et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Endurance exercise remodels the large arteries, but whether a recreational training dose is sufficient to induce such remodelling is unclear. Masters recreational runners over 40 years are under-represented in this research. We compared the ascending aortic diameter and vascular profile of these runners with sedentary controls of similar age. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 42 masters recreational runners (at least 20 km per week for at least one year) and 27 sedentary controls, all over 40 years, free of cardiovascular disease and without bicuspid aortic valve or connective tissue disorder. We measured the ascending aortic diameter and left ventricular function by transthoracic echocardiography, and brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity (baPWV) and the ankle-brachial index (ABI) by oscillometry. Circulating collagen-turnover markers (CTX-I, MMP-2) were assayed. The aortic diameter was compared between groups by regression. RESULTS: The ascending aorta was wider in runners (3.25 vs. 2.90 cm; p = 0.001; Cliff's delta 0.45). The difference persisted after adjustment for age, sex and height (beta 0.31 cm; p = 0.001) and in sensitivity analyses. No aortic diameter reached 4.0 cm; all remained within normal limits. The ABI was higher in runners (1.07 vs. 1.03; p = 0.007), and baPWV did not differ (p = 0.069); both stayed within normal limits. CTX-I and MMP-2 did not differ, and left ventricular function was preserved. CONCLUSION: These findings are consistent with modest, exercise-associated aortic remodelling rather than overt aortopathy in recreational masters runners over 40 years.

articles.title: Blood lactate concentrations are associated with markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Regis C Pearson, Destiny P Hamilton, Nicholas T Broskey et al.
articles.abstract: The ability to detect metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy can impact the health of mother and infant(s). Lactate may serve as a biomarker to predict metabolic dysfunction risk. The purpose of this study was to determine if fasting or postprandial blood lactate concentrations were related to established markers of metabolic dysfunction during late pregnancy. Overnight fasted healthy women between 32-38 weeks gestation underwent a high-fat meal test. Fasted and postprandial (1h, 2h, and 4h) venous blood glucose, insulin, and lactate were collected. Fasted and postprandial (2h and 4h) respiratory exchange ratios (RERs) were assessed by indirect calorimetry. HOMA-IR and Matsuda indexes were calculated. Participants were categorized into lean (18.5-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (25.0-29.9 kg/m2), or obese (≥30.0 kg/m2) based on pre-pregnancy body mass index. To determine the impact that weight status may have on postprandial lactate concentrations, a repeated-measures analysis of variance was performed on log-transformed data. Spearman's rank-order correlation coefficients were used to assess associations between outcome variables. 52 participants were included in the analysis (lean, n = 29; overweight, n = 11; obese, n = 12). Postprandial lactate was higher in women with obesity compared to women who were lean (1h, p = 0.024; 2h, p = 0.025; 4h, p = 0.010). Among all women, higher lactate area under the curve (AUC) was associated with higher insulin AUC, higher HOMA-IR index, lower Matsuda index, and higher RER AUC (p ≤ 0.003). These findings suggest that postprandially elevated lactate may serve as a useful biomarker for identifying metabolic dysfunction during pregnancy.

articles.title: How to Implement a Ketogenic Diet Therapy in Developing Countries: Colombian Consensus on Ketogenic Diet Therapy Use in the Management of Adults with Drug-Resistant Epilepsy.
articles.authors: Jean Paul Vergara-Aguilar, Angélica Lizcano, Adriana Martinez-Perez et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Drug-resistant epilepsy affects up to one-third of patients with epilepsy and is associated with higher morbidity, mortality, trauma events, psychosocial challenges, and decline in quality of life. In Latin America, disease burden is high and access to advanced therapies remains limited. Ketogenic Diet Therapy (KDT) has been shown to be beneficial in adults, but its implementation requires standardized protocols and experienced multidisciplinary teams. This study aimed to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations to guide the indication, implementation, and follow-up of KDT in adults with drug-resistant epilepsy through expert consensus in Colombia. METHODS: A modified version of the Nominal Group Technique was used to develop, discuss, and vote on management concepts. Clinical questions were structured using the PICO framework. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed and EMBASE for articles published since 2015, and the evidence was integrated with the experience of a multidisciplinary expert panel. RESULTS: Twelve recommendations were issued, covering commercial formulas, induction and follow-up protocols, individualized dietary interventions, safety, diagnostic support, nutritional supplementation, and drug-diet interactions. The consensus highlights the need for interdisciplinary teams, structured education, early adherence strategies, and close follow-up, and the role of enteral emergency formulas in intensive care settings. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence around KDT shows it can be implemented safely as an adjunctive treatment for adults with drug-resistant epilepsy and is reasonable to consider following the failure of two adequate antiseizure medications. Structured implementation may reduce seizure frequency, improve quality of life, and reduce the pharmacological burden. Multicenter prospective studies are needed to further assess efficacy, safety, and resource utilization. These recommendations contribute to closing the gap between evidence and clinical practice.

articles.title: Surgical Profiles of Elite Female Athletes and Their Association with Long-Term Musculoskeletal Health: Findings from the Women's Soccer Health Study.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Kai-Lun Law, Polly de Mille, Heidi Prather et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the career and post-career surgeries in female elite-level soccer players and evaluate their association with long-term musculoskeletal health. STUDY DESIGN: This is a cross-sectional study. METHODS: Surgical data (the number and type of surgeries during and after the career) from an anonymous online survey was obtained from a previously published cohort of 560 retired elite women's soccer players. Correlation coefficients were used to evaluate the relationship between the number of surgeries and physical activity levels (UCLA activity scale), joint function (SANE), and physical and mental health (PROMIS-10), which were all collected on the same survey. RESULTS: The average number of career surgeries was 1 (SD=1.6), and the average number of post-career surgeries was 0.5 (SD=1). The most common career surgery sites for women's soccer players were knee (39%), foot/ankle (12%), and leg (4%). The most common knee procedures involved ligament reconstruction, primarily of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), followed by meniscus and cartilage surgery. The most frequent post-career surgery sites were knee (24.0%), foot/ankle (5.1%), and leg (3.2%). Knee ligament and meniscus surgeries were equally reported. More career and post-career surgeries were associated with lower SANE knee scores (p<0.001). Lower SANE knee scores (p=0.017) were associated with lower UCLA activity levels. CONCLUSIONS: The locations of career and post-career surgeries were similar, suggesting a possible association with long-term musculoskeletal impairment, particularly to the knee, in a cohort of mostly White collegiate former players. Having more soccer-related surgeries was associated with reduced joint function and activity levels after retirement, though the correlations were weak or moderate. These findings suggest the need for the development of preventive interventions that address the specific needs of female athletes, implementation of injury prevention programs and strategies to maximize adherence, and long-term musculoskeletal assessments of players after retirement.

articles.title: An Acute Alcoholic Beer Dose Impaired Exercise Performance: A Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Felipe De Russi de Lima, Vitor de Salles Painelli, Raul Canestri et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We investigated whether a small dose of alcoholic beer ingested before a running exercise bout impaired performance and changed psychophysiological responses to exercise. METHODS: After three sessions of familiarizations, 16 healthy and physically active men (25.8 ± 5.1 years, 175.0 ± 5.4 cm, and 76 ± 6.5 kg) performed a 30-min running time trial in a double-blind and placebo-controlled crossover design, after ingesting either beer (alcohol 4.8% v/v; 0.3 g/kg) or nonalcoholic beer (placebo). Performance, cardiopulmonary (oxygen consumption, ventilation, respiratory exchange ratio, and heart rate), and perceptual (perceived exertion, affect, and motivation) variables were assessed throughout the trial and averaged every 5 min during exercise. Running economy was assessed during steady-state running at 8 km/hr. The data were analyzed through t tests and repeated-measures mixed models (p < .05). RESULTS: The ingestion of beer significantly decreased the average speed by 4.7% (p = .04; d = 0.21) and total distance covered by 4.3% (p = .007; d = 0.26) when compared with placebo. The ingestion of beer also impaired the running economy by 1.1% (p = .01; d = 0.39) and increased respiratory exchange ratio throughout the exercise bout (p = .004, d = 1.07). No beer-by-time interaction effects were detected in cardiopulmonary outcomes (p > .05). CONCLUSIONS: A small dose of alcoholic beer reduced the exercise capacity of healthy individuals, likely due to an impairment in running economy.

articles.title: Not Just Faster Horses: Telerehabilitation as a Necessary Evolution in Physical Therapy.
articles.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
articles.authors: Miguel Farraj, Julien Lebleu, Bruno Bonnechère et al.
articles.abstract: SYNOPSIS: This editorial draws an analogy between the transition from "faster horses" to automobiles and the digital transition facing musculoskeletal physical therapy. Musculoskeletal rehabilitation has long emphasized face-to-face sessions; digital solutions such as telerehabilitation have often been perceived as alternatives to conventional care. However, increasing rehabilitation demands, persistent gaps between sessions, and the need for long-term patient support highlight the importance of rethinking how physical therapists deliver care. We argue that telerehabilitation should not replace physical therapists but rather extend their role through facilitating continuous monitoring, communication, education, and patient engagement. Successful implementation requires more than simply adopting new technologies-it requires clinicians to develop new skills, adapt professional habits, and integrate digital tools while preserving therapeutic relationships and patient-centered care. Just as innovation required moving beyond faster horses, the future of musculoskeletal physical therapy may depend on embracing new models of care rather than simply iterating on traditional approaches. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 2026;56(10):624-626. Epub 28 Aug 2026. doi:10.2519/jospt.2026.14510.

articles.title: Dietary patterns and the testosterone-estrogen axis in men: evidence from osteoporotic fractures in men and a systematic review.
articles.authors: Zahra Aslani, Amy E Kless, Steven K Clinton et al.
articles.abstract: Diet may influence circulating sex steroid hormones, but evidence for overall dietary patterns remains limited. We examined associations of dietary patterns reflecting lower inflammatory potential, lower insulinaemic potential and higher overall diet quality, with circulating sex steroids in older men and systematically reviewed the literature in apparently healthy men published through June 2024. We conducted cross-sectional analyses of 1622 men aged ≥65 years from the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study. Diet was assessed using FFQ and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), total and free testosterone and total and free estradiol were measured. Dietary patterns included the reversed Empirical Dietary Inflammatory Pattern (rEDIP), reversed Empirical Dietary Index for Hyperinsulinaemia (rEDIH) and Healthy Eating Index-2020 (HEI-2020). Among older men, each 1-standard deviation increase in rEDIP was associated with higher total testosterone (β = 2·15; 95 % CI 0·12, 4·18) and free testosterone (β = 2·02 ng/dL; 95 % CI 0·29, 3·75), whereas rEDIH showed similar but non-significant associations with total testosterone (β = 1·64; 95 % CI -0·28, 3·57) and free testosterone (β = 1·43; 95 % CI -0·21, 3·08). Higher HEI-2020 scores were associated with higher free estradiol (β = 2·46 pg/mL; 95 % CI 0·85, 4·07). Across twenty-one studies, healthier dietary patterns were generally associated with lower estradiol and higher concentrations of SHBG and total testosterone. Taken together, the individual-level analyses and systematic review suggest that anti-inflammatory, low-insulinaemic and overall healthy dietary patterns are associated with more favourable sex steroid hormone profiles in men, although prospective studies are needed to establish temporality.

articles.title: Effects of Weight-Loss Diets on Circulating MicroRNA Profiles in Overweight and Obese Adults: Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.
articles.authors: Natália Ellen Delmicon, Helen Cristina Vidal, Paula Nascimento Brandão-Lima et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Obesity, particularly visceral adiposity, is associated with metabolic inflammation and increased cardiometabolic risk. Dietary interventions are essential for weight loss and improved metabolic health; however, individual responses vary widely. Circulating microRNAs are key epigenetic mediators of metabolic adaptation, although their variable expression patterns often preclude a unified biological interpretation. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aims to synthesize evidence on how weight-loss diets affect the circulating microRNA profile in adults with overweight or obesity. DATA SOURCES: PubMed Central, LILACS, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Google Scholar were searched without language or publication date restrictions through May 2026. DATA EXTRACTION: Of 4383 records identified, 12 articles representing 9 independent randomized clinical trials met the eligibility criteria. Data on study characteristics, dietary interventions, and circulating microRNA expression profiles were extracted. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. DATA ANALYSIS: The included studies were conducted in 6 countries and evaluated dietary interventions lasting 2-18 months. A total of 32 distinct circulating microRNAs were differentially expressed, with miR-221-3p, miR-223, miR-99b, miR-122, and miR-128 reported in more than one study. Considerable heterogeneity was observed among the dietary protocols, particularly regarding macronutrient composition. Alterations in microRNA expression were associated with weight loss, adiposity, glycemic parameters, lipid profile, inflammation, and cardiovascular risk. Bioinformatic analyses indicated enrichment of pathways related to inflammation, insulin signaling, and lipid metabolism, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK pathways, suggesting an integrated role for these microRNAs in metabolic regulation. CONCLUSION: Weight-loss diets modulate the circulating miRNA profile, potentially influencing glycolipid metabolism and inflammation, supporting their role as candidate biomarkers. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD42024580048.

articles.title: How Plants Feed Our Microbes: Plant-Based Diets and Gut Microbiota Modulation-A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Paulina Kozłowska, Alicja Borowiecka, Martyna Strzemkowska et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Diet is a key factor shaping gut microbiota composition and function, with important implications for human health. The growing popularity of plant-based dietary patterns has increased interest in their effects on the gut microbiota. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review examines specific changes in gut microbiota among individuals following a plant-based diet (PBD), as well as shifts occurring after transitioning from an omnivorous diet. DATA SOURCES: PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for articles reporting original English-language human and animal studies investigating the effects of PBDs on gut microbiota composition or function. Studies published from 2015 onward were primarily considered, with most included articles published during 2020-2024. DATA EXTRACTION: Four reviewers independently screened records according to eligibility criteria and extracted data on study characteristics, populations, dietary patterns, and outcomes related to gut microbiota composition and function. DATA ANALYSIS: A total of 37 studies met the inclusion criteria. A PBD appeared to promote the growth of short-chain fatty acid-producing and probiotic bacteria, which help maintain intestinal integrity and support carbohydrate metabolism and may offer protection against certain diseases. A PBD was also reported to encourage the growth of beneficial taxa such as Roseburia spp., Akkermansia muciniphila, Clostridium symbiosum, and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, which are considered indicators of a healthy microbiome. An increased Bacteroidetes/Firmicutes ratio, which was found to be a common occurrence in study participants following a PBD, correlated with a lower body mass index (BMI) and a more favorable metabolic profile, supporting healthy weight maintenance. In addition, PBDs were also associated with improvements in alpha- and beta-diversity compared with omnivorous diets. CONCLUSIONS: This review indicates that PBDs appear to beneficially influence the gut microbiota and may have positive effects on human health. Nonetheless, not all studies agree on the extent or direction of microbiota changes associated with dietary patterns. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [CRD420251229407]; link: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251229407.

articles.title: Understanding the Complexity of Athlete Sleep: A Systems Approach to Modelling the Athlete Sleep Environment.
articles.authors: Matthew Morrison, Shona L Halson, Carissa L Gardiner et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Athlete sleep can be disrupted by sport- and non-sport-related factors. However, the interactions of these sleep-related factors are not well understood. Systems science approaches, such as causal loop diagramming (CLD), provide an opportunity to map these interactions. This project aimed to (1) develop a CLD of the athlete sleep system describing the interacting variables, (2) identify feedback loops and potential leverage points to optimise athlete sleep, and (3) demonstrate the applicability of a CLD to guide the development of a sleep monitoring framework. METHODS: A systems-based model of athlete sleep was developed using CLD, informed by existing literature and refined through a consensus process involving ten subject matter experts (nine from Australia, one from the USA). The model was then interrogated using network analysis to identify key variables based on their position and connectivity within the system. These findings informed the development of a generic sleep monitoring framework. RESULTS: The CLD comprised 48 variables and 120 relationships across four domains: travel demands, behavioural and lifestyle factors, athlete condition and readiness, and resourcing and scheduling constraints. Overall, 12 key variables were identified, with hours of travel, number of time zones crossed, dose of caffeine, and amount of resources or expenditure available being the most connected upstream variables. Level of pre-sleep arousal, sleep opportunity, travel fatigue, and level of performance received the greatest number of incoming relationships, representing points at which multiple pathways converge. Physical condition, level of performance, quality of diet, and importance of competition most frequently linked different quadrants of the system. These variables informed a three-tier monitoring framework capturing upstream determinants and downstream consequences of sleep. CONCLUSIONS: According to the CLD, sleep health in athletes extends beyond an individual behaviour issue and is influenced by the structure and functioning of sport systems. Interactions among travel demands, physical readiness, behavioural and lifestyle factors, and organisational constraints sustain athlete sleep health over time. Consequently, meaningful improvements in sleep health are likely to arise from both system-level interventions and individual behaviour change strategies.

articles.title: Exercise-induced mitochondrial remodelling: Breaking apart to rebuild.
articles.authors: Lucas Esposito Dos Santos, Andressa Crystine da Silva Sobrinho, Guilherme da Silva Rodrigues et al.

articles.title: Higher Quantity and Diversity of Dietary Bioactive Pigments Are Associated with Lower All-Cause Mortality.
articles.authors: Zhiyu Huang, Kelin Zhao, Wei Chen et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Although higher intakes of specific subclasses of dietary bioactive pigments are associated with lower all-cause mortality, the associations of total pigment intake and dietary diversity with mortality risk remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: The aim of the study was to examine associations of the quantity and diversity of total dietary bioactive pigment with all-cause mortality. METHODS: To address this, we prospectively analyzed 4,596 participants from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) followed for a mean of 7.5 years. Using Shannon entropy converted to Hill's effective numbers, we quantified pigment diversity. Multivariable Cox models estimated mortality hazard ratios (HRs). RESULTS: During 34,583 person-years of follow-up, 717 deaths were identified. Both higher pigment quantity (HRQ5vs.Q1 = 0.63; 95% CI: 0.48 to 0.81; P-trend = 0.002) and greater diversity (HRQ5vs.Q1: 0.64; 95% CI: 0.49 to 0.82; P-trend < 0.001) were associated after mutual adjustment with lower mortality. These pigments were primarily derived from tea, apples or pears, berries, peaches or plums, and dark chocolate. Regarding specific subclasses, higher proanthocyanidin intake was associated with a lower mortality risk. CONCLUSIONS: This study extends an established diversity framework to dietary bioactive pigments and shows that both quantity and diversity of dietary bioactive pigment are inversely associated with mortality risk.

articles.title: Effects of footwear bending stiffness on direction-specific functional base of support in healthy older adults.
articles.authors: Paula S Kramer, Kota Z Takahashi, Jason R Franz et al.
articles.abstract: Less than 30 % of the anatomical footprint is typically available for balance control, and this available area, known as the functional base of support (fBoS), can decrease with age. In older adults, smaller fBoS values are associated with a higher risk of falls. Because the strength of intrinsic foot muscles can influence the fBoS, we hypothesized that increasing footwear bending stiffness may similarly increase the fBoS. Twenty-one healthy older adults (70 ± 6 years, 10F/11 M) provided informed consent. Participants "leaned as far as you can with both feet together in one of four directions (forward, backward, right, left) without stepping". Heels, toes, and feet could lift freely to allow full ankle motion. Footwear stiffness was manipulated using standardized shoes (S00), S00 with a 1.6 mm carbon-fiber insole (S16), and S00 with a 3.2 mm carbon-fiber insole (S32). The directional fBoS was defined using the minimum distance between the maximum excursion of the center of pressure and direction-specific foot boundary landmarks. There were no differences in fBoS between S00 and S16 (all p-values > 0.05) or between S00 and S32 (all p-values > 0.145). Contrary to our hypotheses, no detectable immediate group-level effect of footwear bending stiffness was observed, suggesting that increasing footwear bending stiffness alone does not fully explain a mechanism underlying decreased fBoS with aging.
