articles.title: The So-Called "Vastus Lateralis Obliquus" is the Most Distal Part of the Vastus Intermedius.
articles.authors: Takafumi Ono, Mio Imai, Yuto Kawasaki et al.
articles.abstract: The vastus lateralis (VL) has long been described as comprising a longitudinal part (vastus lateralis longus, VLL) and an oblique part (vastus lateralis obliquus, VLO), the latter inserting onto the superolateral border of the patella and traditionally regarded as a component of the VL that stabilizes the patella laterally. However, the anatomical relationship between the VLO and the remainder of the VL has never been rigorously defined, and electromyographic studies have independently regarded the muscle belly emerging at the distolateral thigh as the "superficial region of the vastus intermedius (VI)." To address this discrepancy, we re-examined the structure and innervation of the VLO in five thighs from five embalmed cadavers by gross dissection. The belly conventionally identified as the VLO was present in all specimens and inserted onto the superolateral patella. When the VLL was reflected, this belly was continuous with the VI, which arose broadly from the anterior surface of the femoral shaft; thus, the VLO was the most distal portion of the VI protruding lateral to the lateral border of the VL. Consistently, this region was supplied by the terminal twigs of the lateral branch of the VI (femoral nerve), whereas the branch to the VL did not reach it. We conclude that the so-called VLO is not part of the VL but the distal part of the VI. This reinterpretation reconciles the anatomical convention with electromyographic findings and has implications for anatomical nomenclature, interpretation of VI surface electromyography, and understanding the traction source in painful bipartite patella.

articles.title: Transient gait instability during the initial phase of the 6-minute walk test in people with stroke: A nonlinear analysis using inertial measurement units.
articles.authors: Yasuhiro Inui, Yusaku Takamura, Shu Morioka
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In people with stroke (PwS), reduced gait speed and trunk acceleration changes in the latter half of the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) have been reported as fatigue-related, but temporal changes in motor control remain understudied. Clinicians often observe instability immediately after gait onset, yet quantitative evidence is scarce. This study used inertial measurement units (IMUs) and nonlinear analysis to examine fatigue-related changes and post-onset instability during the 6MWT in PwS. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 19 PwS and 19 age-matched controls completed the 6MWT wearing IMUs at the L5 vertebra and both ankles. Spatiotemporal parameters and stability indices (root mean square, harmonic ratio, sample entropy, short-term Lyapunov exponent [sLE]) were calculated. Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) analyzed the 6-minute period both continuously and by comparing an initial phase (first 60 s) with the subsequent phase. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses were also performed. RESULTS: Continuous-time LMMs showed reduced cadence and increased double-support ratio in PwS. Among stability indices, only mediolateral sLE (sLE-ML) showed a significant group × phase interaction: increasing in the initial phase in PwS but not in controls. Bayesian and sensitivity analyses confirmed this finding was robust and specific to the 60-second cutoff. Initial-phase sLE-ML correlated negatively with Fugl-Meyer lower-extremity scores. CONCLUSIONS: PwS showed fatigue-related gait changes during the 6MWT, while mediolateral local dynamic stability transiently declined during the first 60 s before stabilizing. This instability was associated with motor paralysis, suggesting trunk IMU-based sLE-ML may reveal motor control deficits not captured by walking distance or speed.

articles.title: Left anterior laryngeal loop of the common carotid artery in a cluster of bilateral cervicothoracic vascular variants: a case report.
articles.authors: Viviana Dincă, Adelina Maria Jianu, Mugurel Constantin Rusu
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The common carotid artery (CCA) normally ascends in the carotid sheath, posterolateral to the larynx and trachea. Anterior or pretracheal CCA courses are rare and have been described mainly on the right, usually in relation to a high-riding brachiocephalic trunk (BCT) or another arch-level anomaly. We report a CTA case with a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk, a high-riding BCT and bilateral carotid redundancy, including a left anterior laryngeal CCA loop. METHODS: Computed tomography angiography (CTA) of the aortic arch and bilateral carotid systems was reviewed using multiplanar reformatting and three-dimensional volume-rendered reconstruction. Vessel loops, branching points and relationships to the hyoid-laryngeal framework, thyroid gland and adjacent skeletal landmarks were recorded. RESULTS: CTA showed a common-origin left CCA-BCT trunk with a high-riding BCT measuring 3.27 cm. The right CCA formed a 1.79 cm lateral loop and bifurcated posterolateral to the hyoid-laryngeal framework; the right external carotid artery (ECA) gave rise to a linguofacial trunk and then formed a retromandibular loop. The left CCA formed a 2.15 cm intramediastinal loop and a 1.75 cm anterior laryngeal loop. The left superior thyroid artery arose directly from the CCA. The left ECA showed independent branching and a retromandibular loop. Tortuosity indices ranged from 33.1% to 92.7%; all segments were tortuous and the right internal carotid artery additionally formed a kink (apex angle 87.3°). CONCLUSION: This case documents a rare left anterior laryngeal CCA loop in association with bilateral carotid and external carotid branching variants. The left-sided anterior loop is the main surgical finding because it brings a major cervical artery close to the anterior laryngeal operative field. Recognition of this pattern is relevant before front-of-neck airway access, thyroid surgery, laryngotracheal surgery and central neck procedures.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of Food Swap Interventions Used in Grocery Store Settings.
articles.authors: Helena Bentil, Edward Hillier, Oliver Huse et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Food swap interventions provide an approach to influence consumer food choices. However, evidence on their design and effectiveness has not yet been synthesized. OBJECTIVE: This review systematically synthesized the literature on food swap interventions in grocery settings by addressing the following questions: (1) What were the key characteristics of the food swap interventions examined in the literature, and what was their intended purpose? (2) Have food swap interventions been effective in changing behavior? DATA SOURCES, EXTRACTION, AND ANALYSIS: A search of MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science up to January 23, 2025, was conducted to identify food swap intervention trials in grocery settings, with no limits on language or publication year. Covidence was used to screen titles, abstracts, and full-text articles in duplicate. Data were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Eleven studies, published during 2006-2024, were included in the review. One intervention was implemented in a real grocery store, 3 in real online supermarkets, and 7 in simulated online supermarkets. Most included studies targeted adults with primary or partial responsibility for their household grocery shopping. All the swaps offered healthier alternatives to selected products. Outcomes examined included shopping basket item healthiness, energy content, saturated fatty acid (SFA) content, salt density, and sodium and sugar content. All but 1 study noted evidence that the studied interventions can change behavior. Two studies found significant improvements in overall nutritional quality. Salt/sodium reductions were seen in 2 studies, while reductions in sugar content were seen in 1 study but not in another study. Studies also demonstrated significant reductions in purchased energy content/density, and SFA. CONCLUSION: A range of food swap interventions have been studied, and most of those identified have been found to be effective in improving the healthiness of food purchases. No studies explored the potential of swap interventions to promote sustainable food choices, which could be a topic of future research. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [CRD42024539803].

articles.title: Impact of minimally processed versus milled whole grains on glycaemic control in type 2 diabetes: A 12-week randomised trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Andrew N Reynolds, Fiona Hood, Ella Iosua et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whole grains are widely promoted within a healthy diet, with dietary advice encouraging the replacement of refined grains with whole grains. However, data from small trials indicates that milling or processing whole grains may influence the glycaemic response. OBJECTIVE: To identify if clinically relevant HbA1c differs with processed (milled) or less processed (unmilled) whole grain intakes in type 2 diabetes management. METHODS: We conducted a 12-week randomised parallel trial in adults with type 2 diabetes. Participants received free and delivered whole grain foods that differed in degree of processing. Each intervention was of four foods from whole grain wheat, rice, and oats, in sufficient amounts (4.5-9kg per fortnight) to accommodate family size. Participants were advised to replace the grain foods they normally consumed with the provided products. The primary outcome was glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c). All analyses were performed using an intention-to-treat approach, with outcome variables investigated using a generalised linear model. RESULTS: 160 adults with type 2 diabetes (mean age 58.5 ± 11.5 years; BMI 33.7 ± 7.3 kg/m2; HbA1c 56.4 ± 14.3 mmol/mol) were randomised, with 143 (89%) providing end-of-intervention blood samples. HbA1c was lower following the less processed whole grain intervention compared with the more processed whole grain intervention (mean difference -2.2 mmol/mol, 95% CI -4.2, -0.1), despite no change observed in body weight between interventions. Whole grain, refined grain, and nutrient intakes did not differ between groups, with intervention foods providing approximately 20% of dietary energy. Among the secondary or exploratory outcomes, improvements were indicated only in self-reported bowel habits with less processed whole grains. CONCLUSIONS: Less processed whole grain foods were associated with improved glycated haemoglobin compared with more processed whole grain foods in adults with type 2 diabetes. These findings indicate that the degree of grain processing influences metabolic outcomes, support food reformulation, and distinguishing between refined grains, milled whole grains (wholemeal), and intact whole grains in dietary guidance, food marketing and labelling. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NUMBER AND WEBSITE WHERE IT WAS OBTAINED: ACTRN12622000060741.

articles.title: Almonds and the optimization of immune responses to influenza vaccination, compared to a control snack, in healthy adults: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Alice van der Schoot, Alice C Creedon, Noa Argomaniz et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Certain nutrient supplements enhance immune responses to vaccination; however, no randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have assessed the impact of a whole food. Almonds may benefit immune function through immunoregulatory nutrients and fiber, which interacts with the immune system via the gut microbiota. OBJECTIVE: This study assessed the effect of almonds on the immune response following influenza vaccination, compared to an isocaloric snack, in healthy adults. METHODS: In this RCT, healthy adults (40-64 years) consumed almonds (56 g/d) or an isocaloric control (86 g/d pretzels) for 8 weeks. Participants received seasonal influenza vaccine at week 4. The primary outcome was seroconversion rates for ≥1 strain at week 8. Antigen-specific antibody titers (HI assay) were quantified pre- (week 4) and post-vaccination (week 8), and seroconversion and seroprotection were calculated. The gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), stool output and gut symptoms were measured at baseline, midpoint and endpoint. RESULTS: Ninety participants were randomized (mean age 51 years, 73% females). Seroconversion rate for ≥1 strain was high and not significantly different between groups [almond: 38/41 (93%) versus control: 37/39 (95%), P=1.000], nor were strain-specific seroconversion or seroprotection rates. Almonds resulted in higher antibody titers for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) strain, compared to control [geometric mean (95% CI): almond 359 (146, 881) versus control 110 (51, 235)], and greater fold-change for A/Wisconsin/67/2022 (H1N1) [geometric mean fold change (95% CI): almond 18 (7, 48) versus control 4 (3, 7)] and B/Yamagata [almond 10 (6, 16) versus control 5 (3, 7)]. Absolute abundance of Roseburia hominis was significantly higher in the almond group compared to control (q=0.049). There was no effect on SCFAs or stool consistency. CONCLUSIONS: Almonds increased influenza vaccine antibody titers but did not affect seroconversion in a healthy population where vaccines are already highly effective. This trial was pre-registered at clinicaltrials.gov as NCT05515263 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05515263).

articles.title: Non-recurrent laryngeal nerve with dual branch pattern and merging: a rare anatomical variant encountered during right hemithyroidectomy.
articles.authors: Badriya Yussuf, Haissan Iftikhar
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The non-recurrent laryngeal nerve (NRLN) is an uncommon anatomical variant that passes directly from the vagus nerve to the larynx without the usual recurrent loop; it occurs on the right side in around one in a hundred individuals and is considerably rarer on the left. Its recognition is central to safe thyroid surgery, because an unanticipated NRLN lies in an unexpected position and is vulnerable to inadvertent injury. We report a right non-recurrent laryngeal nerve with an unusual dual-branch morphology in which the nerve divided and then re-merged before laryngeal entry. CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her 50s underwent right hemithyroidectomy for a benign, compressive multinodular goitre of the right lobe. Intraoperatively, no recurrent laryngeal nerve was found in the expected tracheo-oesophageal groove; systematic tracing of the vagus nerve within the carotid sheath revealed a right NRLN that divided into a superior and an inferior branch. The two branches followed separate courses and re-merged into a single trunk approximately 10 mm before entering the larynx through the cricothyroid membrane. Both branches were identified and preserved. The patient was extubated uneventfully, demonstrated normal vocal cord function, and made an uncomplicated recovery with no voice change at early or later follow-up. CONCLUSION: Dual-branch NRLN in which the branches re-merge before laryngeal entry is a pattern we have not found previously described; while extra-laryngeal division of a non-recurrent nerve has been reported, the subsequent re-merging adds complexity to nerve identification and preservation. Awareness that a non-recurrent nerve may branch and re-merge should prompt complete tracing of every fascicle followed from the vagus during thyroid surgery.

articles.title: Suction-feeding performance in invasive alien giant salamanders within the functional framework of Andrias.
articles.authors: M López-Pachón, S Hayashi, J Fortuny et al.
articles.abstract: Hybridisation between Andrias japonicus and A. cf. davidianus lineages is a major conservation concern in Japan, but whether hybrid individuals retain the suction-feeding pattern described for non-hybrid Andrias remains unclear. We analysed suction feeding in six hybrid giant salamanders using 20 captive feeding events recorded with lateral and frontal high-speed videography. Skull, lower jaw, hyobranchial and prey movements were digitised to quantify trajectories, velocities and accelerations during the active expansion phase of prey capture. The hybrids displayed the characteristic suction-feeding sequence described for cryptobranchids, including mandibular opening, hyobranchial expansion, prey acceleration and capture once suction was initiated. Event-level variation occurred in relation to prey position, attack configuration and individual morphometrics, highlighting the flexibility of suction feeding performance among hybrid specimens. Overall, hybrid specimens retained suction-feeding kinematics within the functional pattern previously described for Andrias, suggesting that hybridisation does not disrupt the core biomechanical organisation of prey capture within the functional range examined here. When compared with published data for non-hybrid A. davidianus and A. japonicus, these results indicate a broadly conserved suction feeding mechanism rather than a distinct hybrid-specific feeding mode. Therefore, any potential ecological advantage of hybrids is unlikely to result from a fundamental change in the suction feeding sequence alone.

articles.title: Effect of Pain Science Education and Behavioral Graded Activity on Pain in Survivors of Breast Cancer: A Study Protocol for a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Astrid Lahousse, Eva Roose, Laurence Leysen et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Pain affects up to half of survivors of breast cancer and is one of the most common long-term consequences of cancer treatment, yet it remains under-recognized and undertreated. Pharmacological options often provide limited relief and may cause adverse effects. Evidence from other pain populations supports a biopsychosocial approach combining pain education and physical activity. OBJECTIVE: The objective is to evaluate whether pain science education (PSE) with behavioral graded activity (BGA) versus usual care (UC), reduces pain intensity and interference in survivors of breast cancer with pain. Secondary aims include assessing health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and central pain modulation. DESIGN: This study is a multicenter, two-arm, assessor- and statistician-blinded, randomized controlled superiority trial. SETTING: The trial will be conducted in Belgium, with interventions delivered in hospital and academic research settings. PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred women with a history of breast cancer and persistent pain will be recruited. INTERVENTIONS: Participants will be randomized to either (1) PSE (1 session) plus 5 BGA sessions delivered by a trained physical therapist, or (2) usual care with a standardized biomedical pain information leaflet, over a 12-week period. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome will be pain intensity and interference (Brief Pain Inventory). Secondary outcomes will include HRQoL (EORTC QLQ-C30) and central pain modulation (Quantitative Sensory Testing). Exploratory outcomes include sleep, fatigue, pain-related cognitions, and health care utilization. Assessments will be conducted at baseline, post-intervention, and at 3-month (primary endpoint), 1-year, and 2-year follow-ups. CONCLUSIONS: This trial will determine whether a structured PSE+BGA program improves pain and HRQoL in survivors of breast cancer, offering a potential scalable non-pharmacological treatment. RELEVANCE: These findings may guide targeted rehabilitation strategies and strengthen the role of physical therapists in managing post-cancer pain, particularly in light of the growing population of survivors of breast cancer and the increasing prevalence of persistent symptoms.

articles.title: Critical appraisal of D3-creatine dilution method for skeletal muscle mass measurement.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Sri Lakshmi S Devarakonda, Carla M Prado, Steven B Heymsfield
articles.abstract: The D3-creatine dilution method is gaining rapid momentum as a tool for quantifying skeletal muscle mass (SMM), with emerging discourse positioning it as a reference standard and influencing peer-review and funding decisions. A critical appraisal of the method's current stage of development is therefore timely and necessary. We reviewed the current D3-creatine dilution method as now widely applied, its foundational assumptions, available validation studies comparing estimates against magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and sources of measurement error, including variability in the assumed skeletal muscle creatine concentration and isotope spillage correction. Only 4 studies with 102 total adult participants varying in sex (78 males), age, activity level (49 athletes), and health status have evaluated the current D3-creatine dilution SMM prediction model against MRI as the reference; mean group differences ranged from -13.8% to 20.9%, lending scant support for the validity of the current approach. The one longitudinal validation study (n = 14) reported wide limits of agreement, ±7 kg for D3-creatine compared with ±1.5 kg for MRI, raising concerns about the method's sensitivity to detect small changes in SMM. Isotope spillage correction algorithms, developed in 1 sample (n = 36), similarly require additional development and validation. Although D3-creatine dilution has potential as a new approach that can add to the multiple currently available SMM estimation methods, characterization as a reference standard for quantifying SMM is premature. Validation studies across well-defined cross-sectional and longitudinal samples varying widely in sex, age, diet, and health characteristics are needed to establish the D3-creatine dilution method's accuracy and generalizability.

articles.title: Use of Botanical Ingredients Relevant to Premenstrual Symptoms and Dysmenorrhea Among Elite Female Athletes: Evidence from Doping Control Forms.
articles.authors: Dominika Granda, Andrzej Pokrywka, Maria Karolina Szmidt et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and dysmenorrhea can impair training performance in female athletes. Botanical ingredients are commonly used to manage these conditions in the general population, but it is unknown whether elite female athletes do so. This study aimed to identify botanical ingredients evaluated in studies for PMS and dysmenorrhea and determine whether elite female athletes declared them on Doping Control Forms (DCFs). METHODS: A narrative literature review was conducted to identify botanical ingredients evaluated in studies for PMS and dysmenorrhea. Then, DCFs completed during routine anti-doping testing among elite athletes in Poland (2018-2023) were analyzed for declarations of these ingredients, both directly and as components of multi-ingredient products. The proportion of DCFs containing these ingredients was compared between female (n = 4451 DCFs) and male athletes (n = 9068 DCFs; reference) using chi-squared tests. RESULTS: The review identified 8 and 21 botanical ingredients with evidence for PMS and dysmenorrhea, respectively; of which 9 were detected in DCFs. The most commonly declared ingredients among female athletes were ginger and turmeric/curcuminoid (1.75% and 1.26%, respectively, both studied for PMS and dysmenorrhea). Chasteberry, on the other hand, with the most extensive, albeit low-confidence evidence, for PMS, was rarely declared (0.22%). Direct declaration of ginkgo, valerian, evening primrose oil, and chasteberry was significantly more common among female than male athletes (0.22% vs. 0.02%, 0.36% vs. 0.03%, 0.47% vs. 0.03%, 0.22% vs. 0.02%; adjusted p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Declarations of botanical ingredients studied for PMS and dysmenorrhea were infrequent on DCFs completed by female athletes. Because DCFs do not record the reason for use, these data cannot establish whether declarations reflected treatment of menstrual symptoms; studies assessing indication, symptom status and motivation are needed.

articles.title: Comparing the coherent point drift algorithm to sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic whole-bone three-dimensional shape analyses.
articles.authors: Christine M Harper, Isabella F X Araiza, Deanna M Goldstein
articles.abstract: The ability to quantify 3D morphologies is critical for anatomical research; however, setting up high-density landmark sets and positioning them on all specimens can represent a substantial challenge. The coherent point drift (CPD) algorithm, a technique for registering two point clouds based on the Gaussian mixture model, was recently used to investigate human variation; however, its performance has yet to be compared to other 3D shape analysis methods. Here we compare the results of a CPD analysis to a sliding semilandmark and weighted spherical harmonic (SPHARM) analysis of the same 60 human and African ape calcanei and a CPD analysis and SPHARM-sliding analysis (a combination SPHARM and sliding semilandmark analysis) of 40 primate third manual proximal phalanges (mPP3s) to determine methodological comparability. Additionally, we run a CPD analysis on a small but wide-ranging sample of primate ulnae to demonstrate its utility for proximodistally long and mediolaterally narrow long bones. All specimens were surface or micro-CT scanned. All calcanei were subjected to a CPD analysis with 2000 semilandmarks, a sliding semilandmark analysis with 1007 semilandmarks, and a SPHARM analysis. All mPP3s underwent a CPD analysis with 2500 semilandmarks and a SPHARM-sliding analysis with 2562 semilandmarks. For the ulna, a CPD analysis with 1252 semilandmarks was run. Shape variation for all analyses was summarized using (separate) principal component analyses (PCAs). Results of the respective analyses for the calcaneus and mPP3 were compared by calculating the maximum and root mean square distances (RMSD) between average taxon shape configurations (scaled based on centroid size) generated from each analysis. All three calcaneus analyses separate taxa along the first two PCs, with humans separating from African apes along PC1 and chimpanzees and gorillas separating across PC2. For the two mPP3 analyses, the three great ape taxa consistently separate along PC1, and Papio separates from the other taxa along PC2. The average RMSD between CPD and sliding semilandmark analyses for the calcaneus was 0.24 mm, and 0.21 mm between CPD and SPHARM analyses. For the mPP3, the average RMSD between CPD and SPHARM-sliding was 0.14 mm. These results indicate that CPD is a comparable 3D shape analysis method to these other approaches. The CPD analysis was also able to place a semilandmark set on primate ulnae ranging from gorillas to tarsiers and capture morphological variations including shaft curvature, relative olecranon process length, and overall robusticity. CPD analyses are less time intensive than sliding semilandmark analyses; however, the sliding semilandmark analysis was better able to capture variation surrounding the borders of the articular facets (although differences were relatively minor), suggesting that these analyses may be better suited when the researcher is interested in a specific anatomical feature. CPD did capture edges better than SPHARM analyses; however, this is likely not an issue for small, relatively round bones such as carpals and most tarsals. In sum, CPD produces similar results to sliding semilandmark, SPHARM, and SPHARM-sliding approaches and has benefits for analyses of long bones with complex morphologies or among taxa that exhibit large amounts of morphological variation.

articles.title: The NHANES WIC Impact Index is a Valid Measure of WIC's Impact on Children.
articles.authors: Meghan Zimmer, Cindy W Leung, Cristina M Gago et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) provides food benefits, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and referrals to social and medical services. However, WIC's impact on children is often evaluated using isolated dietary or health outcomes, and no validated tool exists to measure WIC's multidimensional impact across all program services. OBJECTIVES: We developed and validated the NHANES WIC Impact Index using cross-sectional data from the 2007-2010 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). The index captures the four domains targeted by WIC: dietary intake, nutrition literacy, breastfeeding practices, and social/medical service access. METHODS: Reliability was assessed using item-item correlations and Cronbach's alpha. Validity assessments included content validity via expert consultation and policy mapping; criterion validity of the dietary domain compared with the Healthy Eating Index-2020 (HEI-2020); discriminant validity using known-groups analyses by WIC participation status; and divergent validity by Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation. RESULTS: Reliability was demonstrated through item-item correlations that supported the internal structure of the index domains, and low internal consistency (α = 0.32 to 0.33) as expected for a multidimensional index. The dietary domain was moderately correlated with HEI-2020 scores (r = 0.58), demonstrating criterion validity. Among WIC-eligible children, prior participants scored 2.2 points lower on the index [-2.2 (95% CI: -3.9, -0.5), P<0.05] than current participants, but current participants and nonparticipants (i.e., never enrolled) scored similarly (P>0.05). Scores were not predicted by SNAP participation status (P>0.05), supporting divergent validity. CONCLUSION: The NHANES WIC Impact Index is a reliable and valid measure for evaluating WIC's impact on four domains of child health targeted by WIC. This index enables assessment of WIC's holistic impact and may support future surveillance and policy evaluation research.

articles.title: From compartments to dynamic physiology: toward actionable body composition.
articles.authors: Karl E Friedl, Adam W Potter, Jennifer L Miles-Chan et al.
articles.abstract: The 12th International Symposium on In Vivo Body Composition Studies (ISBCR 2025) highlighted a fundamental transition from estimating static tissue compartments to dynamic physiological phenotyping, actionable interpretation, and demonstrable value for clinical decision-making, health prediction, and human performance assessment. This represents an evolution in technological capability and conceptual framing, as an extension of the Functional Body Composition concept. Classical multicompartment models and established methods such as dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, isotope dilution, bioimpedance, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging remain foundational; however, emerging approaches increasingly integrate advanced imaging, artificial intelligence, bioimpedance spectroscopy, stable isotope methods, wearable sensing, and multidimensional phenotyping. Several themes were prominent at ISBCR 2025, including expansion of imaging beyond traditional DXA paradigms, increasing emphasis on muscle quality and fluid compartments, greater attention to visceral and ectopic adipose tissue, clinical applications in oncology and critical illness, the evaluation of obesity pharmacotherapy, the importance of generalizability to individuals across sex and ethnicity, and data governance. This perspective proposes a framework for future research in which body composition measurements become integral components of predictive models of health, performance, and physiological resilience. Future body composition assessment practices must include demonstrated added value over previous methods, and the greatest advances will come from technologies that bring physiologically meaningful assessment to large populations. The success of future technologies should be judged less by how precisely they estimate tissue compartments than by how effectively they improve physiological understanding, prediction, and decision-making.

articles.title: Oxidative balance and cognitive function in Chinese older adults: the mediating role of plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
articles.authors: Kangting Luo, Rui Li, Qian Guo et al.
articles.abstract: Rapid global ageing is increasing the burden of cognitive impairment. Oxidative stress may contribute to cognitive decline, and the oxidative balance score (OBS), which integrates dietary and lifestyle pro- and antioxidants, has an unclear relationship with cognitive function in older adults. This study aimed to investigate the association between the OBS and cognitive function among older adults and to examine potential indirect pathways through circulating oxidative stress-related biomarkers. We used data from 1891 adults aged ≥60 years who participated in the 2011-2014 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE). Oxidative stress markers, including albumin, superoxide dismutase, malondialdehyde and plasma 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], were measured at baseline and follow-up. Associations were examined using mixed-effects linear regression models and semi-longitudinal cross-lagged mediation analysis. The median cognitive score was 28 (interquartile range, 23-29). Each one-point higher OBS was associated with a 0·16-point higher MMSE score (β = 0·16, 95 % CI 0·06 to 0·26), and participants in the highest OBS tertile had a 1·12-point higher MMSE score than those in the lowest tertile (β = 1·12, 95 % CI 0·50 to 1·73). In mediation analysis, higher baseline OBS predicted lower plasma 25(OH)D at follow-up (path a = -1·015), and higher baseline 25(OH)D was associated with better cognitive scores at follow-up (path b = 0·025). The indirect effect of OBS on cognition through 25(OH)D was significant (a × b = -0·025). OBS was positively associated with cognitive function, partially mediated by 25(OH)D. Further research is warranted to clarify these mechanisms and implications for cognitive aging.

articles.title: Mitochondrial content and intrinsic coupling-related differences shape bioenergetic output and redox responses across striated muscles in rats.
articles.authors: Alex Chan, Jules Devaux, Claudia Wen et al.
articles.abstract: Striated muscles differ markedly in energetic demand, but whether mitochondrial respiration and reactive oxygen species emission differ intrinsically across muscle types remains unclear. This study compared mitochondrial respiration, hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) emission and antioxidant enzyme expression in heart, diaphragm and hindlimb skeletal muscle from healthy rats. Mitochondrial O2 flux and H2O2 emission were measured simultaneously using high-resolution respirometry coupled with fluorometry in tissue homogenates subjected to substrate-uncoupler-inhibitor titration protocols. Mitochondrial content was estimated by citrate synthase activity, and antioxidant enzyme expression was measured by immunoblotting. Heart tissue displayed the highest mitochondrial respiration and H2O2 emission when expressed per tissue mass, followed by diaphragm and skeletal muscle. However, normalisation by citrate synthase activity eliminated differences in respiratory flux between muscles, indicating that variations in tissue-level respiration were primarily driven by mitochondrial content. Net H2O2 emission was greatest during leak respiration and decreased during oxidative phosphorylation and uncoupled states in all muscle types. Cardiac mitochondria exhibited a higher H2O2/O2 ratio during leak respiration and higher coupling-related ratios than those of diaphragm and skeletal muscle. In association, cardiac muscle showed greater expression of the mitochondrial antioxidant enzymes superoxide dismutase 2 and catalase in a separate cohort. These findings indicate that absolute oxidative metabolism across striated muscles is largely determined by mitochondrial content, whereas respiratory capacity per mitochondrial unit was conserved. Cardiac muscle exhibits elevated leak-associated reactive oxygen species emission but compensates by enhancing antioxidant defences, highlighting coordination between bioenergetic demand and redox regulation in continuously active muscles.

articles.title: Concurrent electrical and mechanical adaptations of forearm muscles across graded handgrip intensities: Evidence from EMG and myotonometry.
articles.authors: Abdurrahman Tanhan, Merve Tunçdemir, Tülay Çevik Saldıran
articles.abstract: Grip force production depends on coordinated neural activation and intrinsic muscle mechanical properties; however, their concurrent behavior across graded contraction intensities and potential sex-related differences remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined simultaneous changes in surface EMG (sEMG) activity and myotonometry-derived mechanical properties of the flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS) and extensor digitorum (ED) muscles during graded handgrip contractions. Twenty healthy adults (10 women, 10 men) performed isometric grips at rest and at 40 %, 60 %, 80 %, and 100 % of maximal voluntary contraction (MVC). Muscle activation was recorded via surface EMG (RMS), while tone, stiffness, and logarithmic decrement (LD, an inverse index of elasticity) were concurrently assessed using MyotonPRO. Contraction intensity effects were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA, and sex-based comparisons were conducted at each force level. sEMG amplitudes increased progressively with contraction intensity (p < 0.001). Muscle tone and stiffness showed parallel intensity-dependent increases (p < 0.001), whereas LD remained relatively stable. Sex-related differences were limited in sEMG but more evident in mechanical parameters, with males demonstrating higher FDS tone and stiffness and lower LD in the ED muscle (p < 0.05). Increasing grip force induces coordinated neuromuscular activation and mechanical stiffening with parameter-specific responses. Combined sEMG-myotonometric assessment provides an integrated framework for sex-sensitive evaluation of muscle function.

articles.title: Beyond imbalance: an elasticity framework for the distance-averaged force-velocity relationship in vertical jump.
articles.authors: Zhaoqian Li, Mingyu Li, Xing Zhang et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to (1) establish the distance‑averaged F‑V relationship framework and (2) develop elasticity metrics that quantify how F‑V relationship variables govern jump height and inform training decisions. Theoretical derivation and experimental validation across 108 F-V relationship models derived from 1578 jumps (countermovement jump and squat jump at three knee angles; 20 well-trained subjects) yielded a systematic error of - 2.1% and a strong linear association (r = 0.96, 95% CI [0.93; 0.97]) between measured and predicted jump height. Four elasticity metrics were formulated: force elasticity ([Formula: see text]), the elasticity of jump height to maximal force ([Formula: see text]); velocity elasticity ([Formula: see text]), the elasticity of jump height to maximal velocity ([Formula: see text]); the force-velocity elasticity norm [Formula: see text], reflecting the overall sensitivity of jump height to changes in F-V relationship variables; and the force-velocity elasticity ratio [Formula: see text]), indicating which variable dominates the jump height response. Simulations and experiments revealed that [Formula: see text] bore an inverse relationship to [Formula: see text], and [Formula: see text] was inversely related to [Formula: see text], reflecting diminishing marginal returns. At a fixed jump height, simulations showed [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] displayed a U-shaped relationship; a balanced profile ([Formula: see text] = 1) did not always correspond to the lowest [Formula: see text]. The distance-averaged F-V elasticity framework offers a physically grounded and quantitative tool for linking F-V relationship variables directly to jump performance, providing a basis for informing individualized training decisions.

articles.title: Neural, contractile, and muscular determinants associated with lower strength in recreationally active older men: a cross-sectional study.
articles.authors: Ronan Sherman, Mathias Forsberg Brobakken, Ole Kristian Berg et al.
articles.abstract: Skeletal muscle strength declines with age. However, the relative contributions of various neuromuscular factors to this decline appear to not be fully understood. Thus, we compared relative attenuations in key neural and muscular strength determinants with age, in vivo and in vitro, recruiting 22 old (75 ± 1 years) and 18 young (25 ± 1 years) recreationally active men. Leg extension maximal voluntary contraction (MVC), early (0-100 ms) and late (0-200 ms) rate of force development (RFD), were reduced by - 39%, - 55%, and - 49%, respectively, in the old (all p < 0.001); however, estimated thigh cross-sectional area (CSA) was not different between groups. In contrast, efferent neural drive assessed by evoked recordings (m.soleus normalized V-waves; V/Msup), largely dependent on corticospinal factors, revealed a - 72% age-related reduction (p < 0.001). A - 51% reduction was also observed in peripheral motoneuron excitability, measured as Hmax/Mmax at 10% MVC (p < 0.001). The neural age-related decline was confirmed applying peak electromyography (EMG; - 14%), early (- 31%), and late (- 30%; all p < 0.05) rate of EMG rise, during leg extension MVC. While voluntary activation was unaltered with age, quadriceps contractility was reduced (resting twitch: peak force, - 41%; RFD, - 43%; delay, +39%; time-to-relaxation, +56%; all p < 0.01). Biopsies from m.vastus lateralis showed an age-related decrease in proportion, - 16% (type II: 43% (old) vs. 51% (young); p < 0.001), but not size, of fast twitch fibers. Concomitantly, slow twitch fibers were 12% larger in old vs. young (p < 0.05). Collectively, these findings showed that age-related reductions in muscle strength were accompanied by pronounced alterations in neural function alongside changes in muscle phenotype, despite preserved thigh CSA.

articles.title: When intestinal protection does not improve performance: Biological effect vs. functional effect - why this discrepancy?
articles.authors: Regina Eloina Dos Santos Pereira, Michelle Barbosa Rosário, Isabelle Zanata Fabiane

articles.title: Facial artery morphology assessed by computed tomography angiography: a mixed-effects morphometric analysis of age, sex, and laterality.
articles.authors: Sindy Melissa Sanchez-Romo, Adrian Manuel Verdines-Perez, Mario Campos-Coy et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The facial artery is the principal arterial supply to the midface and is among the most frequently encountered vascular structures during facial reconstructive, aesthetic, and minimally invasive procedures. Precise knowledge of its anatomical course and morphometric characteristics is essential to minimize vascular complications. However, previous morphometric studies have largely been descriptive and have rarely accounted for bilateral anatomical correlation or simultaneously evaluated the independent effects of age, sex, and laterality using appropriate multivariable statistical models. METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed using computed tomography angiography (CTA) examinations from 103 adults, yielding 201 evaluable facial arteries. Standardized three-dimensional morphometric measurements were obtained at the inferior border of the mandible and the lateral alar base. Linear mixed-effects models incorporating patient-specific random intercepts were used to evaluate the effects of age, sex, side, and CTA diagnostic category while accounting for within-subject correlation. Measurement reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Bland-Altman analysis, and Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Type III, according to the Furukawa classification, was the predominant anatomical pattern (67.2%). Among 98 patients with bilateral visualization, Furukawa type showed complete right-left concordance (100%; κ = 1.00). In an additional patient-level logistic model, neither age (OR 0.992 per year; 95% CI, 0.965-1.020; P = 0.584) nor female sex (OR 1.793; 95% CI, 0.767-4.191; P = 0.178) was significantly associated with Type III versus Type II. For continuous morphometric variables, no systematic laterality effect was detected, although individual-level bilateral agreement varied across parameters. After Holm correction across morphometric outcomes, women had a smaller facial artery diameter at the inferior border of the mandible and a shorter zygomatic arch-facial artery distance than men, while increasing age was independently associated with a shorter oral commissure-facial artery distance. Quantitative morphometric measurements demonstrated good-to-excellent observer reproducibility (intraobserver ICC: 0.900-0.960; interobserver ICC: 0.760-0.860), whereas categorical assessment of facial artery position relative to the nasolabial sulcus showed perfect intraobserver (κ = 1.00) and substantial interobserver agreement (κ = 0.79). CONCLUSIONS: CTA provides a reproducible morphometric assessment of the facial artery. No systematic laterality effect was identified for continuous morphometric variables, although individual bilateral agreement varied by measurement, while Furukawa type showed complete bilateral concordance in patients with both arteries visualized. Age and sex were not significantly associated with Furukawa Type III versus Type II, but they influenced selected continuous morphometric parameters. These findings characterize facial artery anatomy in a Mexican clinical cohort and may inform individualized anatomical assessment and preprocedural planning; they do not establish procedural risk thresholds.

articles.title: Effects of forkball pitching on forearm flexor-pronator muscle stiffness and grip strength.
articles.authors: Ryota Oshima, Hiroyuki Nunome
articles.abstract: In baseball, the forkball pitch is a highly effective breaking ball. However, its unique grip has been said to place excessive load on the forearm flexor-pronator muscles. This study aimed to clarify and compare the effects of forkball and fastball pitching on the forearm flexor-pronator muscles using shear wave elastography. This interventional study (single group pre- and post-intervention comparison) included eight adult men. For each pitch type, they pitched 25 balls with maximum effort toward a net 3 m away. We assessed shear wave speed, a quantitative metric of muscle stiffness, and handgrip strength before and after the pitching sessions. To verify changes in shear wave speed after isometric exercise, we also implemented an additional isometric grip exercise protocol. Of the forearm flexor-pronator muscles, we found a significant reduction in shear wave speed only in the flexor digitorum superficialis after forkball pitching (0 pitches: 2.43 ± 0.24 m/s vs 25 pitches: 2.10 ± 0.24 m/s; p = 0.004), while there were no significant changes in the forearm flexor-pronator muscles after fastball pitching. Shear wave speed also decreased significantly in the forearm flexor-pronator muscles after the additional isometric grip exercise. The observed reduction in shear wave speed during repeated isometric grip likely reflects transient changes in forearm flexor-pronator muscle stiffness. Similarly, among the forearm flexor-pronator muscles, only the flexor digitorum superficialis showed a significant reduction in shear wave speed after repeated forkball pitching, suggesting that pitching forkball with a unique grip, in which the second and third fingers were spread apart during pitching, placed a specific load on that muscle.

articles.title: Regional Histological Anatomy of the Supraperiosteal Tissues of the Oral Cavity: Implications for Periodontal Flap Surgery and Periosteal Releasing Incisions.
articles.authors: Joe Iwanaga, Norio Kitagawa, Michitsuna Katafuchi et al.
articles.abstract: Periodontal and implant procedures increasingly involve tissue planes superficial to the periosteum, yet their regional anatomy remains poorly understood. This study conducted a histological investigation of the supraperiosteal anatomy of the oral cavity and its implications for periosteal releasing incisions (PRIs). Intraoral dissection of the mimetic muscle was performed using a fresh anatomical donor. Subsequently, maxillary and mandibular incisor, premolar, and molar regions from five formalin-fixed donors were examined histologically using Masson's trichrome staining. Muscular, neural, vascular, and connective tissue structures within 5 mm of the facial alveolar bone surface were evaluated. Supraperiosteal tissue architecture differed markedly by region. Muscular, neural, and vascular structures showed distinct region-specific distributions. The mental nerve and its branches were identified in the mandibular premolar region, whereas facial and buccal vessels were present near the bone surface in the posterior regions. Muscle attachment and intervening connective tissue also varied regionally. Structures potentially injured during PRI and their associated risks are region-dependent. PRI should therefore be guided by region-specific anatomy and the tissues requiring release for sufficient flap mobility rather than by a predetermined incision depth alone.

articles.title: Sex-specific Lower Limb Strength, Flexibility, and Running Biomechanics in Adolescents With and Without Osgood-Schlatter Disease.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Sungwan Kim, Alexandra F DeJong Lempke, Kristin E Whitney et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine sex-specific lower limb strength, flexibility, and running biomechanics in adolescents with and without OSD. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective chart review of 100 adolescents (n=25 each group): females with OSD (age=14.6 ± 1.9 y; body mass index [BMI]=21.3 ± 2.1 kg/m2); males with OSD (age=14.4 ± 1.6 y; BMI=21.7 ± 3.2 kg/m2); females without OSD (age=14.8 ± 2.2 y; BMI=21.7 ± 3.0 kg/m2); and males without OSD (age=14.4 ± 2.2 y; BMI=22.0 ± 4.6 kg/m2). We assessed mass-normalized sagittal and frontal hip strength and sagittal knee strength via hand-held dynamometry, and quadriceps femoris (prone knee flexion) and hip flexor (Thomas test) flexibility. Limb crossover, contralateral pelvic drop [CPD], medial knee displacement, and tibial dominant stride were assessed during treadmill running. Group differences were analyzed using a two-way multivariate analysis of variance (continuous outcomes) and logistic regression (categorical outcomes), covarying for age and BMI. Analyses were performed using SPSS (alpha set at p<0.05). RESULTS: Compared with sex-matched healthy peers, females with OSD had impaired hip abduction strength and a greater propensity for CPD and medial knee displacement, though greater hip flexion strength (p≤0.03; Table). Males with OSD had greater hip and knee sagittal plane strength yet impaired flexibility (p≤0.02; Table). Compared with males with OSD, females with OSD had lower hip and knee strength, greater quadriceps femoris flexibility, and higher odds of frontal plane biomechanical deficits (p≤0.02; Table). CONCLUSION: We observed sex-specific differences in lower limb muscular and biomechanical features in adolescents with OSD, suggesting that clinicians should consider sex-specific rehabilitation strategies for adolescents with OSD.

articles.title: Absorption and Metabolism of Steroidal Alkaloids from Tomato Juice in Healthy Adults: a Pharmacokinetic Study.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Daniel Do, Maria J Sholola, Jessica L Cooperstone
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Steroidal alkaloids may be responsible for some of the health benefits of a tomato rich diet, but little is known about their metabolic fate after consumption. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to elucidate the pharmacokinetic parameters of plasma steroidal alkaloids and to define their bioavailability and metabolism following a single tomato containing meal. METHODS: Healthy subjects (n = 11, 6M/5F) consumed 505 g of tomato juice following a two-week tomato washout and blood plasma were collected post-prandially at 11 time points over 12-hours. Plasma steroidal alkaloids were analyzed using ultra-high performance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. The pharmacokinetic parameters AUC0-12hr, Cmax, and Tmax were calculated using non-compartmental analysis. The quantity of steroidal alkaloids and their metabolites present in plasma were used to calculate a a fractional systemic exposure. Metabolite standards were "bio"-synthesized using the liver microsomes to improve confidence in identification when authentic standards were not available. RESULTS: The fraction of steroidal alkaloids from juice that appeared in plasma intact or as metabolized products was 9.7% ± 5.7% with a range of 2.4-17.9%. Over 99% of steroidal alkaloids present in circulation were metabolized products. The Cmax of total plasma steroidal alkaloids in subjects reached an average 406.5 nmol/L and ranged from 103.7-1145.6 nmol/L. Mean Tmax was 8.9 h (range 6-12 h) and average AUC0-12hr was 2529.0 ± 1644.8 nmol*h/L. Steroidal alkaloids remained above baseline at12 hours so absorption is likely underestimated. Liver S9 enzymatic synthesis of steroidal alkaloid metabolites including trihydroxy-tomatidine and sulfonated dihydroxy-tomatidine improved confidence in compound identification. CONCLUSIONS: This study reports the first pharmacokinetic data for tomato steroidal alkaloids, demonstrating moderate absorption and extensive metabolism after tomato juice consumption. These data provide context for future studies investigating the potential role that these compounds may play in human health. Clinical Trial Registry number and website where it was obtained https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01696773.

articles.title: A dive into the physiological responses to O2- and CO2-tables in freedivers.
articles.authors: Louise Declercq, Sander Lefere, Kasper Van Eetvelde et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Current literature focuses on maximal apneas to improve apnea duration, whereas in practice, apnea training often involves two distinct forms of timed-repeated submaximal apnea protocols: "O2-tables", intended to progressively decrease oxygenation and purportedly train O2 conservation, and "CO2-tables", intended to progressively accumulate carbon dioxide (CO2) and purportedly train hypercapnia tolerance. In apnea novices, O2- and CO2-tables failed to induce strong deoxygenation and CO2 accumulation, respectively. Therefore, the aim of this study was to compare physiological responses to maximal apneas, O2- and CO2-tables in apnea trained individuals. METHODS: After medical screening, fourteen freedivers performed three apnea protocols: maximal apneas, O2-table and CO2-table. During apnea, heart rate (HR), muscle tissue oxygenation index (mTOI) and peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) were measured continuously. End-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) was measured before and after apneas. Capillary partial pressure of CO2 (PCO2) was measured after the fourth and final apnea. Perceived Exertion (RPE) was rated after each protocol. RESULTS: RPE was lower after O2- and CO2-tables than after maximal apneas. Changes in HR and mTOI did not differ between O2- and CO2-tables. CO2-tables elicited greater increases in PCO2 and EtCO2 compared to O2-tables and maximal apneas. Maximal apneas induced greater changes in SpO2 than O2- and CO2-tables. CONCLUSION: These results suggest that, in freedivers, O2- and CO2-tables offer a less mentally and physically demanding alternative to repeated maximal apneas, allowing greater variation in apnea training while still targeting O2 conservation and CO2 tolerance, respectively.

articles.title: Metabolic phenotyping identifies early interindividual variation in infant energy expenditure with implications for obesity risk.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: Emily W Flanagan, Abby D Altazan, Leanne M Redman
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pediatric obesity is a major public health crisis. Early identification of metabolic traits that increase individual risk are emerging. As such, identification of variability in early energy expenditure would reveal the need for precision nutritional approaches from birth. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the interindividual variability in components of energy expenditure for the purpose of understanding early nutritional considerations in very young infants. METHODS: Infant participants (<3 months of age) underwent extensive energy expenditure phenotyping using a combination of doubly labeled water for total daily energy expenditure and a novel infant metabolic chamber for sleeping energy expenditure. Descriptive statistics, intraclass correlation coefficients, and univariable and multivariable linear regression analyses were used to assess reliability and characterize variability, predictors, and phenotypes of energy expenditure. We identified interindividual variability in total, mass-adjusted, and fat-free mass adjusted energy expenditures. Energy phenotypes (thrifty and spendthrift) were assigned based on the residuals between measured and predicted energy expenditure from metabolic mass. Discrepancies between measured energy expenditure and predicted by national dietary recommendations for infants (2023 DRI) were evaluated. RESULTS: Total daily and sleeping energy expenditures were 368±60 kcal/d and 250±60 kcal/d, respectively. Energy expenditure related to activity accounted for 21±9% of total measured. Age (r=.59), weight (r=.83), length (r=.75), and fat-free mass (r=.82) were positively associated with sleeping energy expenditure. We identified 40% of measured infants with a thrifty energy phenotype, classified as having sleeping energy expenditure under that predicted by cohort age, sex, and fat and fat-free mass. Mean prediction error of the 2023 DRI from our cohort was 10±7% and was positively associated with the amount of energy expenditure attributed to activity. CONCLUSIONS: These findings warrant further comprehensive metabolic phenotyping studies in young infants to understand how early energy expenditure tracks through the life course and influences obesity risk as well as the thorough evaluation and refinement of infant nutritional recommendations.

articles.title: Large Language Models and Applied Surgical Anatomy: Evaluation of Anatomical Reasoning in Expert-Derived Plastic Surgery Scenarios.
articles.authors: Menekşe Kastamoni Başkan, Süleyman Çeçen, Yadigar Kastamoni
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into medical education, research, and clinical decision-support applications; however, their ability to apply anatomical knowledge in clinically relevant surgical scenarios remains insufficiently studied. This study evaluated and compared the performance of six contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, and Manus) using 25 expert-derived applied surgical anatomy scenarios relevant to plastic surgery. Scenarios were developed by an expert panel consisting of one associate professor of anatomy and two plastic surgeons. Responses were generated using a standardized prompt and assessed with a structured scoring rubric evaluating anatomical accuracy, clinical reasoning, completeness, and safety, with a maximum score of 10 points per question. Critical errors were additionally assessed. Significant differences in overall performance were observed among models (Friedman χ2 = 43.51, p < 0.001). ChatGPT achieved the maximum aggregate score (250/250), followed by Gemini (248/250), DeepSeek (241/250), Copilot (240/250), Claude (235/250), and Manus (219/250). Critical errors were infrequent and were confined to a reconstructive vascular physiology scenario: DeepSeek, Claude, and Manus each demonstrated one observed critical error, whereas ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot demonstrated none. Although all evaluated models demonstrated excellent performance, clinically significant anatomical misconceptions persisted despite high aggregate scores. These findings demonstrate strong performance by the tested LLMs on this specific scenario-based benchmark, while also identifying clinically meaningful anatomical errors in a subset of responses. Future evaluations should focus not only on overall accuracy but also on clinically meaningful error patterns that may influence surgical decision-making. Importantly, substantial ceiling effects limited discrimination among high-performing models, and the findings should therefore be interpreted as performance on this specific benchmark rather than as evidence of a general hierarchy of anatomical reasoning capability.

articles.title: One Carbon Metabolism - The Missing Link for Cancer and Sepsis.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Abigail Anderson, Carter Weeg
articles.abstract: One-carbon (1C) metabolism (OCM) is a biosynthetic and physiological process essential to cells. OCM encompasses a multitude of tightly regulated biochemical reactions that are responsible for nucleotide synthesis (purines and pyrimidines), amino acid homeostasis (Met, Ser, Gly), redox balance, and epigenetic regulation. Dysregulations of this pathway have been implicated in the development and progression of cancer and sepsis - two complex pathologies, each with a characteristically high morbidity and mortality rate. OCM changes in the oncogenic state have been extensively investigated, while metabolic pathway changes in sepsis remain more elusive. Given that emerging evidence suggests that 1 in 5 sepsis hospitalizations occur in patients with a cancer diagnosis, and recovering sepsis patients have a higher incidence of cancer diagnosis, our review aims to analyze the known OCM changes that occur in each pathology, highlight commonalities and variations, and suggest clinical implications that explore possible therapeutic targets. Through a novel cross-disease examination, a more comprehensive understanding of OCM metabolic changes in these disease states could inform clinical practice and lead to the development of targeted therapeutic interventions that further our understanding and treatment of one or both conditions.

articles.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Skeletal Muscle and Cardiometabolic Risk During the Menopause Transition.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Hannah E Cabre, Kaja Falkenhain, Steve R Smith et al.
articles.abstract: We assessed longitudinal changes in body composition and cardiometabolic risk in those with normal-weight and overweight/obese women across the menopausal transition. We examined a 10-year longitudinal analysis of 81 healthy women in the prospective Healthy Transitions cohort. Body composition measures were obtained via dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Skeletal muscle was estimated using a validated prediction model: 1.12 × appendicular lean mass- 0.63. Serum sex steroid hormones and cardiometabolic factors were quantified in fasting blood. Participants were stratified by BMI into normal weight (n=41) and overweight/obesity (n=40) groups. Changes within and between BMI groups across the menopause transition were assessed with linear mixed models. At menopause onset, compared to those with normal weight, participants with overweight/obesity had lower sex hormone-binding globulin (-30.9±10.3 nmol/L; p=0.01), greater percent body fat (13.1±1.3%; p<0.001), greater skeletal muscle mass (2.5±0.6 kg; p<0.001), and worse cardiometabolic risk factors (p<0.001). In the 5 years before menopause, participants with overweight/obesity gained skeletal muscle (+1.2 kg) and fat mass (+3.5 kg), while participants with normal weight increased percent body fat (+1.5%) only. At menopause onset, women with overweight/obesity exhibit distinct alterations in body composition, hormonal profiles, and cardiometabolic risk that exist in the years preceding menopause, highlighting the importance of early, targeted interventions to mitigate adverse health trajectories during the menopause transition.

articles.title: Cardiovascular dietary guidance at an inflection point: the 2025-2030 US dietary guidelines versus the 2026 AHA scientific statement.
articles.authors: Luiz Fernando Sella, Daniela Kanno

articles.title: The impact of work-related foot pain on work and personal life: an interview study.
articles.authors: Ann-Sophie Hörnell, Anncristine Fjellman-Wiklund, Åsa Svedmark et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The occurrence of foot pain is high, especially in those with physically demanding occupations. Work-related foot pain has been shown to impact work performance, family life, and leisure activities. While prevalence across various sectors is documented, research exploring experiences and total life impact of work-related foot pain remains limited. AIM: The aim of this study was to explore experiences of living with foot pain among individuals employed in highly demanding physical occupations, and occupations characterised by prolonged standing or walking. METHODS: A qualitative, semi-structured interview-based approach was chosen. Twelve individual interviews were conducted with nine women and three men, and analysed using Qualitative Content Analysis. RESULTS: One main theme, Walking a fine line - Balancing challenges in multiple aspects of life due to work-related foot pain, and three sub-themes were identified, describing how external work-environment factors and internal experiences of autonomy impact an individual's overall life situation, including impact on family life and the mental toll of living and working with foot pain. The sub-theme Struggling with increased pain due to work conditions and environment highlights how factors such as certain types of floors, physical work demands, time spent on the feet, walking, heavy lifting, and inadequate footwear directly exacerbate pain. The sub-theme Feeling like just another cog in the machine due to limited control over workplace organisation reflects difficulties for employees in influencing work tasks, planning daily work tasks and responsibilities, a lack of recovery during the workday, and communication within the workplace. The sub-theme Experiencing inequality and low quality of life outside of work describes the consequences for individuals' personal lives, including restricted social participation, strained family relations, negative emotions, and sleep disturbances. Overall, the individuals expressed a sense of resignation, feeling that they had to "grit their teeth" and continue working despite the pain. CONCLUSION: The central findings of this study are negative experiences and struggles, during both work and leisure time. Understanding the experiences of individuals with work-related foot pain can help employers and healthcare providers to identify work-related risks and consider preventative measures, although further research on this topic is needed. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Dynamical systems-based metrics reveal fatigue-related biomechanical changes during running in endurance-trained male and female runners.
articles.authors: Yiyang Chen, Jill Emmerzaal, Gleydciane A Fernandes et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Linear and nonlinear metrics derived from a small number of accelerometers provide global insight into fatigue-related changes and injury risk. RESEARCH QUESTION: This study aimed to determine the effects of fatigue on movement dynamics estimated from lower-back accelerometry between endurance-trained male and female runners. METHODS: Thirty-two endurance-trained runners (16 females) performed a fatiguing running task until volitional exhaustion (20 on the Borg CR20 scale), while wearing one inertial measurement unit (IMU) placed on their pelvis/lower back. Step and stride regularity (unbiased autocorrelation), root mean square (RMS)-based measures of variability (absolute RMS and RMS ratio), complexity (Sample Entropy), jerk-based measure of smoothness (Log Dimensionless Jerk; LDLJ), and stability (short- and long-term Lyapunov Exponent) were calculated from the raw accelerations. RESULTS: Significant main effects of fatigue were observed across both sexes for gait regularity, with an 8% reduction in anteroposterior step regularity and an 11% reduction in stride regularity. Fatigue also altered variability characteristics, resulting in a 12% increase in mediolateral absolute RMS, a 13% increase in anteroposterior absolute RMS, a 2% decrease in vertical RMS ratio, a 6% increase in mediolateral RMS ratio, and an 8% increase in anteroposterior RMS ratio. Fatigue increased movement complexity, as evidenced by a 14% increase in vertical Sample Entropy and an 11% increase in anteroposterior Sample Entropy. In addition to these overall fatigue effects, RMS-based measure of variability showed sex-specific responses. Interaction effects showed that males exhibited a 4% increase in the vertical absolute RMS of lower-back acceleration with fatigue, whereas females did not. SIGNIFICANCE: Both male and female endurance-trained runners may adopt a less regular and less predictable whole-body movement pattern with fatigue, while RMS-based variability showed sex-specific responses, with increased fatigue-related changes in males. These findings highlight the importance of considering both general and sex-specific adaptations when monitoring fatigue.

articles.title: Individual Calibration of a Multiinput Wearable Device Improves Exercise Energy Expenditure Estimation During Intermittent High-Intensity but Not Resistance Exercise in an Athletic Female Population.
articles.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
articles.authors: Rebekka Frazer, Christopher D Askew, Amy-Lee Bowler et al.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to determine the accuracy of a multiinput wearable device (Actiheart 5) and commercially available accelerometer (GENEActiv) in the estimation of exercise energy expenditure (EEE) during intermittent high-intensity and resistance exercise sessions among 31 trained females. Data were collected over two testing sessions involving (a) measurement of resting metabolic rate, physique and a graded exercise test on a treadmill to enable individualized calibration of the wearables, and (b) A modified Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test followed by a resistance exercise session. GENEActiv and Actiheart EEE-derived measures, using both generic and individually calibrated algorithms, were compared against (a) indirect calorimetry for Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test and (b) indirect calorimetry plus the estimated anaerobic energy contribution based on blood lactate responses for resistance exercise. Equivalence was evaluated using predefined bounds of ±10% mean indirect calorimetry EEE. The use of individually-calibrated Actiheart algorithms improved estimation of EEE during Bath University Rugby Union Shuttle Test (mean bias 4.5 ± 60.4 kcal) compared with individually-calibrated GENEActiv algorithms (mean bias 69.5 ± 86.6 kcal), and equivalence with indirect calorimetry was achieved, although substantial individual error remained (95% limits of agreement -113.9 to 122.8 kcal and intraclass correlation coefficients, .62 [.34 to .80]). Individualized Actiheart algorithms provided equivalent group-level estimates of EEE during intermittent high-intensity exercise, whereas neither Actiheart nor GENEActiv demonstrated acceptable validity or equivalence against the reference method for resistance training, suggesting Metabolic Equivalents of Task may be a more practical method of estimating EEE.

articles.title: General Morphology and Neurite Projection Patterns of Supramedullary Neurons in the Cunner, Tautogolabrus adspersus.
articles.authors: Nick Hiza, Jun Liu, Tina Wong et al.
articles.abstract: Supramedullary neurons (SMNs) are located on the dorsal surface of the hindbrain and spinal cord in many adults of teleost fishes. Comparative morphological studies have revealed differences in SMN size, number and distribution among fishes. However, little information exists on the projection patterns of SMN neurites within the central nervous system. We focus on a single species of adult teleost fish, the cunner, Tautogolabrus adspersus, a fish that has 25-46 SMN somata aligned dorsally along the midline in the hindbrain and rostral third of the spinal cord. Light and transmission electron microscopic techniques provide new information on the general morphology of SMNs and Lucifer yellow filled SMNs reveal that these neurons are not morphologically homogeneous. Rather, four different morphotypes can be identified based on projection patterns of major neurites in the hindbrain and spinal cord wholemounts. The morphological variations suggest that some SMNs exit the brain exclusively through the first dorsal root while others exit the central nervous system through a dorsal root and the trigeminal nerve. Despite the remarkable size and accessibility of SMNs, their function(s) remains unknown. One proposed role of these cells is eliciting mucous secretion in response to skin abrasion from predation. Variation in projection patterns in the cunner provides a morphological framework from which to design electrophysiological studies to help reveal SMN function.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic Outcomes in Dahl Salt-Sensitive Rat Pregnancies: Impact of a Maternal Hypertensive High-Fat Diet.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Viviane C L Gomes, Victoria N Bailey, Lauren G Kim et al.
articles.abstract: Excessive adiposity and chronic hypertension are major risk factors of preeclampsia, a leading hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Yet, mechanisms underlying the complex interplay between adiposity, chronic hypertension, and preeclampsia remain incompletely understood, partly due to the limited availability of experimental models that capture these interactions. Herein, we explored maternal cardiometabolic adaptations in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive rats, an established model of HFD-associated chronic hypertension. We hypothesized that HFD-fed dams would display a superimposed preeclampsia-like phenotype compared to control diet (CD)-fed Dahl Salt-Sensitive females. HFD-fed dams exhibited attenuated gestational weight gain, increased ketogenesis, cardiovascular dysfunction and blunted uteroplacental vascular adaptation to pregnancy. HFD feeding was associated with high blood pressure pre-pregnancy and during most of gestation and lactation. Interestingly, however, both groups displayed a drop in blood pressure during late gestation, with lower blood pressure nadir and lower urine protein excretion in HFD-fed dams. Short-term pregnancy outcomes were largely preserved in HFD-fed dams, including litter size, pup viability, and placental efficiency. Long-term, dietary normalization failed to reverse the hypertensive phenotype of HFD-exposed dams, with blood pressure remaining 10-15 mmHg higher than controls for at least 14 weeks post-weaning. In conclusion, HFD-fed Dahl salt-sensitive females developed chronic hypertension and impaired metabolic and cardiovascular adaptations to pregnancy. Yet, neither CD- nor HFD-fed dams exhibited hallmark preeclampsia features, including late-gestation blood pressure rise, proteinuria, and fetal growth restriction. This model therefore provides a valuable platform to investigate adaptive cardiometabolic mechanisms that may attenuate preeclampsia risk in obese and chronic hypertensive patients.

articles.title: On methodological approaches for non-invasive characterization of muscle oxygen uptake recovery kinetics.
articles.authors: Alessio Marciano, Harry B Rossiter

articles.title: Increased muscle temperature: A time-dependent stimulus of group III/IV afferent-mediated exercise pressor reflex.
articles.authors: Elsa N Musselman, Ashley M Day, Jake W C Johansen et al.

articles.title: The Vertebral Nerve as a Selective Target for Upper Limb Sympathetic Blockade: Anatomy, Ultrasound-Guided Technique, and Proof of Concept.
articles.authors: Bruno Buchholz, Alejandro Ortega, Verena B Franco-Riveros et al.
articles.abstract: The vertebral nerve (VN) is a postganglionic sympathetic structure that arises from the cervicothoracic ganglion, ascends alongside the vertebral artery, and provides sympathetic innervation to the upper limb via the brachial plexus. Despite its anatomical relevance, it remains largely unknown to anesthesiologists and pain clinicians. The stellate ganglion block (SGB) is the current standard for upper-limb sympatholysis but produces nonselective effects, including Horner's syndrome and potential cardiac involvement. A more selective approach targeting the VN could achieve equivalent upper-limb sympatholysis while potentially offering a superior safety profile. We conducted a comprehensive anatomical review of the VN, covering its origin, trajectory, branching patterns, and communications with both the cervical spinal nerves and the vertebral plexus. Using this anatomical framework, we describe an ultrasound-guided technique for selective VN blockade at the C7 level, validated with fluoroscopic contrast confirmation. We objectively evaluated clinical efficacy using infrared thermography and laser Doppler flowmetry. The VN is an anatomically consistent and sonographically accessible target for selective upper-limb sympathetic blockade. At this target, effective sympatholysis can be achieved with minimal injectate volumes, thereby avoiding the nonselective effects of conventional SGB. Further studies are needed to compare efficacy, optimal technique parameters, and complication rates with existing approaches.

articles.title: Taxonomic and anatomical comments on "Traversodon(?) major" von Huene, 1936 (Cynodontia) from the Middle Triassic of Brazil.
articles.authors: Leonardo Kerber, Ingmar Werneburg
articles.abstract: Traversodontids were diverse non-mammaliaform cynodonts that occupied herbivorous and omnivorous niches during the Middle and Late Triassic. In Brazil, they are particularly well represented in the Santa Maria Supersequence, although the taxonomic status of some historically described taxa remains uncertain. Among them, "Traversodon(?) major" von Huene, 1936 was established on the basis of isolated cranial, mandibular, and postcranial remains from the Chiniquá region of southern Brazil. Here, we reassess the anatomy and taxonomic affinities of the specimens historically assigned to this species. A left maxilla (GPIT-PV-61005, here designated as lectotype) is the most informative specimen. It exhibits a combination of a broad maxillary platform, a maxillary recess, and strongly shouldered postcanine alveoli, supporting traversodontid affinities but not the original assignment to the genus Traversodon. These features are typical of deeply nested gomphodontosuchines, but do not form a unique combination of diagnostic characters that would allow a confident referral to any particular genus.
