The remaining specimens have no association or anatomical overlap with the lectotype and are here treated independently: the mandibular fragment is referred to Traversodontidae indet., the humerus to Eucynodontia indet., and the scapulocoracoid to an indeterminate non-cynodont amniote. Accordingly, "Traversodon(?) major" is retained as a nomen dubium: its lectotype lacks autapomorphies, and the remaining specimens cannot be reliably referred to the same taxon.

articles.title: Identifying 24-h Urine Osmolality Thresholds for Adequate Water Intake in U.S. Children.
articles.authors: HyunGyu Suh, Adam D Seal, Sajjad Rezaei et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Validated pediatric reference values for hydration biomarkers remain limited. This study aimed to identify 24-h urine osmolality (UOsm) thresholds corresponding to the reference water intake values for children as defined by National Academy of Medicine (NAM) guidelines. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 729 healthy children (3-13 y; 46% female) from Arkansas and Arizona completed two-day dietary records and provided 24-h urine samples. We used logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses, and relative risk (RR) analyses to identify optimal UOsm cutoffs for adequate water intake and compare them with previously used candidate thresholds (<500 and <800 mmol/kg). RESULTS: More than half of children (58%) did not meet NAM water intake reference values. Children meeting the recommendations consumed more plain water than those who did not (P<0.05). Among children aged ≥4 years, not meeting the recommendations was consistently associated with higher UOsm, darker urine, and lower urine volume (all P<0.05). ROC analysis suggested an optimal UOsm cutoff of 595 mmol/kg (AUC=61%; sensitivity=0.72; specificity=0.45; P<0.001). After adjusting for age, sex, body mass index z-score, and physical activity, children with UOsm >600 mmol/kg had a 39% higher risk of not meeting NAM recommendations. Logistic regression revealed that children with UOsm <500 mmol/kg and 500-600 mmol/kg had significantly higher odds of meeting NAM guidelines than those with UOsm >800 mmol/kg (OR: 3.02 and 1.84, respectively; P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest using approximately 600 mmol/kg as a clinically meaningful 24-h UOsm cutoff for identifying adequate water intake in children. This is slightly higher than the traditional 500 mmol/kg threshold suggested for adults.

articles.title: Neonatal stress is associated with region-specific changes in mitochondrial respiration and sex-dependent respiratory instability in adulthood.
articles.authors: Antonia Vallejo Puerta, Lida Sanchez, Fernanda Aliaga-Raduan et al.
articles.abstract: Early-life stress is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of brain development, yet its long-term impact on the neural control of breathing remains poorly defined. Here we show that neonatal maternal separation (NMS, P3-P12) induces long-term alterations in respiratory stability and mitochondrial function within respiratory circuits. In adulthood, NMS altered respiratory stability, with significant treatment × sex interactions for total and postsigh apnoeas; post hoc comparisons showed increased frequencies of these apnoeic events in males. Sigh frequency also showed a significant main effect of treatment. Region-specific high-resolution respirometry showed that NMS was associated with reduced mitochondrial respiration in the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH) and increased mitochondrial respiration in the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) and ventral respiratory column (VRC), without significant treatment × sex interactions. Normalization to cytochrome c oxidase (COX) activity largely eliminated these differences, suggesting that changes in absolute respiration are consistent with a contribution of differences in mitochondrial content rather than major alterations in respiratory capacity relative to mitochondrial abundance. In the pre-Bötzinger complex, absolute mitochondrial respiration was preserved, whereas oxygen consumption rate (OCR)/COX ratios revealed treatment-dependent alterations in mitochondrial respiratory flux relative to mitochondrial content. NMS also altered the expression of selected genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, fusion and fission in the NTS and VRC, with significant main effects of treatment and sex but no treatment × sex interactions. Oxidative and inflammatory markers were largely preserved, although selective effects of sex and treatment were detected. Together, these findings demonstrate that neonatal stress produces persistent, region-specific remodelling of mitochondrial and molecular pathways within respiratory circuits, accompanied by sex-dependent vulnerability to respiratory instability. KEY POINTS: Early-life stress induces a persistent, sex-dependent disruption of respiratory control, increasing apnoeas in adult males, whereas females remain comparatively resistant. This phenotype is associated with region-specific remodelling of mitochondrial function along the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH)-brainstem axis, characterized by reduced hypothalamic respiration and increased brainstem mitochondrial respiration after neonatal stress. Neonatal stress alters transcriptional pathways involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy and dynamics within respiratory brainstem regions, revealing persistent molecular remodelling associated with early-life adversity.

articles.title: The interaction of surface stiffness and hopping frequency on the metabolic cost and biomechanics of human hopping.
articles.authors: Luis Morata-Moreno, Alena Marie Grabowski
articles.abstract: The use of in-series passive-elastic devices, such as surfaces and shoes, can reduce the metabolic cost of bouncing gaits, such as running and hopping. These reductions in metabolic cost may arise from increased leg stiffness and ground contact time with less stiff surfaces or footwear. We examined how changes in surface stiffness influence the metabolic cost and biomechanics of hopping across a range of frequencies. As changes in hopping frequency result in changes in leg stiffness and ground contact time, we hypothesized that the metabolic cost associated with hopping on elastic surfaces would be modulated by hopping frequency. Sixteen participants hopped in place on both feet at 2.4, 2.6, and 2.8 Hz on surfaces with different linear stiffness (rigid ∼35,000 kN/m, and 0.9, 0.7, and 0.5 kN/m/kg) using a custom-built adjustable elastic springy platform while we collected metabolic, ground-reaction force, and kinematic data. Hopping on elastic surfaces reduced net metabolic power (W/kg) by 17.6-44.7% compared with a rigid surface; however, the surface stiffness that minimized net metabolic power was stiffer at faster hopping frequencies. We also found that leg stiffness and ground contact time increased as surface stiffness decreased, and this effect was amplified at faster hopping frequencies. These biomechanical changes were not consistently associated with net metabolic power changes. Our data suggest that surface energy return was most closely timed with leg extension on stiffer surfaces at faster hopping frequencies. Thus, tuning in-series passive-elastic devices to a user's movement frequency may reduce the metabolic cost of bouncing gaits.NEW & NOTEWORTHY Metabolic cost reductions for stationary hopping on elastic compared with rigid surfaces are frequency dependent. We found that the surface stiffness that minimized metabolic cost was stiffer at faster hopping frequencies. Leg stiffness and contact time increased as surface stiffness decreased, and this effect was amplified at faster hopping frequencies. These findings suggest that the stiffness of passive-elastic devices, like elastic surfaces and footwear, should be tuned to movement frequency to minimize metabolic cost.

articles.title: Skeletal muscle oxidative capacity and tissue composition in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
articles.authors: Miles F Bartlett, Jimin Ren, Satyam Sarma et al.
articles.abstract: Increasing evidence suggests that exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is related to peripheral abnormalities; however, the roles of muscle oxidative capacity and muscle steatosis remain incompletely understood. To address this knowledge gap, 38 HFpEF patients [mean age 69.8 ± 6.1 yr, body mass index (BMI) 37.6 ± 6.9 kg/m2] and 17 healthy older adults (HOAs; mean age 67.6 ± 5.4 yr, BMI 27.3 ± 4.8 kg/m2) performed a graded exercise test on a cycle ergometer to assess exercise tolerance (peak watts) and whole body aerobic capacity [peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak)]. In vivo quadriceps oxidative capacity [phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr)] and thigh tissue composition [i.e., lean thigh mass (LTM); intermuscular fat % (IMF%)] were measured separately via 31P-magnetic resonance spectroscopy (31P-MRS) and T2-weighted MRI, respectively. LTM was similar between HFpEF patients and HOAs (P = 0.854), but IMF% was significantly greater in HFpEF (P ≤ 0.001). Peak watts and V̇o2peak normalized to LTM were lower and quadriceps τPCr was slower in HFpEF patients compared to HOAs (all P < 0.03). Although IMF% was associated with peak watts normalized to LTM (R2 = 0.148) and whole body V̇o2peak normalized to body mass (R2 = 0.347), it was not associated with V̇o2peak normalized to LTM (R2 < 0.001) or τPCr (R2 = 0.020). In contrast, V̇o2peak normalized to LTM and quadriceps τPCr were both associated with peak watts (R2 = 0.509 and 0.252, respectively) and with each other (R2 = 0.298). Taken together, these data suggest that exercise intolerance in HFpEF is associated with increased muscle steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps muscle oxidative capacity. However, the lack of association between IMF% and measures of oxidative capacity suggest that they affect exercise tolerance via different physiological mechanisms.NEW & NOTEWORTHY We compared peripheral mechanisms of exercise intolerance in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) patients and healthy older adults. HFpEF patients exhibited significantly greater intermuscular steatosis and impaired whole body and quadriceps oxidative capacity [i.e., peak O2 uptake (V̇o2peak) and phosphocreatine recovery time constant (τPCr), respectively], all of which were associated with impaired exercise tolerance. However, increased intermuscular steatosis was not associated with impaired V̇o2peak and τPCr, suggesting that steatosis and impaired oxidative capacity affect exercise tolerance through different physiological mechanisms.

articles.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence or Telerehabilitation on Consumer Ratings in Physical Therapy: An Online Randomized Experiment.
articles.authors: Megan H Ross, Joshua Simmich, Daniela Berg et al.
articles.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into health care delivery, but its influence on consumer perceptions of physical therapist services remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to examine how the use of AI influences consumer perceptions of in-person and telerehabilitation physical therapist services. DESIGN: This study used a randomized 2 × 2 factorial experimental design comparing AI use and delivery mode. SETTING: The experiment was conducted online in Australia. PARTICIPANTS: The study included 710 Australian adults recruited through a paid panel. EXPOSURE: Participants were randomized to 1 of 4 hypothetical physical therapist consultation scenarios (in-person vs telerehabilitation; AI used vs not used). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Perceived warmth; competence; safety; provider trust; emotional trust; relational and functional service quality; working alliance; and intention to use were measured on 7-point Likert-scales. Composite mean scores were analyzed using ordinary least squares regression with heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. RESULTS: Mean scores in the no-AI, in-person condition ranged from 4.8 to 5.8. Among in-person scenarios, described AI use was associated with lower ratings across all outcomes, including warmth (b = -0.3, 95% CI = -0.5 to -0.1), competence (-0.4, -0.6 to -0.2) and safety (-0.8, -1.1 to -0.6), provider trust (-0.5, -0.7 to -0.3) and intention to use (-0.8, -1.0 to -0.5). Without AI, telerehabilitation also reduced ratings by 0.2 to 0.7 points across outcomes. Positive interaction effects indicated attenuation of AI-related reductions in telerehabilitation for relational (interaction b = 0.4, 95% CI = 0.1 to 0.8) and functional service quality (0.36, 0.02 to 0.70), intention to use (0.6, 0.1 to 1.0), and perceived safety (0.5, 0.1 to 0.9). CONCLUSIONS: Hypothetical in-person consultations described as involving AI were associated with poorer consumer perceptions of physical therapists and services. Telerehabilitation was also perceived less favorably than in-person care. RELEVANCE: Future studies should test whether transparency and reassurance mitigate the effects of AI-use on consumer perceptions of physical therapy.

articles.title: Layered anatomy of the greater and lesser occipital nerves with photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models: a cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Wei Zhou, Haosu Zhang, Lean Sun et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The superficial neurovascular anatomy of the posterior occipital region is important for occipital nerve block, greater occipital nerve (GON) decompression, and posterior fossa incision planning. However, the continuous layered relationship between the medial GON-occipital artery (OA) region and the lateral lesser occipital nerve (LON) channel remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: This cadaveric study examined 10 formalin-fixed specimens (20 sides). Layer-by-layer dissection documented nerve courses, emergence points, diameters, terminal branches, neurovascular relationships, GON-LON communications, and relationships with the OA and adjacent muscles. Photogrammetry-based three-dimensional models were constructed for visualization, not quantitative measurement. RESULTS: The GON and LON were identified on all 20 sides. The GON had 6.0 ± 1.4 terminal branches. Its trapezius muscle/fascial emergence point was located 25.4 ± 3.2 mm horizontally from the posterior midline and 14.0 ± 2.2 mm vertically from the external occipital protuberance (EOP) level. GON-OA relationships comprised a single crossing on 3 sides, multiple crossings on 8 sides, continuous contact on 5 sides, and coiling on 4 sides. The LON traversed a trapezius muscle-related plane on 9 sides and followed a posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border course on 11 sides. In descriptive side-level comparisons, the trapezius muscle-related emergence point was closer to the posterior midline and EOP level but farther from the mastoid reference line than the posterior sternocleidomastoid muscle-border emergence point. GON-LON communications were observed on 17 sides. CONCLUSION: These findings support a layered, pathway-based, and conceptual zone-based model of posterior occipital neurovascular anatomy, rather than localization based only on isolated surface landmarks.

articles.title: Photobiomodulation as a contemporary antioxidant intervention in myocardial infarction.
articles.authors: Gabriel Matheus Da Silva Batista, Ighor Luiz Azevedo Teixeira, Ednei Luiz Antonio et al.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers a complex cascade of structural and functional alterations that frequently culminate in adverse cardiac remodelling and heart failure. Central to this process is the excessive production of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which disrupt mitochondrial function, impair calcium handling, and activate pro-apoptotic and pro-fibrotic pathways. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has emerged as a non-invasive therapeutic approach capable of modulating several key biological processes involved in post-infarction remodelling. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate that PBM reduces infarct size, attenuates ventricular dilation, and improves both systolic and diastolic function. Through the absorption of red to near-infrared light by mitochondrial chromophores, particularly cytochrome c oxidase, PBM enhances cellular bioenergetics, modulates ROS production and activates redox-sensitive signalling pathways. These effects promote a shift from detrimental oxidative stress toward controlled ROS signalling and, in turn, facilitate cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory and pro-angiogenic responses. In addition, PBM promotes the mobilization of progenitor cells, contributing to tissue repair and microvascular restoration. Although still limited, the available clinical evidence suggests that PBM may confer modest improvements in cardiac function. However, variability in treatment protocols, delivery methods and study designs currently precludes definitive conclusions regarding its clinical efficacy. In summary, PBM represents a promising strategy for modulating oxidative stress after MI, integrating metabolic, redox and signalling pathways to attenuate cardiac remodelling. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to establish standardized protocols and to clarify its therapeutic potential in cardiovascular medicine.

articles.title: A balancing act: Passive ankle exoskeletons alter neuromuscular function and postural stability during balance.
articles.authors: Jemima C N Po, James L Williamson, Jordan Yee et al.
articles.abstract: Spring-loaded passive ankle exoskeletons have the potential to modulate neuromuscular function during standing balance by altering the mechanical demands placed on the muscle-tendon units spanning the ankle joint. This study investigated the effect of exoskeleton assistance on postural stability and neuromuscular function across balance conditions of varying difficulty. We hypothesised that assistance would improve postural stability and reduce ankle plantar flexor muscle activity during balance tasks, although these benefits may vary with balance task complexity. Participants performed standing balance tasks of varying difficulty with and without rotational stiffness provided by spring-loaded ankle exoskeletons. Balance tasks included (i) quiet standing with eyes open (EO), (ii) eyes closed (EC), and (iii) reduced base of support (RBOS). We recorded centre of pressure (COP)-based postural sway measures, lower limb joint kinematics, muscle activation data from the medial (MG) and lateral gastrocnemii (LG), soleus (SOL), and tibialis anterior (TA), and MG fascicle behaviour. Exoskeleton assistance reduced LG and SOL activation but also altered joint kinematics and coordination. Ankle-based adjustments were most evident with assistance during simpler balance tasks (EO and EC), whereas assistance during the most challenging task (RBOS) was associated with increases in COP sway velocity, COP variability and TA activation. Our results suggest that despite the potential energetic benefits from offloading the plantar flexors, passive ankle exoskeletons may induce unintended effects that hinder the control of standing balance, particularly during more challenging conditions. Further work is needed to determine the mechanisms underlying these effects.

articles.title: Persistent Skeletal Deficits Following Weight Restoration in a Rodent Model of Anorexia Nervosa.
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
articles.authors: Malihe Jafari, Daniel J Brooks, Benton Swanson et al.
articles.abstract: Purpose: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is associated with significant changes in bone density and microstructure. However, the extent and nature of skeletal recovery following weight restoration is unclear. The aim of this study was to investigate these changes in bone during simulated AN in rats across short- and long-term recovery. Methods: Female Sprague Dawley rats were exposed to 50-60% food restriction for 30 days to simulate AN, followed by recovery periods of 5, 15, and 30 days. Bone parameters were assessed longitudinally using peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT) and micro-computed tomography (µCT). Bodyweight and muscle strength were correlated with bone parameters. Results: AN resulted in significant reductions in total and trabecular bone density, as well as impairments in cortical and trabecular microarchitecture. Even with weight restoration, these deficits persisted and the compensatory responses were not sufficient for bone recovery. Bodyweight showed an association with total and trabecular bone density. Measures of muscle strength also correlated with total and trabecular density and were additive in multiple regression analysis prediction of total and trabecular bone density when combined with bodyweight. Conclusion: Recovery from AN-induced bone disorders is incomplete even after weight restoration and likely requires targeted interventions beyond nutritional rehabilitation. Furthermore, muscle function is an important predictor of bone health when combined with bodyweight.

articles.title: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy Protects Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow and Cerebrovascular Blood Oxygen Saturation with Simulated Hemorrhage in Humans.
articles.authors: Viet Q Dinh, K Austin Davis, Lindsey Peralez et al.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile Perfusion Therapy (PPT), a method we developed to induce 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations (10-second cycles), protects blood oxygen saturation during ischemia. PPT via oscillatory lower body negative pressure (LBNP) protected cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation (ScO2) during simulated hemorrhage in humans (induced via LBNP). Thigh cuff compressions are a new approach to achieve similar 0.1 Hz hemodynamic oscillations. We hypothesized that PPT via thigh cuff compressions would attenuate reductions in cerebral blood flow and cerebrovascular blood oxygen saturation during LBNP in humans. Fifteen healthy humans (6F/9M; age, 25.8 ± 4.5 y) completed two protocols of -60 mmHg LBNP. In the PPT condition, thigh cuffs intermittently inflated and deflated in 10-s cycles during the LBNP protocol. In the control condition (CON), the thigh cuffs remained deflated. Internal carotid artery (ICA) blood flow and ScO2 were measured continuously. PPT attenuated reductions in ICA blood flow (PPT: -17.6 ± 11.3% vs. CON: -31.0 ± 11.8%; P=0.02) and ScO2 (PPT: -5.2 ± 2.4% vs. CON: -7.1 ± 3.6%; P=0.07) compared to CON. These data provide evidence for PPT as a potential intervention for the treatment of cerebral hypoperfusion during hemorrhage.

articles.title: An Empirical Snapshot of Local Nutrition Governance Capacity in the Rasuwa District of Nepal Before the Flood Surge of August 2026.
articles.authors: Patrick Webb, Robin Shrestha, Shibani Ghosh
articles.abstract: On August 26, 2026, flash floods swept through the Rasuwa district of Nepal, causing mass casualties and severe destruction. Research on disasters has led to valuable recommendations on how governments can be more attentive to warning signs and react more rapidly, and how tapping into local capacity and know-how can lead to more effective responses. However, in most crises not much is known about individual or institutional capacities that predated a shock or what resources donors and governments subsequently should bolster to support emergency responses and build resilience. In this Commentary, we draw on the self-reported data of civil servants and other local professionals tasked with implementing the national multisectoral nutrition strategy in Rasuwa. Data collection in 2024 predated the flood by roughly 2 years. The survey measured routine governance capacity, not disaster-response capacity specifically, and yet such data offer some insights into local capacity before the latest disaster and help our understanding of which elements were already under strain. The aim of this Commentary is not to report full survey findings but to highlight observations most relevant to the 2026 Rasuwa flood. Broadly, we suggest that routine governance research on nutrition and other technical topics of relevance can serve as a baseline for disaster recovery and that global calls for the localization of aid require much deeper understanding and measurement of local capacity to act.

articles.title: The internal pudendal artery: a narrative review of proximal origin, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy.
articles.authors: Mugurel Constantin Rusu, Iulian Brezean
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evidence on the internal pudendal artery (IPA) is distributed across studies of internal iliac artery branching, accessory pudendal arteries, distal perineal branches, perforators, anastomoses and clinical applications. OBJECTIVE: To map human anatomical, imaging and surgical evidence on IPA origin, branching, accessory supply and clinically relevant variation. METHODS: This is a narrative review of the human anatomy of the internal pudendal artery. Relevant cadaveric, imaging, angiographic and surgical literature was identified through iterative database searching (PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science and Google Scholar), citation chasing, hand-searching of historical anatomical sources, and standard reference works on anatomical variation. Reports were organised by anatomical domain. Numerical findings were summarised as study-level results and crude aggregate counts; no meta-analysis was performed. RESULTS: The charted evidence base comprises 28 studies across 30 evidence-domain assignments, complemented by additional historical, female and clinical reports discussed narratively. Eleven proximal branching studies contributed 1,403 pelvic sides or halves. The crude distribution was 62.0% for a separate superior gluteal artery with a common inferior gluteal-IPA trunk, 20.0% for separate superior gluteal, inferior gluteal and pudendal arteries, 12.5% for a common superior-inferior gluteal trunk with a separate IPA, 3.2% for a three-artery common trunk, 1.4% for a common superior gluteal-IPA trunk and 0.8% unclassified. Five studies addressed accessory pudendal arteries, six addressed distal branches, perforators, morphometry or anastomoses, and eight provided clinical or contextual evidence. Accessory pudendal artery estimates varied substantially with the detection method. CONCLUSION: Read as a single arterial axis that continues beyond the pelvis into the ischioanal fossa and perineum, the IPA unifies several otherwise separate literatures - proximal branching, accessory supply, distal branches and clinical anatomy - that involve different units of analysis and detection methods. Future systematic reviews should examine proximal branching, accessory supply and selected distal outcomes separately.

articles.title: Bioerosion traces in bones reveal an increase in ethological diversity in the insect exploitation of carcasses in the late Triassic.
articles.authors: Lucca S Cunha, Francesco Battista, Heitor Francischini
articles.abstract: This study presents the first detailed description of bioerosion traces produced by insects in bones from the Santa Cruz Sequence (early Carnian, Santa Maria Supersequence, Brazil). An array of traces is reported, consisting of notches, a tube, trails of grooves attributed to the ichnotaxon Osteocallis mandibulus and ornamented depressions attributed to a new ichnotaxon Osteograptus thanatobios igen. nov. et isp. nov. The traces were likely produced by insects, but a less inclusive taxonomic attribution is currently not possible. The ethological interpretation for the bioerosion structures is that they represent feeding traces. This report increases the contrast between the Middle and Late Triassic bioerosion record, since the latter is significantly more diverse and abundant. Hypotheses related to the onset of the Carnian Humid Episode as well as taphonomic biases are discussed as possible explanations for this contrast.

articles.title: Age and ethnicity influence serum holotranscobalamin ('Active' B12) and methylmalonic acid concentrations, two markers of vitamin B12 status assessment.
articles.authors: Agata Sobczyńska-Malefora, Maheen Siddiqui, Dominic J Harrington
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Serum vitamin B12 and holotranscobalamin (holoTC) are biomarkers of vitamin B12 status, often used with confirmatory tests such as methylmalonic acid (MMA). Serum B12 concentrations vary by age and ethnicity, but the impact of these factors on holoTC is unclear. METHODS: HoloTC was measured in 61,193 samples from an ethnically-diverse hospital population in London (Jan 2022-Oct 2023). HoloTC <25, 25-70 and >70 pmol/L were classified as deficient, indeterminate and replete, respectively. MMA was measured in 12,233 patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L. RESULTS: HoloTC concentrations differed significantly by ethnicity. Ethnic differences were minimal in children but became apparent in adulthood, with Black patients showing the highest holoTC concentrations, Asians intermediate, and White the lowest (p < 0.001). Overall, 1.7% of patients were holoTC deficient and 25.3% indeterminate. Among patients with holoTC 25-70 pmol/L, elevated MMA occurred in 32.7% of White, 14.8% of Black and 34.1% of Asian patients (p < 0.001) using age-specific MMA cut-offs ( > 280 nmol/L for ≤65 years; >360 nmol/L for >65 years). Using a higher MMA cut-off ( > 750 nmol/L), prevalence fell to 4.0%, 1.2%, and 4.7%, respectively. The overall prevalence of vitamin B12 deficiency in the entire cohort was 7.8% or 2.4%, depending on the MMA threshold. Compared with White patients, Black patients were 34.6% less likely to have elevated MMA. CONCLUSIONS: HoloTC and MMA concentrations vary significantly by age and ethnicity. Black adults exhibited higher holoTC and lower MMA concentrations, suggesting better B12 status or differences in metabolism. Age- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges for holoTC and MMA should be considered.

articles.title: Determining the association between gender-related factors and the perception of exertional dyspnoea in healthy males and females.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Jasvir K Dhaliwal, Jack R Dunsford, Gracie O Grift et al.
articles.abstract: The perception exertional dyspnoea is greater in females than males at absolute, but not relative, levels of minute ventilation (VE). The mechanisms of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea are unclear, but since dyspnoea perception is influenced by psychological, social, and cultural factors, it is possible that gender-related characteristics confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea. We sought to determine the association between gender-related characteristics and dyspnoea during exercise in males and females. Forty-six healthy adults (n=22 males, n=24 females) completed the Stanford Gender-related Variables for Health Research questionnaire to assess their gender-related characteristics (i.e., caregiver strain, work strain, independence, risk-taking, emotional intelligence, social support, and discrimination), spirometry, and an incremental cycle exercise test. Throughout exercise, standard cardiorespiratory parameters were monitored, and dyspnoea perception was assessed using the Borg scale. Females had significantly higher scores than males for emotional intelligence (p=0.029) and social support (p=0.049); whereas other gender-related characteristics were similar between the sexes (all p>0.05). Females reported significantly higher dyspnoea intensity and unpleasantness ratings than males at a V̇E of 80 l·min-1 (both p<0.05); however, males had higher dyspnoea intensity ratings at 20 and 40 % of maximum voluntary ventilation (MVV; both p<0.05). After adjusting for sex, height, body mass, and age, emotional intelligence was significantly associated with dyspnoea intensity at a V̇E of 50 l·min-1 and 50 %MVV (R2=0.14-0.18, all p<0.05). Our findings suggest that gender-related characteristics influence the perception of exertional dyspnoea, and may confound the assessment of sex differences in exertional dyspnoea perception.

articles.title: Studying multiple health behaviours in older adults using a measurement burst design: protocol, feasibility, compliance, behavioural patterns and lessons learned.
articles.authors: Kim Cnudde, Laura Maenhout, Femke De Backere et al.
articles.abstract: Overweight and obesity are major public health challenges, requiring preventive efforts targeting diet, physical activity (PA), sedentary behaviour (SB) and sleep. Current research often treats these behaviours in isolation, ignores daily fluctuations and focuses on between-person differences. Studies examining the temporal covariance of these behaviours, assessing within-day and day-to-day variations in determinants and exploring how these time-varying determinants predict within-person variability in behaviours are needed. This paper aims to evaluate the feasibility of a measurement burst design with repeated intensive longitudinal assessments and to present patterns of behaviours and determinants. A 12-month observational study with a measurement burst design was conducted (January-December 2025). In total, 130 participants aged 55-75 years enrolled in the study, which consisted of four 7-day measurement bursts. Data collection included monitoring of diet, PA, SB, sleep and time-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Compliance rates, descriptive statistics per burst and across bursts were computed. 116 participants completed all bursts (retention rate = 89·2 %). Compliance rates ranged from 83·5 % for time-based EMA to 91·8 % for SB, supporting feasibility of the protocol. Mean values of 1692 kcal/day (sd = 565) for energy intake, 9·4 h/day (sd = 2·4) for sedentary time and 10 610 steps/day (sd = 6302) were observed. Mean daily light, moderate and vigorous PA-levels were 102·9 (sd = 37·4), 65·5 (sd = 43·4) and 11·5 (sd = 17·0) minutes, respectively. Mean sleep duration was 6·4 h/night (sd = 1·3), with a mean sleep efficiency of 79·2 % (sd = 10·2). This paper demonstrated the feasibility of integrating multiple assessment methods within a measurement burst design for studying health behaviours in adults aged 55-75 years and highlighted the value of analyses at more fine-grained temporal and individual levels.

articles.title: Intermittent Normobaric Hypoxia and Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Adults: A Systematic Review.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Pedro Navarro-Gómez, Josep Vidal-Conti
articles.abstract: Intermittent normobaric hypoxia is used as a hypoxic-conditioning strategy in sport, exercise, and health settings, but its effects on cardiac autonomic modulation remain unclear. This review synthesised passive and exercise-combined protocols in adults. We searched 4 databases through March 2026 and reported the review according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I; findings were synthesised narratively, and certainty was graded for coherent evidence. Of 4,866 records, 18 studies were included, 12 arising from controlled parent designs. Controlled resting evidence for the root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD) comprised 3 comparisons involving 47 analysed participants. Of these, 2 multiweek comparisons (n = 34) showed numerically concordant between-group differences in RMSSD change, whereas 1 single-session crossover comparison (n = 13) did not establish a clear between-condition effect; certainty was very low in both strata. Frequency-domain heart rate variability evidence was sparse and methodologically unstable, baroreflex sensitivity findings were non-convergent, and exercise-combined evidence was insufficient for directional inference. Heterogeneous dosing, limited sham control, and limited respiratory monitoring restricted interpretation. Evidence remains insufficient to establish reproducible cardiac autonomic changes after intermittent normobaric hypoxia. Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261338890.

articles.title: Perceptions and Attitudes Toward Plant-Based Meat Alternatives: A Systematic Meta-Ethnography Review.
articles.authors: Lucrezia Caselli, Clara Gómez-Donoso, Carmen Vargas et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs) can support the transition toward healthier and more sustainable dietary patterns. However, PBMA adoption remains limited despite availability and awareness of health and environmental benefits, highlighting a gap between potential and practice. OBJECTIVE: This review sought to synthesize evidence on perceptions and attitudes toward PBMAs across populations and to examine how sociodemographic factors shape consumer perspectives. DATA SOURCES: A comprehensive search was conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, Greenfile, and Cochrane from inception to August 2025. DATA EXTRACTION: This systematic review was informed by meta-ethnographic principles (4 to 6), while qualitative data were synthesized using thematic synthesis. Qualitative data from eligible studies were analyzed using a thematic synthesis assisted by ATLAS.ti software and an inductive and iterative approach for coding. Quality assessment employed the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) checklist, and confidence in findings was evaluated using the GRADE-CERQual (Confidence in Evidence from Reviews of Qualitative Research) approach. DATA ANALYSIS: This review included 31 studies with a total of 2425 participants (aged 9 to > 65 years) from the Asia-Pacific (n = 14), Europe (n = 14), the United States (n = 1), and the United Kingdom (n = 4). Analysis of 914 quotations identified 6 themes (12 subthemes): with moderate GRADE-CERQual confidence, including dietary options, food ethics, dietary perceptions, food openness, food preferences, and dietary drivers; high confidence for dietary alternatives and substitutes; and low confidence for animal ethics. Younger participants (aged <18 years) linked PBMAs with identity and experimentation, while middle-aged adults showed both critical evaluation and resistance. Women demonstrated greater awareness and culinary engagement; men expressed stronger reluctance tied to masculinity. High-income countries exhibited culinary narratives linked to sociocultural values, whereas low- and middle-income countries emphasized affordability and access barriers. CONCLUSIONS: Acceptance of PBMAs is shaped by intersecting sociodemographic factors that reflect broader social identities, moral values, and structural inequities. Future research should adopt intersectional and gender-informed approaches while prioritizing underrepresented low- and middle-income country contexts. PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251114306.

articles.title: Assessing the risk of iodine deficiency - a study to validate a digital screening tool in UK adults.
articles.authors: Katie Nicol, Anne P Nugent, Jayne Woodside et al.
articles.abstract: Iodine is essential for thyroid hormone synthesis and is needed for brain development. In the UK, milk and dairy products are the main dietary sources, but the increasing consumption of plant-based alternatives may affect iodine intake. Few iodine-specific dietary assessment tools have been validated in UK adults, and none reflects recent changes in food availability, food composition and dietary patterns. This study aimed to develop and validate the Iodine Intake Risk Score screening tool, using a rapid digital iodine-specific questionnaire. Healthy UK adults (n 108) aged ≥18 years completed the Iodine Intake Risk Score screening tool and a 6-d food diary, which served as the reference method. Iodine intake from the tool and food diaries was estimated and was classified as insufficient (<140 µg/d) or sufficient (140-600 µg/d). Agreement between methods was assessed using Cohen's kappa, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Spearman's correlation. There was substantial agreement in iodine classification (κ = 0·68, p < 0·001). The screening tool demonstrated high sensitivity (82%) and specificity (87%) for identifying individuals with insufficient iodine intake. The median iodine intake from the screening tool did not differ significantly from that of the food diaries (145 v 140 µg/d; p = 0·07), and the two methods were strongly correlated (r 0·70, p < 0·001). Median completion time was 4 min. The screening tool provides a valid and efficient method for assessing iodine intake in UK adults, incorporating conventional and plant-based sources. It offers a practical approach for identifying individuals at risk of iodine deficiency and for supporting population monitoring and dietary interventions.

articles.title: Differential Effects of Hip- and Knee-Based Stretches on Torque and Motor Unit Activity in the Hamstrings.
articles.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
articles.authors: Chrysostomos Sahinis, Ioannis G Amiridis, Roger M Enoka et al.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of the study was to compare the acute effects of hip- and knee-based static stretches on hamstrings torque and motor unit discharge characteristics. METHODS: Fourteen healthy young adults (2 females) completed three experimental sessions that comprised hip- and knee-focused stretching exercises or a control condition. Participants performed maximal voluntary contractions as well as submaximal contractions at 10% and 40% of maximal torque during a hip-extension and knee-flexion task. High-density surface electromyography recordings were obtained from proximal and distal regions of semitendinosus and biceps femoris. Motor unit discharge times were identified and a subset was tracked before and after stretching using a filter reapplication approach. Mean discharge rate (MDR), coefficient of variation for interspike interval (variability in discharge times), and standard deviation of the filtered cumulative spike train (neural-drive variability) were analyzed. RESULTS: Analysis of variance indicated hip-stretching resulted in greater reduction in maximal hip-extension torque compared with knee-stretching (~19% vs ~8%), whereas knee-stretching led to a larger reduction in maximal knee-flexion torque (~16% vs ~8%;p<0.001). Torque fluctuations increased (~28-32%) in the task most closely associated with the stretching modality. Linear mixed-effects models showed that both stretching conditions increased MDR (~5-20%), variability in discharge times (~10-25%), and neural drive variability (~20-45%), with no significant differences between muscles (p>0.05). Notably, hip-stretching induced greater increases in MDR in proximal regions (~10-18%), whereas knee-stretching produced larger increases distally (~12-25%). These regional patterns were also observed in the tracked motor-unit subset. CONCLUSIONS: The acute neuromuscular effects of prolonged static stretching depend on joint configuration and differ between muscle regions. Thus, hip- and knee-stretching exercises should not be treated as equivalent interventions.

articles.title: Eicosapentaenoic acid in adipose tissue is associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke: A Danish case-cohort study.
articles.authors: Johanne Havskov Thygesen, Villads Bové Hesislev, Phillip Czerwonka et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have been linked to a lower risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, however, their association with hemorrhagic stroke remains uncertain. We investigated associations between adipose tissue content of individual omega-3 PUFAs (α-linolenic acid (ALA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA), docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), the sum of EPA+DHA), and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke and its subtypes intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage. METHODS: This case-cohort study based on the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health Cohort included 54,546 men and women aged 50 to 65 years at baseline (1993-1997). Adipose tissue composition of omega-3 PUFAs was determined by gas chromatography for all hemorrhagic stroke cases and within a randomly drawn subcohort of 4,615 participants. Cases were identified by linkage to the Danish National Patient Register. Hazard ratios (HR) were obtained by weighted Cox regression. RESULTS: During a median of 21 years follow-up, we identified 729 hemorrhagic stroke cases. In multivariable analyses, a significant inverse association between the content of EPA in adipose tissue and the risk of total hemorrhagic stroke was found. Thus, the HR for hemorrhagic stroke was 0.64 (95% CI: 0.50-0.82) when comparing the highest quintile of EPA content in adipose tissue with the lowest. Associations were similar when stratified according to sex and when investigating subtypes of hemorrhagic stroke, although findings were not statistically significant for subarachnoid hemorrhages. No statistically significant associations were observed between adipose tissue content of DHA, DPA and EPA+DHA and hemorrhagic strokes. A high content of ALA in adipose tissue was associated with a higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke (HR for quintile 5 vs. 1: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.01-1.72). CONCLUSION: A high content of EPA in adipose tissue was associated with a lower risk of hemorrhagic stroke, while a high content of ALA was associated with a higher risk in this cohort.

articles.title: Whale swimming evolution recorded in vertebral microanatomy from the Eocene to present.
articles.authors: Lene Liebe Delsett, Justin J L Kimball, Vanja Simonsen et al.
articles.abstract: Among modern aquatic amniote clades that evolved pelagic locomotion, whales are a prime example, but timing and mode of evolutionary changes in their swimming are poorly understood. Here, we use 3D vertebral microanatomy derived from CT scanning to investigate swimming patterns in extinct whales. All vertebral centra from a single specimen of the extant common dolphin Delphinus delphis were used to provide a baseline for the correlation of microanatomical parameters and spinal movements in our dataset of fossil whales. We find that bone anisotropy, and to some extent bone compactness, mirrors the amount of compression and movement in vertebral regions. We use these parameters to infer regional movements and thus swimming mode for several lineages of stem cetaceans (Natchitochia jonesi, Pachycetus wardi, Zygorhiza kochii) and crown cetaceans (Maiabalaena nesbittae, an undescribed Oligocene odontocete and a modern minke whale). Natchitochia jonesi could walk on land, whereas Pachycetus wardi and Zygorhiza kochii were obligately aquatic, but show more spinal flexibility than modern taxa. The early Oligocene mysticete and odontocete differ in microstructural properties and might have experienced a different trajectory towards their extant bauplans. Overall, microanatomical data confirm increasing pelagic specializations in cetacean evolution that include a stiffer torso, but our data also highlight modular patterns of compactness within vertebral regions. Our approach is promising for future use of three-dimensional vertebral microanatomical data to understand locomotory patterns.

articles.title: Temporal Eating Patterns Show Inconsistent Associations With Cancer Incidence and Mortality: Systematic Review of Prospective Studies.
articles.authors: Sihan Song, Tuo Lan, Seho Park et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Temporal eating patterns, such as eating time, frequency, and regularity, may be associated with cancer outcomes through circadian and metabolic pathways, but evidence remains limited. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to systematically review prospective studies examining associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer incidence or mortality. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to September 2, 2026. Eligible studies included prospective cohorts of adults assessing eating or fasting duration, nighttime eating, breakfast frequency or timing, meal regularity, or eating frequency in relation to cancer incidence or mortality. Meta-analyses were conducted when ≥3 studies examined comparable exposure-outcome pairs, and the quality of meta-evidence was evaluated using the NutriGrade scoring system. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias for Nutrition Observational Studies tool. RESULTS: Seventeen prospective cohort studies were included. Findings for eating or fasting duration and nighttime eating varied across studies for both cancer incidence and mortality. Lower breakfast frequency was associated with higher cancer mortality and colorectal cancer incidence in some studies, but not with breast cancer incidence. Greater eating-time variability and unrestrained eating were associated with higher cancer mortality, with unrestrained eating also associated with higher colorectal cancer incidence. Associations between eating frequency and cancer outcomes varied across studies and cancer sites. A meta-analysis of three studies showed a non-significant inverse association between eating frequency and colorectal cancer incidence in both categorical (HR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.64-1.03) and dose-response analyses (HR per 1 time/day increase = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.89-1.01), with very low-quality meta-evidence. Risk of bias varied across domains, with common concerns related to confounding and exposure changes over follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Findings from cohort studies suggest potential associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer outcomes, but the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, underscoring the need for further investigation. PROSPERO REGISTRATION: CRD420251246423.

articles.title: New decompression gas CF₄/O₂: reducing DCS risk and ameliorating injuries in male rats.
articles.authors: Jiaqi Li, Hong Chen, Zhi Li et al.
articles.abstract: Decompression sickness (DCS) remains a major risk in diving. Prolonging decompression reduces inert gas load but increases operation time and underwater exposure. We tested a carbon tetrafluoride-oxygen mixture (CF₄/O₂) as a decompression gas in two rat decompression protocols: 6 ATA compressed air and 9 ATA helium-oxygen (heliox). Switching to CF₄/O₂ 10 min before decompression significantly reduced DCS incidence in both protocols: air, 68% (19/28) to 11% (3/28); heliox, 68% (15/22) to 18% (4/22). Mortality was significantly reduced in the compressed-air protocol (29% [8/28] to 0 [0/28], P = 0.004) but not in the heliox protocol (14% [3/22] to 0 [0/22], P = 0.233). Echocardiography showed fewer or no intracardiac bubbles after CF₄/O₂. In the heliox protocol, CF₄/O₂ significantly modulated some pulmonary function parameters; in the compressed-air protocol, pulmonary function changes were time-dependent and did not differ significantly between groups. CF₄/O₂ also reduced lung inflammation, endothelial injury, and histological damage in both protocols. In a 28-day repeated hyperbaric exposure protocol assessing selected serum biochemical endpoints, CF₄/O₂ did not increase serum alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, creatinine or urea; however, this protocol did not include post-exposure histopathology or haematology, so safety conclusions are limited to the measured endpoints. These findings support the tested CF₄/O₂ gas-switching strategy under the specific conditions used. Shorter decompression protocols were not tested, and shortening decompression time remains a potential application rather than a demonstrated outcome.

articles.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
articles.authors: Yue Lin, Yusi Huang, Junming Zhou et al.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

articles.title: Mechanisms of body rotation in the discus throw: contributions of ground reaction forces and the free moment to the angular momentum of the body-discus system in male throwers.
articles.authors: Keitaro Seki, Shota Kikuchi
articles.abstract: The angular momentum about the vertical axis is closely associated with release speed in the discus throw; however, kinetic studies remain almost nonexistent due to the methodological difficulties of measurement. The present study aimed to investigate the mechanisms underlying angular momentum generation about the vertical axis from the perspective of the ground reaction forces. Twelve elite or highly trained male right-handed discus throwers performed discus throw on force platforms while their motions were captured. The largest contributions to angular momentum were the moments of ground reaction forces (MGRF) of both feet during the first double support phase (DSP1). Furthermore, the MGRF of the right foot during DSP1 and the left foot during the first single support phase (SSP1) were correlated positively with the maximum angular momentum. The leftward shift of the system's center of mass during DSP1 effectively increased the moment arm, thereby enhancing the contribution of the MGRF to the angular momentum. During SSP1, although the contribution of the left foot MGRF was relatively smaller than that during DSP1, its correlation with the maximum angular momentum suggests that precise control of the right leg swing is crucial for minimizing the loss of angular momentum.

articles.title: Making sense of touch: Spatial tactile cues promote efficient visuo-somatosensory integration and restore motor accuracy under sensory conflict.
articles.authors: Maria Evangelia Vlachou, Eva Lafaverges, Laurence Mouchnino et al.
articles.abstract: Effective interaction with complex environments relies on the integration of somatosensory and visual signals into coherent spatial representations of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, as during goal-directed hand movements under mirror-reversed visual feedback, motor performance deteriorates. Despite this conflict, the visual mapping between the hand and the environment remains preserved, and visual information typically facilitates motor performance, whereas tactile feedback impairs it. Here, we tested whether providing tactile input with explicit spatial structure renders visuo-somatosensory integration functionally relevant and stabilizes motor behaviour under sensory conflict. Healthy adults performed a mirror-tracing task, tracing a shape's contour with the index finger while tactile feedback conveyed either motion-related cues alone or additional discrete spatial landmarks aligned with the outline. Spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness relative to motion-related tactile input, indicating more effective online motor control. EEG source analyses further revealed that, when spatial tactile cues were present, somatosensory activity increased and functional connectivity was largely restricted to sensorimotor areas. In contrast, when tactile cues did not convey spatial information, sensory conflict was associated with widespread reductions in cortical activity, including in somatosensory and parietal areas, and with a diffuse functional connectivity pattern consistent with elevated sensorimotor uncertainty. Together, these findings indicate that providing spatial structure to tactile input can mitigate the detrimental effects of visuo-somatosensory conflict on motor performance and support more efficient integration of visual and somatosensory information during action. KEY POINTS: Accurate movements depend on combining visual and somatosensory information to estimate the position of the body in external space. When these signals conflict, motor performance usually deteriorates and tactile feedback can become disruptive. We tested whether tactile feedback becomes useful for movement control when it provides explicit spatial landmarks, rather than only motion-related information from finger-surface contact. During a tracing task under visuo-somatosensory conflict, spatially structured tactile cues preserved movement accuracy and smoothness compared with when touch conveyed motion cues alone. Spatial tactile cues were associated with increased somatosensory cortical activity and a more spatially restricted pattern of functional coupling within sensorimotor networks, whereas their absence was associated with reduced somatosensory and parietal activity and a more distributed connectivity profile. Spatial structure in touch promotes multisensory integration, helping stabilize motor control under sensory conflict and highlighting how tactile cue design may improve sensorimotor function.

articles.title: Simultaneous acquisition of maternal and dual-fetal electrocardiography with maternal haemodynamic monitoring in anaesthetized pregnant rats.
articles.authors: Sarah Pribil Pardun, Spencer Duff, Payton Ward et al.
articles.abstract: Experimental approaches that acquire maternal haemodynamics together with direct cardiac signals from more than one fetus remain limited. We developed a standardized in vivo method for simultaneous acquisition of maternal ECG, maternal arterial blood pressure and ECGs from two fetuses in anaesthetized late-gestation Sprague-Dawley rats. The platform combines custom-fabricated needle electrodes with conventional cardiovascular instrumentation and PowerLab/LabChart acquisition. Stable, analysable maternal arterial blood pressure, maternal ECG and dual-fetal ECG were maintained for ≤5 h. The recordings supported beat-to-beat ECG interval and heart rate variability analyses. Fetuses had lower heart rates and longer R-R intervals than dams, and fetal root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), high-frequency power and standard deviation of RR intervals (SDRR) were lower than maternal values. As proof of recording responsiveness, maternal noradrenaline and verapamil administration produced readily resolved maternal haemodynamic changes together with time-aligned fetal heart rate responses. This protocol does not by itself demonstrate maternal-fetal cardiac coupling; rather, it provides synchronized high-resolution signals suitable for future analyses of dynamic maternal-fetal cardiovascular relationships and pharmacological responses.

articles.title: The Effects of Blueberry Consumption on Cerebral Blood Flow and Brain Glutathione Levels in Older Adults: A Double-Blind Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
articles.authors: In-Young Choi, Caitlin Payne, Phil Lee et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Age-related declines in brain antioxidant capacity and cerebral blood flow (CBF) contribute to cognitive decline and increase the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementias. Dietary approaches that enhance cerebral antioxidant defenses and CBF may promote brain health during aging. Blueberries are rich in polyphenols with antioxidant properties, and cardiometabolic and endothelial benefits, and may improve both brain glutathione (GSH), a major endogenous antioxidant, and CBF. However, the effects of blueberry intake on brain GSH and CBF have not been well established. OBJECTIVE: To determine the effects of blueberry consumption on brain GSH and CBF in brain regions vulnerable to aging and neurodegeneration in older adults. METHODS: In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, older adults aged 65-89 years with low berry intake (≤1 serving/week) consumed freeze-dried whole blueberry powder (hereafter "blueberry") equivalent to one cup of fresh blueberries or a matched placebo powder for three months. Brain GSH and regional CBF were measured using multiple quantum chemical shift imaging and pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling MRI, respectively. RESULTS: Sixty participants completed the intervention with adherence exceeding 92% in both groups. Blueberry powder consumption did not alter brain GSH concentrations compared with placebo but significantly increased CBF in the anterior cingulate cortex (P=0.03), a region involved in executive function and cognitive control. Within-group analyses showed increased CBF after blueberry consumption in the anterior cingulate cortex (7%, P=0.03; 95% confidence interval: 1.0%, 14.7%), caudate (7%, P=0.01; 2.9%, 15.8%), and putamen (6%, P=0.04; 0.3%, 13.9%), whereas no significant changes were observed in the placebo group. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with placebo, blueberry consumption increased CBF in the anterior cingulate cortex, a brain region relevant to age-related cognitive decline. No corresponding brain GSH changes were observed, suggesting that the effects of blueberry polyphenols are more consistent with vascular modulation than alterations in cerebral antioxidant status. articles.title: Virtual cranial endocast of Lotheridium mengi and brain evolution in early metatherians.
articles.authors: Alexander Bi, Byron D Ford, Qian Li et al.
articles.abstract: Very little is known about the early brain evolution of Metatheria, and no brain endocast of this group has been described from prior to the Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg) boundary. This has led to great uncertainty regarding the ancestral condition of the therian brain. Here, we aim to fill some of this gap by describing the first brain endocast of a Cretaceous metatherian, Lotheridium mengi from the Late Cretaceous of Henan, China. Lotheridium has an encephalization quotient comparable to the Cretaceous multituberculate Chulsanbaatar and eutherian Asioryctes and reaches the lower range of crown mammals. Together with patterns observed in other Mesozoic mammals, this suggests that increased encephalization evolved independently in several major mammalian lineages. The endocast is characterized by relatively small olfactory bulbs, well-developed petrosal lobules, and a prominent hypophyseal cast, differentiating it from earlier mammals. With the addition of a dorsally exposed midbrain, Lotheridium closely resembles the condition observed in Cretaceous eutherians. We propose that reduced olfactory bulb proportions and increased endocranial volume in Cretaceous eutherians and metatherians reflect a major shift in mammalian brain evolution, from primarily olfactory bulb expansion in the Jurassic to predominantly neocortical, brainstem, and cerebellar expansion in the Late Cretaceous. The endocranial morphology of Lotheridium further indicates that several neuroanatomical features characteristic of Paleogene and extant marsupials, including relatively enlarged olfactory bulbs and a smaller brain size compared to eutherians, are unlikely to represent the plesiomorphic condition for Metatheria. Ultimately, Lotheridium provides crucial new information regarding the ancestral condition of marsupial brains.

articles.title: A multimodal deep learning model for classifying early- versus late-stage osteonecrosis of the femoral head on biparametric MRI.
articles.authors: Siyuan Li, Huimin Huang, Yetong He et al.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Precise early- versus late-stage stratification of osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is critical for hip-preserving treatment selection, yet conventional MRI interpretation suffers from interobserver variability and limited objectivity. This study aimed to develop a multimodal deep learning model integrating biparametric MRI (STIR and T1-FSE) with clinical parameters (including age, sex, affected side (left, right, or bilateral), and etiology) to differentiate early- from late-stage ONFH and provide objective imaging evidence. METHODS: This retrospective study included 530 patients with ONFH, yielding imaging data from 851 hips. The collected data comprised STIR sequences, T1-FSE sequences, and clinical information, including age, sex, and etiology. The dataset was randomly divided at the patient level into a training set (424 patients, 675 hips) and a test set (106 patients, 176 hips) at an 8:2 ratio. Seven models were constructed: a clinical model, a STIR model, a T1-FSE model, a bpMRI model, a STIR-clinical model, a T1-FSE-clinical model, and a bpMRI-clinical model. Early- and late-fusion strategies were used for multimodal integration. The diagnostic performance of the seven models for classifying early- versus late-stage ONFH was systematically compared, with particular emphasis on their ability to identify borderline cases at the transition between clinical stages. Model interpretability was assessed using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). RESULTS: The early-fusion bpMRI-clinical model achieved the highest AUC of 0.944 (95% CI 0.905-0.973), accuracy 90.9%, sensitivity 89.0%, and specificity 92.9%, significantly outperforming single-sequence models (all P < 0.05). The confusion matrix showed that the model misclassified 10 late-stage cases as early-stage and 6 early-stage cases as late-stage. Grad-CAM visualizations indicated that the model primarily focused on clinically relevant regions, including the necrotic lesion boundary, areas of bone marrow edema, and subchondral structural abnormalities. These attention patterns were highly consistent with the core imaging features used for early- versus late-stage ONFH stratification. CONCLUSION: This study presents an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates dual-sequence MRI with clinical parameters. The framework accurately differentiates early- from late-stage ONFH according to the ARCO classification and provides objective evidence for determining the critical threshold for hip-preservation decision-making. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No: ChiCTR2300075354. Sep 1, 2023).

articles.title: Axial Complex of Deep-Sea Acorn Worm Quatuoralisia malakhovi (Hemichordata, Enteropneusta, Torquaratoridae).
articles.authors: Olga V Ezhova, Anastasiya I Lukinykh, Vladimir V Malakhov
articles.abstract: The axial complex (proboscis complex or heart-kidney) is well-studied for the shallow-living enteropneusts that burrow into the sediment and use the muscular proboscis as the primary locomotor organ. However, the deep-sea enteropneusts in the family Torquaratoridae are epibenthic surface-dwellers with a dispersed, poorly developed proboscis musculature. There is little data on the structure of their axial complex (AC). We have studied in detail the microscopic anatomy of the AC of three specimens of torquaratorid Quatuoralisia malakhovi Ezhova et Lukinykh, 2022. The proboscis of Q. malakhovi is widely fused with the collar along the entire dorsal side rather than being connected by a narrow stalk. The AC includes the buccal diverticulum (stomochord), pericardium, glomerulus (axial organ) and associated blood vessels, perihaemal coeloms, and proboscis skeletal elements. The latter are two separate symmetrical plates supporting the buccal diverticulum laterally. The buccal diverticulum is elongated in transverse direction and packed with large, vacuolated cells without a lumen. It is completely separated from the main course of the gut. The pericardium lies on the dorsal side of the buccal diverticulum. The heart is absent. The glomerulus consists of two symmetrical extensions separated by the confluence of the dorsal blood vessel. The latter is accompanied by the perihaemal coeloms and splits into several branches resembling the mouth of a river, which then flow into the glomerulus. Two buccal blood vessels with folded walls run from the sides of the glomerulus to the ventral blood vessel. A protocoelomic coelomopore is absent, however we found a pair of mesocoelomic coelomoducts and coelomopores. The torquaratorid AC demonstrates varying degrees of reduction. None of the previously studied species of Torquaratoridae possesses a complete set of AC components characteristic of shallow-living enteropneusts. Torquaratoridae are derived in terms of structure and composition of the AC compared to non-torquaratorid hemichordates.

articles.title: Biological Insights From the Osteohistology of a Nile Crocodile.
articles.authors: Ayanda Buso, Maria Eugenia Pereyra, Anusuya Chinsamy
articles.abstract: While long bones are mostly utlised for skeletochronology of extant and extinct vertebrates, among crocodilians, dermal bones have also been studied. However, there is a lack of a systematic and comprehensive study of the variation in osteohistology and skeletochronology of limb, axial, and dermal bones of extant crocodilians. Here, we undertake a comprehensive assessment of the histology of multiple postcranial elements of a single, captive adult Crocodylus niloticus (with approximately known age) to assess their utility for skeletochronology. We document the intraskeletal histological variability in the skeleton and show that despite the gastralia recording the highest number of growth rings, the radius, ulna, and fibula are more reliable for skeletochronology. We show substantial variation in the histology of the osteoderms depending on the plane of sectioning, as well as their location on the body of the crocodile. Additionally, we report that anteriorly sectioned dorsal osteoderms preserved the highest number of growth marks. Our study provides important information regarding intraskeletal variation in osteohistology and presents key information regarding the choice of skeletal elements for reliable life history reconstruction of C. niloticus.

articles.title: The Evolutionary History of Early Ray-Finned Fishes (Pan-Actinopterygii).
articles.authors: Jack Stack
articles.abstract: One out of every two vertebrate species is a ray-finned fish (Actinopterygii). The ~380-million-year fossil record of ray-finned fishes provides a window into the evolutionary history of actinopterygian diversity in deep time. The actinopterygian fossil record shows that the ray-finned fish crown group (Actinopterygii) lived alongside speciose members of now extinct lineages, collectively referred to as early actinopterygians. I review the evolutionary history of early actinopterygians through deep time, including morphology, taxonomy, phylogeny, and the fossil record itself, to form a foundation for future research. Early actinopterygians are a paraphyletic assemblage of ~600 extinct species divided between ~22 named clades and the "palaeoniscoids," a taxonomic wastebasket comprised of hundreds of species. Although nearly a decade of phylogenetic research indicates that most early actinopterygians branch off the ray-finned fish stem group, their interrelationships are largely unresolved. Notable gaps in the record of early actinopterygians, which ranges from the Early Devonian to the Early Cretaceous, include a nearly non-existent Early Devonian record, an almost complete lack of Pennsylvanian-Middle Permian marine assemblages, a gap in the Middle Triassic record obscuring the start of a decline in early actinopterygian diversity, and a sparsely documented Jurassic record. We are poised to build a reliable systematic framework for early actinopterygians via novel methods for phylogenetic analysis, fossil imaging, and the increased connectivity of paleoichthyologyists around the globe. The promise of a reliable systematic framework for early actinopterygians is to better describe the entire history of Actinopterygii and actinopterygian macroevolution in deep time.

articles.title: Development of a pro-angiogenic stem cell-derived vascular cell extracellular matrix-decorated hyaluronic acid hydrogel.
articles.authors: Louise Hosty, Yu-Yin Joanne Chang, Martina Konečná et al.
articles.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) are debilitating chronic wounds which affect up to a third of diabetic patients. Due to the underlying diabetic pathophysiology, normal wound healing is perturbed. In particular, there is insufficient re-vascularisation of the wound bed, ultimately leading to the development of chronic wounds. Current treatment protocols are insufficient to stimulate re-vascularisation and wound closure, ultimately leading to ~20% of patients with a DFU requiring lower limb amputation. Extracellular matrix (ECM)-derived biomaterials have demonstrated great promise to promote tissue vascularisation and wound repair. In the present study, the overarching goal was to develop a decellularised ECM from human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived vascular cells, and incorporate it into a hyaluronic acid-based hydrogel for wound healing. Vascular differentiation of hiPSCs yielded a heterogenous population containing both CD31 expressing endothelial cells (iEC), and CD31-negative stromal cells (iSC). ECM deposition by iSCs was stimulated by treatment with ascorbic acid and macromolecular crowder carrageenan. Post-decellularisation, the ECM composition was analysed by immunofluorescent and histological staining, indicating the presence of ECM components such as fibronectin, fibrillar collagens, perlecan and glycosaminoglycans, all having implications in angiogenic processes. Decellularised ECM accelerated the capacity of iECs to form tube-like structures when added to cell culture media in 2D. Decoration of hyaluronic acid (HyA)-based hydrogels with this decellularised ECM enhanced metabolic activity and attachment of both HUVECs and human dermal fibroblasts seeded on these hydrogels. Taken together, this ECM-decorated HyA-based hydrogel has the potential to enhance angiogenesis and revascularisation in chronic wound applications such as DFU.

articles.title: Development of a novel sigmoid notch index and its association with dental status in adult human mandibles.
articles.authors: Thayumanasamy Venkateswaran Guru, Sridharan Neelamegan
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The mandible is constantly altered based on function and age, especially in cases of tooth loss. Although the measurements of Ramus have been extensively studied, the quantitative analysis of sigmoid notch morphology and its proportional relationships has not yet been well documented. In this paper, we propose a new measurement called the Sigmoid Notch In​dex (SNI) to evaluate these relationships. METHODS: A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted on 121 adult dry human mandibles of South Indian origin, categorized based on dental status as completely dentulous (CD), partially edentulous (PE), and completely edentulous (CE). Bilateral measurements including sigmoid notch depth, condyle-coronoid interdistance, condyle height, coronoid height, gonial angle, ramus height, and ramus width were measured using digital calipers and a goniometer. Linear mixed effects models were used to assess the influence of dental status and side. RESULTS: Significant variations were noted in multiple mandibular parameters with regard to their dental status, specifically the gonial angle, ramus height, and condylar measurements. However, there was no significant variability in SNI despite variations in individual parameters. CONCLUSIONS: The SNI appears to be an innovative and reproducible morphometric index that demonstrates stability in relation to proportionality of the mandibular ramus.

articles.title: Architectural and Force-Producing Characteristics of Knee Extensor Muscles Between Alpine Skiers and Road Cyclists.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Tae-Gyu Han, Hae-Dong Lee
articles.abstract: Han, T-G and Lee, H-D. Architectural and force-producing characteristics of knee extensor muscles between alpine skiers and road cyclists. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to investigate whether muscle architecture and torque characteristics differ among athletes subjected to different sport-specific loading conditions. Alpine skiers (AS; n = 9, predominantly eccentric [ECC]-loading exposure) and road cyclists (RC; n = 9, predominantly concentric [CON]-loading exposure) were recruited. Muscle architecture (fascicle length, pennation angle, and thickness) of the vastus lateralis (VL) was measured at rest using ultrasonography at 10° and 100° of knee flexion. Maximum voluntary isometric (ISO) knee-extension torque was measured at 40°, 60°, 80°, and 100° of knee flexion, from which the optimum joint angle and peak ISO torque were estimated. Peak knee-extension torque was measured during CON and ECC contractions over a knee-flexion range of 0°-110° at 30°/s and 150°/s. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Among the architectural variables, RC exhibited greater VL thickness than AS at 10° of knee flexion, whereas fascicle length and pennation angle did not differ between groups. Compared with RC, AS showed significantly greater ISO knee-extension torque at 100° (p < 0.05). The estimated optimum joint angle was also greater in AS (p < 0.05). Absolute ECC peak torque did not differ significantly between groups; however, AS demonstrated greater ECC torque when values were normalized to the estimated peak ISO torque. These findings show that AS and RC demonstrate different knee-extensor torque-angle and torque-velocity characteristics despite similar VL fascicle length and pennation angle. They further indicate that knee-extensor force-producing characteristics may be shaped by the dominant loading and contraction-mode demands repeatedly experienced in each sport.
